author: copilot
body:
Implements a piecewise-linear approximation of quadratic line losses following the PLP/FESOP methodology (`genpdlin.f` in CEN65/src/). The flow range is divided into N equal segments with increasing loss coefficients that approximate P_loss = R·f²/V². The existing linear lossfactor model is preserved; the quadratic model activates when `resistance > 0`, `voltage > 0`, `loss_segments > 1`, and no explicit `lossfactor` is set.

### New fields

- **`Line.loss_segments`** — per-line segment count override (optional)
- **`Options.loss_segments`** — global default segment count (default: 1 = linear only)

JSON contracts, `Options::merge()`, and `OptionsLP` accessor updated accordingly.

### LP formulation (per direction, per block)

Each direction creates N segment variables `f_seg_k ∈ [0, tmax/N]` with loss coefficient `loss_k = (tmax/N) · R · (2k−1) / V²`, plus a total-flow variable and a loss-tracking variable linked by equality constraints. The sending bus balance sees `−(f_total + loss)`, the receiving bus sees `+f_total`. Units: R [Ω], f [MW], V [kV] → P_loss [MW].

### Refactored `LineLP::add_to_lp`

Broke the monolithic method into focused helpers:

- **`compute_loss_params()`** — returns a `LossParams` struct with stage-level loss model parameters
- **`add_quadratic_flow_direction()`** — handles one direction of the piecewise-linear model, parameterized by a `constexpr DirectionLabels` struct (plain string literals, consistent with codebase convention)
- **`add_kirchhoff_rows()`** — DC OPF theta constraints

`add_to_lp` is now a thin ~80-line orchestrator.

### C++26 idioms

- `std::views::iota` for segment iteration
- `constexpr` designated-initializer structs for direction labels and loss parameters

### Example usage

```json
{
  "options": { "loss_segments": 5, "use_line_losses": true },
  "line_array": [{
    "uid": 1, "bus_a": 1, "bus_b": 2,
    "tmax_ab": 200, "tmax_ba": 200,
    "resistance": 0.01, "voltage": 100.0,
    "reactance": 0.05
  }]
}
```

### Tests

3 new test cases: basic quadratic loss, quadratic + Kirchhoff, segment count override. 0 clang-tidy-21 warnings on `line_lp.cpp`. All 664 existing tests pass.

author: netlify-coding[bot]
body:
🔗 **View agent run:** https://app.netlify.com/projects/signal-net/agent-runs/69acd454d40effdde8fb41c0

🤖 **Agent:** Claude

💬 **Prompt:** why is this not working now, when it was just moments ago?

✅ **Result:** The app was not working because it was originally built as a full-stack Express server (configured for Render via `render.yaml`) but was being deployed to Netlify, which uses a serverless architecture. There were two fundamental issues:

1. **Missing `netlify.toml`** — Netlify had no configuration telling it how to build or serve the app.
2. **Missing `GEMINI_API_KEY` environment variable** — The API key required for Gemini AI calls was not set in the Netlify site's environment settings.
3. **Incompatible server architecture** — The Express server that served both the API and frontend cannot run on Netlify's serverless platform.

To fix this, the following changes were made:

- **Created `netlify.toml`** with the correct build command (`npx vite build`), publish directory (`dist/public`), SPA redirect for client-side routing, and `pdfkit` marked as an external module so its font files load correctly at runtime.

- **Created `netlify/functions/generate-content.mts`** — a Netlify Functions v2 serverless function that replicates the Express `/api/generate-content` endpoint. It uses the Web API `formData()` to parse multipart uploads (transcript + images), calls the Gemini API for vision analysis, content generation, and image generation, then builds and returns a styled PDF using PDFKit. The function is mapped to `/api/generate-content` via its config, so the frontend code requires no changes.

**Important**: The `GEMINI_API_KEY` environment variable must be set in the Netlify site's environment settings (Site settings > Environment variables) for the AI features to work. Without it, the API will return a 503 error.

author: eric-zhang-developer
body: ## Summary This PR adds a post-win recap flow to make the end of each round feel more intentional. When the player wins: - their guesses are now shown on a US recap map - the victory UI is delayed briefly instead of appearing instantly - the page auto-scrolls to the recap section once it appears It also slightly speeds up the final guess reveal so the end-of-round pacing feels tighter. ## Changes - Added react-usa-map and a local type declaration for it - Added a STATE_ABBREVIATIONS mapping so guessed states can be colored on the recap map - Added a new RecapMap component that: - colors incorrect guesses red - colors the winning state green - renders below the guess table after a win - Updated the home page win flow to: - delay the win message / CTA / recap map by 2500ms - hide the normal input once the game is won - auto-scroll the recap section into view when it appears - reset the delayed reveal state correctly when entering endless mode or starting the next round - Tightened the guess reveal pacing by: - reducing row stagger from 400ms to 300ms - shortening the uncover animation from 350ms to 250ms - Added bottom spacing beneath the guess table so the recap map has cleaner separation ## Why Previously, winning immediately showed the result map and end-state UI, which made the finish feel abrupt and anti-climactic. This change gives the last row time to resolve, then reveals the recap as a separate beat. ## Testing - npm run lint ## Notes This branch is based on main and includes three commits: - feat: add result map after win - feat: delayed victory reveal - feat: add auto scroll to bottom on victory ## Preview

`AsSplitQueryEvaluator` had the core `AsSplitQuery()` call permanently commented out with a TODO citing lack of EF Core support. The project now targets EF Core 9.x (`AsSplitQuery` available since EF Core 5.0), so this evaluator was silently a no-op despite `ISpecification<T>.AsSplitQuery` being set.

## Changes

- **`AsSplitQueryEvaluator.cs`**: Uncomment and activate `query = query.AsSplitQuery()`, add missing `using Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore` import, remove stale TODO comment

```csharp
// Before: silently ignored
if (specification.AsSplitQuery)
{
    //query = query.AsSplitQuery(); // TODO: Support for split query is not in the current EF Core version.
}

// After: consistent with AsNoTrackingEvaluator pattern
if (specification.AsSplitQuery)
{
    query = query.AsSplitQuery();
}
```

author: adlio
body:
## Summary

Comprehensive fixes for 18 issues identified during a data analyst review of the asanadw codebase (everything except manager/report hierarchy). Changes span storage, sync, metrics, query, and CLI layers.

### P0 — Data corruption
- Replace `INSERT OR REPLACE` with `ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE` in `upsert_task`, `upsert_comment`, and `upsert_status_update` to prevent CASCADE deletes of child rows (comments, custom fields, bridge tables)
- Delete and reinsert stale `bridge_task_projects` and `bridge_task_tags` on each upsert

### P1 — Metrics accuracy
- Team metrics now aggregate via team's projects (not per-member), so unassigned tasks are counted
- Exclude subtasks (`is_subtask=1`) from throughput, health, and lead time
- Collaboration counts comments **by** the user (`author_gid`), not comments **on** their tasks
- Likes query scoped to tasks active during the period
- Overdue filter computed from `due_on < date('now')` instead of stale stored column
- Team query filter uses `project.team_gid` instead of assignee-based join

### P1 — Sync correctness
- Handle deleted/removed tasks in incremental sync
- User sync now fetches comments and batches DB writes
- Record `synced_range` after successful project and user syncs
- Fetch and store task dependencies during full project sync
- Fetch and store status updates for projects and portfolios

### P2 — Period bugs
- Rolling period cache key includes anchor date to prevent stale hits
- `Week(year, 1).previous()` computes actual last ISO week of prior year (handles week 53)
- `ensure_dim_period` no longer short-circuits, so new years get period rows

### P2 — New features
- `--compare` flag on all metrics targets for period-over-period deltas
- `status-updates` CLI command
- `--tag`, `--custom-field`, `--modified-after`, `--modified-before` query filters
- Completion rate and open-task aging in metrics output
- `GROUP_CONCAT` for multi-homed task project names
- CSV formula injection prevention (`=`, `+`, `@` prefixes escaped)
- ORDER BY field whitelist to prevent SQL injection
- Migration 005: assignment history tracking via SQLite trigger

## Test plan
- [x] All 82 existing tests pass
- [x] New tests for upsert preservation (comments, bridge rows, custom fields)
- [x] New tests for task dependency CRUD
- [x] New tests for team health with unassigned tasks
- [x] New tests for subtask exclusion from metrics
- [x] New tests for completion rate
- [x] New tests for overdue filter SQL (computed, not stored)
- [x] New tests for CSV formula/dash escaping
- [x] New tests for ISO week 53 and rolling cache key
- [x] `cargo clippy` clean, `cargo fmt` clean

## Summary

Migrate all CLI command references across documentation, proto API docs, guides, examples, and seedpack definitions from the deprecated type-first format (`stigmer <type> <verb>`) to the current verb-first format (`stigmer <verb> <type>`). Also renames the seedpack MCP server from `stigmer-mcp-server` to `mcp-server-stigmer` and bumps to v0.1.0.

## Context

When running `stigmer draft mcp-server` (via the agent-fleet `01_generate-approval-policy.sh` script), the mcp-server-creator agent attempted `stigmer mcp-server get planton` — the old, deprecated command format. The agent learned this from its SKILL.md, which was generated from proto API docs that still used the old syntax. This PR fixes the root cause by updating all source-of-truth documentation so that regenerated skills will teach agents the correct commands.

## Changes

- **Proto API docs (10 files)**: Update CLI examples in mcpserver, agent, project, and organization docs
- **Product docs (5 files)**: Fix what-is-mcp-server, what-is-agent, what-is-project, what-is-organization, what-is-stigmer-server

- **Changelogs (2 files)**: Document both changes

## Implementation notes

- Seedpack skills (`seedpack/skills/`) are intentionally NOT modified — they are auto-generated and will be regenerated from the now-corrected source docs
- `client-apps/cli/COMMANDS.md` migration table is intentionally preserved (it documents old → new mapping)
- `_changelog/` and `_projects/` historical records are not modified

## Breaking changes

The Prop 123 compliance checklist had no state persistence (lost on refresh), no accessibility support, and broken auto-population for items 4–5. This adds a dedicated module with full localStorage persistence, ARIA live region announcements, DOLA deadline warnings, and cross-tab sync.

## New module: `js/compliance-checklist.js`
Pure-function manager (IIFE, CommonJS-compatible) exposing 7 public functions on `window.ComplianceChecklist`:

- `initComplianceChecklist(geoType, geoid)` — load or create state, sync DOM
- `updateChecklistItem(itemId, checked, metadata)` — persist + broadcast
- `getChecklistState(geoType, geoid)` — raw state from localStorage
- `isChecklistComplete(geoType, geoid)` — all 5 checked?
- `getNextAction([geoType, geoid])` — first unchecked item or DOLA deadline warning
- `broadcastChecklistChange(eventData)` — CustomEvent + cross-tab `storage` key
- `validateChecklistItem(itemId, value)` — validates before save

State is keyed as `hna_compliance_{geoType}_{geoid}` (e.g. `hna_compliance_county_08031`). Graceful degradation when localStorage is unavailable.

## `housing-needs-assessment.html`
- `data-storage-key` on each `<li>` maps DOM to state item IDs
- `.checklist-status-icon` spans (✓ / ⏳ / ⚠️)
- `.checklist-date-completed` `<time>` elements for completion timestamps
- `aria-checked` kept in sync on all checkboxes
- `id="checklistAnnouncer"` with `aria-live="polite" aria-atomic="true"` (WCAG 4.1.3)

## `css/pages/housing-needs-assessment.css`
New classes: `.checklist-status-icon`, `.checklist-item.warning` (orange, 30-day DOLA alert), `.checklist-item.pending`, `.checklist-date-completed`. Added `@media (max-width: 480px)` `flex-wrap: wrap` breakpoint.

## `js/housing-needs-assessment.js`
`renderChecklist()` now calls `initComplianceChecklist` and auto-checks items 1–3 only when not already persisted. `init()` wires a `change` listener on `#prop123Checklist` for manual clicks and a `beforeunload` broadcast:

```js
checklistEl.addEventListener('change', (e) => {
  const itemId = e.target.closest('[data-storage-key]')?.getAttribute('data-storage-key');
  ComplianceChecklist.updateChecklistItem(itemId, e.target.checked, { date: new Date().toISOString() });
});
```

## Tests
- `test/compliance-checklist.test.js` — 121 unit tests (persistence, validation, deadline logic, cross-tab sync, edge cases including corrupted JSON and null geography)
- `test/integration/housing-needs-assessment.test.js` — 12 new assertions covering HTML structure, CSS classes, and JS wiring

## Docs
- `HOUSING-NEEDS-ASSESSMENT-USER-GUIDE.md` §5 — added "Checking Off Items & Progress Tracking"
- `docs/COMPLIANCE-CHECKLIST-TECHNICAL-SPEC.md` — new full technical reference

author: m4ttblanke
body:
## **MERGE AFTER #151 THIS BRANCH DEPENDS ON THAT BRANCH**

## Summary

This PR adds three major improvements to class and event lifecycle management:

1. **Class end date with auto-inactive transition** — users can set an end date on any class; when that date passes, the class automatically transitions from `ACTIVE` to `INACTIVE` on next app launch.
2. **Toggleable event deletion with visual feedback** — deleting an event is now a reversible "queue for deletion" action with clear UI indicators, rather than an immediate soft-delete.
3. **Google Calendar deletion on class removal** — deleting a class in Plannr now also deletes the corresponding secondary Google Calendar via the backend.

---

## Changes

### iOS — `ClassManager.swift`

- Added `endDate: Date?` field to the `Class` model.
- Updated all three `init` overloads and `init(from decoder:)` to include `endDate` with `decodeIfPresent` (backward-compatible with existing saved data).
- Added `endDate` to `CodingKeys`.

### iOS — `ClassEditView.swift`

**End date UI:**
- New end date row in the class metadata section with a calendar icon.
- Tapping "Set" expands an inline `DatePicker` (graphical style, dark scheme).
- Once set, the date is shown with an `×` button to clear it.
- On `.onAppear`, if `endDate` is in the past and the class is `ACTIVE`, status is automatically set to `INACTIVE` and persisted.

**Toggleable event deletion:**
- Renamed `softDeleteEvent()` → `toggleDeleteEvent()`. Tapping "Delete" now toggles `isDeletedLocally`; tapping again ("Undo") reverses it.
- `hasUnsyncedChanges` is recalculated from scratch after each toggle rather than just being set to `true`.
- `visibleEvents` now shows **all** events (including queued-for-deletion), so users can undo before syncing.
- `activeEventCount` (used in the "Events (N)" header) counts only non-deleted events.
- `unsyncedCount` no longer includes never-synced events — only explicitly edited or deletion-queued events count as pending changes.

**Event row visual states (`ClassEventRow`):**
- Deleted events show: red left bar, strikethrough title, grayed-out text, red-tinted card background, `QUEUED` badge (red), and the action button changes from "Delete 🗑" to "Undo ↩".
- Edit button is disabled while an event is queued for deletion.
- Resync button label uses correct singular/plural: "Re-sync (1) Change" vs "Re-sync (N) Changes".

**Resync efficiency:**
- `eventsToSync` now only sends events that need API action:
  - **Insert**: `googleEventId == nil && !isDeletedLocally`
  - **Update**: `isEdited && googleEventId != nil`
  - **Delete**: `isDeletedLocally && googleEventId != nil`
  - Unchanged, already-synced events are skipped entirely.
- After a successful sync, a "Sync Successful" confirmation alert is shown.
- `navigateToUpload = false` is set on sync complete, popping back from `SyllabusUploadView` / `CalendarPreviewView` cleanly.

**Other:**
- Removed `Text("Color")` label from `ColorPicker`; constrained picker to 40pt width (swatch only).

### iOS — `PDFUploadView.swift`

- `ClassCard` now receives `AuthManager` as an `@EnvironmentObject`.
- Delete confirmation button replaced with `Task { await deleteClass() }`.
- New `deleteClass()` async function:
  - If the class has a `googleCalendarId` and the user is not a guest, calls `DELETE /calendar?email=...&google_calendar_id=...` on the backend (best-effort — local deletion always proceeds regardless of API outcome).
  - Then calls `classManager.removeClass(classItem)`.
- `ClassCard` instantiation in `PDFUploadView` now passes `.environmentObject(authManager)`.

### Backend — `app.py`

- New `DELETE /calendar` endpoint:
  - Query params: `email`, `google_calendar_id`.
  - Authenticates user via stored credentials, builds a Google Calendar service, and calls `service.calendars().delete(calendarId=...)`.
  - Returns `200 {"message": "Calendar deleted."}` on success, `401` if unauthenticated, `400` on any other error.

---

## Behavior Details

### End Date Auto-Transition
The transition check runs on `ClassEditView.onAppear`. If `Date() > endDate` and `status == .active`, the status is set to `.inactive` and written to UserDefaults immediately. No manual action required from the user.

### Event Deletion Flow
```
Tap "Delete" → isDeletedLocally = true → card turns red, "QUEUED" badge appears, Undo available
Tap "Undo"   → isDeletedLocally = false → card returns to normal
Tap "Re-sync" → deleted events with a googleEventId are sent to backend with is_deleted: true
              → deleted events without a googleEventId are simply dropped (never synced, no GCal action needed)
After sync   → isDeletedLocally events are removed from the local model
```

### GCal Calendar Deletion
```
User taps Delete on a class card → confirmation dialog
Confirm → deleteClass() fires async
  → if googleCalendarId exists + authenticated user:
      DELETE /calendar?email=...&google_calendar_id=... (backend deletes GCal secondary calendar)
  → classManager.removeClass() always runs after (regardless of API result)
```

---

## Test Plan

- [x] Create a class, upload a syllabus, sync → class becomes ACTIVE
- [x] Set an end date in the past → reopen ClassEditView → status auto-transitions to INACTIVE
- [ ] Set an end date in the future → no transition on open
- [x] Clear the end date via the × button → endDate is nil, persisted correctly
- [x] In ClassEditView, tap Delete on an event → card turns red with QUEUED badge and strikethrough
- [x] Tap Undo on a queued event → card returns to normal state
- [x] Queue multiple events for deletion, tap Re-sync → only those events are deleted in GCal, others untouched
- [x] Delete a class that has a synced Google Calendar → verify secondary calendar is removed from Google Calendar
- [x] Delete a class in guest mode → no backend call made, class removed locally only
- [x] Delete a class with no Google Calendar (noSyllabus status) → no backend call, class removed locally

## Summary

- Replaces flat GitHub Actions CI with **Dagger pipeline** — same code runs locally (`dagger call ci --src=.`) and in CI
- Tiered pipeline with stage gates: **Check** (vet/compile/lint) → **Test** (unit/contract/arch/PBT/TUI/cross-schema) → **Validate** (integration/mutation/snapshots) → **Build** (binary with ldflags)
- Parallel execution within each tier via `errgroup`, Dagger cache volumes for Go modules + build cache + pip
- `TuiTestMatrix` runs Python 3.11/3.12/3.13 in parallel containers (replaces manual GHA matrix)

## Local Verification

| Function | Result |
|----------|--------|
| `dagger call build --src=.` | PASS — CGO/gozstd builds in `golang:1.25-bookworm` |
| `dagger call check --src=.` | PASS — go vet + compile + ruff (advisory) |
| `dagger call test --src=.` | PASS — all tier-1 tests green |
| `dagger call validate --src=.` | 2 pre-existing integration test failures (also fail on bare metal) |
| `dagger call tui-test-matrix --src=.` | PASS — Python 3.11/3.12/3.13 |
| `make install` | PASS — no regression |

## Known Issues

- `validate` surfaces 2 pre-existing daemon integration test failures (`TestIntegration_DaemonLifecycleWithCacheBridge`, `TestIntegration_DaemonWritesCacheNotDolt`) — these also fail locally without Dagger and were never in CI before (current CI runs `go test -race ./...` without `-tags integration`)
- Ruff lint is advisory (matches existing Taskfile behavior) — 32 pre-existing warnings
- Snapshot tests use `--snapshot-update` in containers (baselines differ from local rendering)

## Test plan

- [ ] Verify `dagger call check --src=.` passes locally
- [ ] Verify `dagger call test --src=.` passes locally
- [ ] Verify `dagger call tui-test-matrix --src=.` passes locally
- [ ] Verify `make install && make dev` still works (no regression)
- [ ] GitHub Actions CI runs Dagger pipeline

## 📝 O que foi feito

* Criação da migration para a tabela **users**.
* Criação da migration para a tabela **posts**.
* Definição das colunas necessárias para armazenar informações dos posts (title, content, slug, etc.).
* Criação da relação entre **posts** e **users** através da foreign key `authorId`.

## 💼 Regra de Negócio

* Cada **post** pode estar associado a um **usuário (autor)**.
* Um usuário pode possuir múltiplos posts.
* Caso um usuário seja removido, os posts relacionados serão removidos automaticamente (`CASCADE`).

## 🗄️ Alterações no Banco de Dados

Foram adicionadas duas novas tabelas:

**users**

* id
* name
* email
* password
* createdAt
* updatedAt

**posts**

* id
* title
* content
* slug
* authorId (FK → users.id)
* createdAt
* updatedAt

## 🚀 Como testar

1. Rodar as migrations:

```bash
npm run migration:run
```

2. Verificar se as tabelas `users` e `posts` foram criadas no banco.

3. Validar se a relação entre posts e usuários está funcionando corretamente.

## ⚠️ Impacto

* [ ] Breaking Change
* [x] Mudança no Banco de Dados (necessário rodar as migrations)

author: ahzs645
body:
## Summary

This PR significantly expands the CAD editor's capabilities by introducing a comprehensive constraint solver system, pattern nesting algorithm, boolean operations via Clipper, text-to-path conversion with OpenType.js, and freehand drawing with curve fitting. It also refactors the undo/redo system to use operation-based history for better memory efficiency.

## Key Changes

### Constraint Solver System
- **constraint-solver.ts**: Expanded from 2 constraint types to 10, adding horizontal, vertical, parallel, perpendicular, equal-length, angle, symmetric, and tangent constraints
- Implemented individual solver functions for each constraint type with iterative refinement
- Added conflict detection to identify overconstrained or conflicting constraint sets
- Refactored anchor point manipulation helpers and added utility functions for shape geometry (length, direction, normalization)

### Operation-Based History System
- **operation-history.ts**: New operation-based undo/redo system replacing snapshot-based approach
- Supports 13 operation types (add/remove shapes, move, modify, fold lines, stitch holes, hardware, boolean ops, offset, and snapshots)
- Implements size-based and count-based eviction for memory management
- Provides operation compression and meaningful undo labels
- Includes comprehensive test coverage (operation-history.test.ts)

### Pattern Nesting Algorithm
- **nesting-ops.ts**: Implements NFP (No-Fit Polygon) computation using Minkowski sum approach
- Bottom-left placement heuristic with rotation support (0°, 90°, 180°, 270°)
- Waste percentage calculation and hide boundary definition
- Includes test coverage (nesting-ops.test.ts)
- **NestingModal.tsx**: UI component for configuring and running nesting operations

### Boolean Operations & Path Offsetting
- **clipper-ops.ts**: Integrates Clipper-lib for robust boolean operations (union, intersection, difference, XOR)
- Proper path offsetting with miter/round/square join types
- Handles coordinate scaling for sub-micron precision
- Replaces naive perpendicular offset with industry-standard Vatti clipping algorithm

### Text-to-Path Conversion
- **opentype-ops.ts**: OpenType.js integration for font loading and glyph conversion
- Actual font metrics (kerning, advance width) instead of estimation
- Converts text shapes to vector path outlines (LineShape/BezierShape)
- Font caching for performance

### Freehand Drawing
- **freehand-ops.ts**: Ramer-Douglas-Peucker polyline simplification
- Quadratic bezier fitting via least-squares optimization
- Converts raw mouse/touch points into smooth bezier curves
- Includes test coverage (freehand-ops.test.ts)
- **canvas-tool-manager.ts**: New freehand tool handler integrated into canvas tools

### Auto-Constraint Detection
- **auto-constraint-ops.ts**: Analyzes drawn shapes and suggests geometric constraints
- Detects horizontal, vertical, parallel, perpendicular, equal-length, and tangent relationships
- Configurable tolerance and confidence scoring
- Includes test coverage (auto-constraint-ops.test.ts)

### Polygon Utilities
- **polygon-ops.ts**: Shared polygon conversion utilities for Clipper and nesting operations
- Shape-to-polygon conversion with endpoint chaining
- Polygon area, bounds, centroid, translation, and rotation calculations
- Includes test coverage (polygon-ops.test.ts)

### 3D Material Presets
- **material-presets.ts**: PBR material presets for different leather types
- Defines roughness, metalness, normal scale, and bump scale for realistic rendering
- **three-bridge.ts**: Integration for applying presets to 3D preview
- **ThreePreviewPanel.tsx**: UI for selecting leather material presets

### UI & Integration
- **PatternToolsModal.tsx**: Added boolean operation, offset, text-to-path, and nesting buttons
- **EditorApp.tsx**: Integrated nesting modal and auto-constraint settings
- **editor-constants.ts**: Added 'freehand' tool to available tools

## Summary
- Implemented `CRedEntry::ClearWaveData(int)` in `src/RedSound/RedEntry.cpp` (previously TODO).
- Added the PAL metadata block for the function (`0x801c1190`, `316b`) to match project documentation format.
- Used existing `RedEntry` data layout conventions (`int*` bank tables and `0x10` bank stride) and existing member calls (`SearchWaveSequence`, `WaveDelete`) for a source-plausible first pass.

## Units/functions improved
- Unit: `main/RedSound/RedEntry`
- Function: `ClearWaveData__9CRedEntryFi`

- `ClearWaveData__9CRedEntryFi` match: **1.2658228% -> 13.974684%**
- Unit `.text` match (`main/RedSound/RedEntry`): **31.128971% -> 31.5043%**
- Function size remains `316` bytes; no regressions introduced in this unit from this change.

## Plausibility rationale
- The implementation follows expected game-source behavior for wave-bank clearing modes:
  - `-1`: clear all valid banks
  - `-2`: clear banks in history-managed range
  - `-3`: clear banks in history range with non-zero history count
  - `>=0`: clear by wave number via `SearchWaveSequence`
- Logic uses established object-local bank table layout already used across this file, instead of hardcoded external hacks.

## Technical details
- Control flow and loop boundaries are aligned to the recovered RedEntry bank table representation:
  - bank array base: `entry[0]`
  - full table span: `+0x400`
  - history range start: `+0x100`
  - bank step: `0x10` bytes (`int[4]`)
- This is an incremental decomp pass focused on real assembly improvement while preserving readable, maintainable C++.

author: odabir33
body:
I went through the code for the artefacts agent and found that we have actually hard-coded the logic for the mermaid code and user stories, and there is a lot of manual parsing and data manipulation.

This is not what we want. Because the output has to be dynamic depending upon each use case or idea given by the user. Let the LLM generate content dynamically! The JSON output of the requirements agent is not the final artefact! It is just a summary of the info gathered from the user.

We should pass the JSON response received from the requirements agent to the LLM and define clear instructions on what we want it to generate. We can ask for the clear, structured output in the instruction itself, so we don't need to parse the output on our own.
We should focus more on what artefacts or spec docs we need instead of manually writing the entire logic.

The more detailed the output is, the better it is for our next stages.
Today, they mentioned that we can divide the specs into technical and non-technical ones. We need not show the technical stuff to the user right now. Those will be for the engineering teams to pick up and start working on later.

We have to show non-tech specs to the user (PMs) and ask for approval/changes now.

What I think we should generate:

Non-tech
PRD with Problem statement, target users, Detailed Functional + Non-functional requirements + Scope (pdf)
User stories with tasks + Acceptance Criteria for each (pdf)
Interfaces + User Flow descriptions (pdf/images)

Tech (Once non-tech requirements are approved)
Low-level system design with details for each module/service (mmd)
Class / ER diagram (Class interfaces and their relationships) (mmd)
API docs (with URLs, methods, params, expected outputs)  (pdf)
Project structure (frontend components, services, pages + backend services, apis, auth handlers, etc.
Most of this will be handled via the instruction prompt (ask ChatGPT to generate a detailed prompt based on above data).

We can write simple Python functions to convert mmd code to image or text to pdf and pass these functions as tools to the LLM agent.

body:
### Motivation
- Replace the portal-heavy two-attempt baseline (modern -> legacy(off)) with a structural-first sequence to prioritize topology-aware search before any legacy rescue.
- Make attempt-level budgets sensitive to the level solver profile instead of only splitting at the stage level.
- Add exit conditions driven by solver search-quality indicators (branching collapse, phase/target progress) so wasted attempts can be abandoned earlier.
- Ensure Stage 2 uses a deterministic structural policy by default and prevent randomized exploration in expensive tiers unless explicitly enabled.

### Description
- Reworked `Referee.runBaselineStage` to build an attempt plan from `level.solverProfile` with profile-aware per-attempt budgets and a structural-first ordering: `structural-modern`, `structural-conservative`, then optional `legacy-rescue` when policy allows.
- Added `getSearchQuality` to extract per-attempt metrics (`branchFactor`, `branchingCollapse`, `maxProgress`, `targetProgressGood`, `finalObjectives`) from solver debug (`phaseTimeline`, `nodesExpanded`, `branchesTried`) and attach them to attempt telemetry.
- Implemented early-exit logic (`shouldStopAfterAttempt`) to stop further attempts when indicators show poor branching/low progress or on terminal statuses (`timeout`, `no-solution-proven`) while preserving last-attempt reporting.
- Updated `runAttempt` to accept attempt labels and respect a new `allowRandomizedExploration` flag so randomized `dirOrderVariant === 'random'` is only used when explicitly permitted; updated `Referee.solve` to pass `profile` and to disable randomized exploration and legacy rescue for Stage 2 by default while allowing opt-in for expensive tiers via `allowRandomizedExplorationOnExpensiveTiers`.
- Attempt telemetry now includes `label` and `quality` to aid diagnosis and analytics.

### Testing
- Ran an automated patch/format diff check (patch/diff-check) on the modified file and it reported no formatting/patch conflicts.
- Performed static inspection of the changed call sites in `Referee.solve` to ensure Stage 2 receives deterministic structural options and that baseline attempts receive the new profile and flags.
- No unit/integration test suite was executed as part of this change; changes are confined to solver orchestration and include defensive fallbacks (optional legacy-rescue and final fallback stage) to preserve existing behavior under default settings.

author: asazhou923
body:
### Motivation
- Prevent accidental token leakage and ensure correct cookie behavior across environments by adjusting guest cookie attributes and redirect behavior.
- Avoid persisting sensitive secrets in audit logs by masking common secret fields before storing request bodies.
- Make client-side auth more robust by adding storage fallbacks and preventing duplicate guest user creation during concurrent requests.

### Description
- Update `bind_guest_token` to set the cookie `secure` flag based on `settings.app_env` and use `SameSite=None` in non-dev environments so cross-site requests (and iOS WebKit) preserve guest identity.  
- Change Google OAuth callback flow to return tokens in the URL fragment instead of the query string and simplify a Google verification error message in `auth_google_login`.  
- Add a lightweight JSON-field masker in `services/audit.py` (`SENSITIVE_JSON_FIELDS` and `_mask_sensitive_text`) and apply it in `_safe_text_from_body` to redact secrets before persisting audit `request_body`.  
- Frontend `GoogleCallbackPage` now reads OAuth parameters from both query and URL fragment via a `readParam` helper so it can handle the new fragment-based redirect.  
- Revamp client auth persistence in `auth-context.tsx` to: add cookie fallback (`TOKEN_KEY` cookie), use both `localStorage` and `sessionStorage` fallbacks, add `persistAuthToken`/`readStoredAuthToken`/`clearStoredAuthToken` helpers, and persist tokens to cookie with a `Max-Age`.  
- Add deduplication for concurrent guest-session creation in the client using `pendingGuestTokenRef` so multiple simultaneous `ensureToken` calls share the same `authGuest()` promise.

### Testing
- Ran backend unit tests with `pytest`; test suite passed.  
- Ran frontend unit tests with the project test runner (`pnpm test`); test suite passed.  
- Verified the Google callback flow and guest-token persistence locally in development by simulating query and fragment responses and by exercising concurrent `ensureToken` calls (manual integration checks).

body:
## Summary
- Add `freshLogin` flag to skip redundant `authRefresh()` call immediately after `authWithPassword`/`authWithOAuth2` succeeds — the token is already valid and re-validating it causes a 401 race condition in some browsers
- Discriminate 401 vs 500 errors in the layout auth catch block — server errors no longer incorrectly log users out
- Applied to all auth methods: password, Google OAuth, and GitHub OAuth

## Root Cause
After `authWithPassword` succeeds, the layout's `onMount` calls `authRefresh()` to validate the token. Due to timing in how Svelte 5's effect batching interacts with the PB SDK's fetch pipeline, `authRefresh` returns 401 despite the token being valid — causing an infinite login loop.

## Test plan
- [ ] Login with email/password — should redirect to admin dashboard without looping
- [ ] Login with Google OAuth (if configured) — should redirect without looping
- [ ] Login with GitHub OAuth (if configured) — should redirect without looping
- [ ] Stale token (manually corrupt `pb_auth` cookie) — should redirect to login page
- [ ] Server temporarily down during auth check — should not log out the user

author: rossku
body:
## Summary

Closes #701

When `calculate_mass()` returns `StorageMassExceedsMaximumTransactionMass`, the Generator now returns `Ok(None)` to continue the accumulation loop instead of propagating the error via `?`. Adding more inputs strictly reduces storage mass per KIP-9, so the loop converges.

Previously, a user with a small UTXO (e.g. 0.296 KAS) and a larger one (e.g. 4.0 KAS) would get a hard failure when sending 0.2 KAS — the first UTXO alone exceeded the storage mass limit, and the Generator never tried accumulating the second.

## Changes (2 files)

- `wallet/core/src/tx/generator/generator.rs` — catch `StorageMassExceedsMaximumTransactionMass` in `try_finish_standard_stage_processing`, return `Ok(None)` to continue accumulation
- `wallet/core/src/tx/generator/test.rs` — add `test_generator_storage_mass_exceed_accumulates`

author: seatsfordeparture
body:
### Motivation
- Observed race/double-join between join paths produced spurious disconnects and `CryptoError decoding packet data` followed by `OpusError('corrupted stream')`, indicating a primary crypto/session desync. 
- The goal is to serialize connection flows per guild and ensure a single attach/listen lifecycle to avoid crypto state corruption and spurious reconnects.

### Description
- Added a per-guild state machine (`_VoiceConnectionState`) with explicit states `idle`, `connecting`, `connected`, `disconnecting`, `reconnecting`, `failed` and structured logging via `_set_voice_state(...)` to record `reason` and `listener_attached`.
- Centralized join logic into `ensure_voice_connected(guild, channel, reason=...)` and updated callers (privacy enforcer, voice-state auto-join, join command, legacy join) to use it; this serializes joins under a per-guild `join_locks` and emits `join skipped: already connecting` / `join skipped: already connected same channel` / `listen skipped: already attached` where appropriate.
- Extended `VoiceReceiveAdapter` to track listener attachment identity and expose an idempotent `attach_listener(...)`, plus added `AdapterDecodeCounters.crypto_decode_errors` to separate crypto decode counts from opus decode counters and added distinct logging paths for crypto vs opus decode failures.
- Made disconnect flow explicit and stateful (mark `disconnecting`, cleanup adapter/session, set `idle`) and added reasoned logs for connect/disconnect transitions to help triage.
- Added/updated tests to assert idempotent joins, single connect behavior across concurrent callers, idempotent listener attach, and separate tracking of crypto vs opus decode errors.

### Testing
- Ran the focused test suite: `PYTHONPATH=. pytest -q tests/test_voice_receive_adapter.py tests/test_voice_ingest_join_robustness.py` and all tests passed (11 passed) with warnings from test monkeypatches but no failures.
- New/updated automated tests include `test_double_join_is_idempotent_single_connect`, `test_join_skips_reconnect_when_already_connected_same_channel`, `test_privacy_enforcer_and_voice_state_autojoin_single_connect`, `test_listener_attach_is_idempotent`, and `test_crypto_and_opus_errors_are_tracked_separately`, and they succeeded in CI-local runs.
- Tests exercise both the adapter changes and the new `ensure_voice_connected` orchestration to validate single connect, idempotent attach, and separate crypto/opus counters.

author: vansyson1308
body:
### Motivation
- E2E compose runs were using `NODE_ENV=test`, which disabled BullMQ queue init and caused webhook ACKs without enqueued work, leading to end-to-end timeouts.
- Worker job persistence was failing under RLS and ambiguous parameter typing during `PROCESS_INBOUND_EVENT` handling and needed tenant-scoped execution and explicit typing.
- Tests lacked actionable timeout diagnostics, making CI triage slow and brittle.

### Description
- Add an explicit test-mode override `ENABLE_QUEUE_IN_TEST` and wire it into gateway and worker startup so queues can be initialized under `NODE_ENV=test` when explicitly enabled, and expose `queue_enabled_in_test` and `queue_transport` in startup logs for visibility. 
- Make `enqueue()` fail loud with `queue_not_configured` when tests expect a queue but none is configured, while preserving the existing `queueCmd` fallback for test runners. 
- Fix `markJob(...)` in `apps/worker/src/process-inbound.ts` by casting the correlation parameter to text (`$3::text`) and executing the jobs insert inside `deps.runInTenantTransaction(...)` when available to satisfy RLS tenant session requirements, with a direct fallback when the helper is absent. 
- Propagate `ENABLE_QUEUE_IN_TEST` into compose env for gateway and worker, and update `scripts/v2/run_e2e_compose.mjs` to write `ENABLE_QUEUE_IN_TEST=true`, add stage-specific diagnostics (inbound rows, canonical counts, Redis queue depth, filtered gateway/worker logs), and invoke those diagnostics on timeout to aid triage. 
- Add a set of triage documentation artifacts under `docs/triage/` capturing the investigative passes and the chosen fixes.

### Testing
- Ran static type checks via `npm run typecheck`, which completed successfully. 
- Attempted local E2E via `npm run e2e`, but the run was blocked in this environment due to missing Docker CLI (`spawnSync docker ENOENT`), so runtime verification must be performed in CI or a docker-capable host.

author: officialinspire
body:
### Motivation
- Improve data hygiene, validation, and reliability for local/production-like usage without changing the existing runtime model or CLI.
- Prevent bad/ambiguous input (missing required fields, malformed invoice numbers, negative totals, invalid numeric/item values) from being persisted.
- Make upload and OCR flows safer with size/type checks and clearer failure semantics.
- Provide a lightweight, idempotent migration mechanism to evolve on-disk schema safely.

### Description
- Added canonicalization helpers and validations: `normalizePhoneNumber`, `normalizeDate`, `normalizeSourcePath`, `isValidInvoiceNumber`, `validateInvoicePayload`, and `makeValidationError` to normalize inputs and produce structured validation errors (`VALIDATION_ERROR`).
- Enforced required fields (`sold_to`, `directions`), numeric checks for item and money fields, payment flag validation, and prevented negative totals/deposits unless `allow_negative_totals=true` is explicitly provided.
- Hardened invoice persistence by validating payloads before DB writes, checking for duplicate invoice numbers with explicit `409 DUPLICATE_INVOICE_NUMBER` responses, and keeping the invoice + items upsert/delete flows inside transactions.
- Improved upload handling with an allowlist of MIME types, a 15MB size limit, multer error handling, safer renaming to `uploads/`, improved OCR error logging and structured responses (`UPLOAD_TOO_LARGE`, `INVALID_UPLOAD_TYPE`, `OCR_FAILED`), and confined source_path resolution to uploads via `resolveUploadPath`.
- Extended search query coverage to include more invoice fields and invoice_items text fields and added digit-based phone matching for better search hits.
- Introduced a minimal migrations subsystem (`schema_migrations` table and `runMigrations`) and bumped the schema version to 4 with one migration that normalizes legacy `source_path` values and trims date-like strings to `YYYY-MM-DD` when possible.

### Testing
- Static syntax checks: `node --check cr-customer-manager/server.js && node --check cr-customer-manager/db.js` (succeeded).
- Local run smoke: `cd cr-customer-manager && npm start` and validated server logs/health endpoint (server started and `/api/health` returned OK).

author: damacus
body:
💡 **What**: Replaced the database-bound `schedules.active.sum` call with the in-memory `schedules.select(&:active?).sum` inside `Medication#estimated_daily_consumption`. Added a comment explaining the optimization.

🎯 **Why**: When `estimated_daily_consumption` is calculated in a loop on eager-loaded medication records (e.g., when determining if forecasting is available for many medications), calling the `.active` scope triggered an N+1 database query. Filtering the already-loaded collection in-memory eliminates these redundant queries.

📊 **Impact**: Prevents one database query per medication when calculating daily consumption, substantially reducing database load and response times for views presenting medication inventories or forecasts.

🔬 **Measurement**: Verify that accessing medication dashboards or running scripts that batch process `forecast_available?` for `PersonMedication` records do not exhibit `SELECT "schedules".* FROM "schedules" WHERE "schedules"."medication_id" = ?` queries in the server logs.

## Summary

body:
Builds a complete drug interaction checker from an empty repo: given two drug names, returns interaction description, pharmacological mechanism, severity, and clinical recommendation.

## Package: `drug_interaction_checker/`

- **`models.py`** — `Severity` enum (Minor/Moderate/Major/Contraindicated), `Drug`, `Interaction`, `InteractionResult` dataclasses
- **`database.py`** — 55+ curated interactions across anticoagulants, NSAIDs, antibiotics, SSRIs/MAOIs, statins, opioids, antihypertensives, immunosuppressants, and more; 80+ brand→generic aliases (e.g. Coumadin→Warfarin, Advil→Ibuprofen)
- **`utils.py`** — `resolve_drug_name()` with exact + `difflib` fuzzy matching; confidence scoring
- **`checker.py`** — `DrugInteractionChecker.check(drug1, drug2) → InteractionResult`; handles aliases, misspellings, same-drug detection, and unknown names with suggestions

## Interfaces

- **`main.py`** — Rich CLI; single-lookup (`python main.py Warfarin Aspirin`) and interactive mode; colour-coded severity badges
- **`app.py`** — Flask web app with dark-themed UI and a JSON API endpoint:

```bash
POST /api/check
{"drug1": "Coumadin", "drug2": "Flagyl"}
# → {"found": true, "drug1_matched": "Warfarin", "drug2_matched": "Metronidazole",
#    "interaction": {"severity": "Major", "mechanism": "...", ...}, "confidence": 1.0}
```

## Tests

59 tests covering known interactions, brand name resolution, fuzzy matching, no-interaction paths, and error handling.

## Summary
This PR introduces a comprehensive error classification system for analyzing Black Box LLM reasoning experiments. It adds deterministic classification of ray physics rule failures based on outcome mismatches, along with LLM-as-judge capabilities for deeper error analysis.

## Key Changes
- **New `classify_errors.py` module**: Implements dual-mode error classification
  - Predict mode: Deterministic classification comparing predicted vs actual outcomes to identify specific ray physics rule failures (no LLM required)
  - Play mode: LLM-as-judge classification for more nuanced error analysis
  - Supports batch processing of experimental results with configurable output formats

- **New `error_classifications.json` dataset**: Comprehensive error classification data (~102KB) containing labeled examples and classification patterns for training and validation

- **Enhanced `blackbox_llm_study.qmd`**: Expanded error analysis section with detailed classification methodology and visualizations of ray physics rule breakdowns

## Implementation Details
The error classification system provides deterministic rule-based classification by analyzing mismatches between predicted and actual ray physics outcomes. This enables systematic identification of which specific physics rules (e.g., reflection, refraction, absorption) failed in each incorrect prediction, moving beyond simple outcome-level confusion matrices to provide actionable insights into model failure modes.

author: giulio-leone
body:
## Summary

Fixes #6852 — `AnthropicBedrock.__init__() got an unexpected keyword argument 'api_key'` when using `AWS_BEDROCK_API_KEY`.

## Root Cause

`_get_client_params()` in `agno/models/aws/claude.py` constructs `{"api_key": self.api_key}` and passes it to `AnthropicBedrock(**client_params)`. However, the `anthropic` library's `AnthropicBedrock` class **does not accept** an `api_key` parameter — it only accepts `aws_access_key`, `aws_secret_key`, `aws_session_token`, `aws_region`, `default_headers`, etc.

## Fix

Bedrock API keys are bearer tokens. Pass them via the `default_headers` parameter:

```python
# Before (broken):
client_params = {"api_key": self.api_key}

# After (fixed):
client_params = {"default_headers": {"Authorization": f"Bearer {self.api_key}"}}
```

This uses `AnthropicBedrock`'s `default_headers` parameter, which attaches the `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header to every request.

## Tests

- Updated `TestApiKeyPath::test_api_key_params` to verify:
  - `default_headers["Authorization"]` contains the bearer token
  - No `api_key` key exists in the params
- All 14 existing AWS Claude client tests pass (zero regression)

## Reproducer

```python
from agno.agent import Agent
from agno.models.aws import Claude
import os

os.environ["AWS_BEDROCK_API_KEY"] = "your-key"
os.environ["AWS_REGION"] = "us-east-2"

agent = Agent(model=Claude(id="anthropic.claude-opus-4-6-v1"))
# Before fix: crashes with TypeError
# After fix: initializes correctly with bearer token auth
```

author: pimlock
body:
## Summary
- classify IPv6 ULA addresses in `fc00::/7` as internal in the sandbox proxy SSRF check
- add regression coverage for the host-side ULA address seen from `host.docker.internal`
- document `fc00::/7` in the security policy reference so the allowlist behavior matches the implementation

## Context
- this fixes a sandbox networking issue where `host.docker.internal` resolved to both IPv4 and IPv6, but the IPv6 ULA address was not treated as internal
- on the plain HTTP forward-proxy path, that caused requests to be denied before reaching the host MCP server even when policy and `allowed_ips` were configured correctly
- the concrete regression case here is `fdc4:f303:9324::254`, which should be treated as private/internal like RFC1918 IPv4 addresses

Policy I was using:

```
network_policies:
  host_mcp:
    name: host-mcp
    endpoints:
      - host: host.docker.internal
        port: 8001
        allowed_ips:
          - "172.29.0.254"
          - "fdc4:f303:9324::254"
    binaries:
      - { path: /usr/bin/node }
```

## Test Plan
- `cargo test -p navigator-sandbox proxy::tests`
- `mise run pre-commit`

<!-- START COPILOT ORIGINAL PROMPT -->



<details>

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

> 
> ## 背景
> 
> 当前 `src/include/handlers/search.py` 中的搜索处理逻辑存在多个显著的性能瓶颈，导致匹配结果越多、响应越慢。
> 
> ---
> 
> ## 需要修复的问题
> 
> ### 1. `.all()` 全量拉取 + Python 层 LIMIT（应下推至数据库）
> 
> ```python
> # 现状（search.py 第 85 行 / 第 122 行）
> documents = documents_query.all()   # 不管多少条，全部拉进内存
> ...
> all_results = all_results[:limit]   # limit 在 Python 里截断
> ```
> 
> 应在 SQL 层加上足够大的 `LIMIT`（例如 `limit * 10`，为权限过滤留余量），避免无效数据进入内存。
> 
> ### 2. N+1 懒加载问题（权限规则 + 文件信息）
> 
> `check_access_requirements` 内部访问 `self.access_rules`，在没有预加载的情况下每个对象产生一次额外 `SELECT`。对文档还额外访问 `document.revisions`（含 `DocumentRevision.file`），产生更多懒加载。
> 
> N 条匹配 = 至少 1 + N（权限）+ 2N（revision + file）次查询。
> 
> 应使用 `selectinload` / `joinedload` 进行预加载，将总查询数压缩到固定的 3~4 次。
> 
> ### 3. `name`/`title` 字段缺少数据库索引
> 
> `Document.title` 和 `Folder.name` 目前没有索引，`ILIKE '%xxx%'` 必须全表扫描。应在模型定义中为这两个字段加上 `index=True`，并通过 Alembic 迁移落实到数据库。
> 
> ### 4. Python 层排序（应下推至数据库）
> 
> 排序目前在 Python 里完成。对于 `name` 和 `created_time` 字段，应将 `ORDER BY` 下推到 SQL，减少内存排序开销（注意：`size` 和 `last_modified` 需要关联文件信息，可保留在 Python 层处理）。
> 
> ---
> 
> ## 需要修改的文件
> 
> ### `src/include/handlers/search.py`
> 
> 对 `RequestSearchHandler.handle` 方法做如下改造：
> 
> 1. 在文档查询中加入 `selectinload`，预加载 `access_rules`、`current_revision`（含其 `file`）、`revisions`（含其 `file`）。
> 2. 在目录查询中加入 `selectinload`，预加载 `access_rules`。
> 3. 文档/目录查询均加上 `.limit(limit * 10)`（SQL 层预截断）。
> 4. 对 `name`/`created_time` 排序，在 SQL 层加上对应 `ORDER BY`（`sort_by` 为 `name` 时按 `title`/`name`，为 `created_time` 时按 `created_time`）。
> 
> 示例伪代码（供参考，实际实现需与现有逻辑保持一致）：
> 
> ```python
> from sqlalchemy.orm import selectinload, joinedload
> 
> # 文档查询
> documents_query = (
>     session.query(Document)
>     .options(
>         selectinload(Document.access_rules),
>         selectinload(Document.revisions).joinedload(DocumentRevision.file),
>         joinedload(Document.current_revision).joinedload(DocumentRevision.file),
>     )
>     .filter(Document.title.ilike(f"%{query}%"))
>     .limit(limit * 10)
> )
> 
> # 目录查询
> directories_query = (
>     session.query(Folder)
>     .options(selectinload(Folder.access_rules))
>     .filter(Folder.name.ilike(f"%{query}%"))
>     .limit(limit * 10)
> )
> ```
> 
> 注意：需同时在 import 中引入 `DocumentRevision`（来自 `include.database.models.entity`）。
> 
> ### `src/include/database/models/entity.py`
> 
> 为 `Document.title` 和 `Folder.name` 字段添加 `index=True`：
> 
> ```python
> # Folder（第 278 行）
> name: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(VARCHAR(255), nullable=False, index=True)
> 
> # Document（第 351 行）
> title: Mapped[Optional[str]] = mapped_column(
>     VARCHAR(255), nullable=False, default="Untitled Document", index=True
> )
> ```
> 
> ### `src/alembic/versions/<new_revision>_add_search_indexes.py`（新建）
> 
> 创建新的 Alembic 迁移文件，为 `documents.title` 和 `folders.name` 添加索引。
> 
> - `down_revision` 应设为当前最新迁移版本（即 `ccd985e08120`）。
> - 新的 `revision` ID 可自行生成（任意 12 位十六进制字符串）。
> 
> ```python
> """add search indexes on documents.title and folders.name
> 
> Revision ID: <new_id>
> Revises: ccd985e08120
> Create Date: 2026-03-08 ...
> """
> from alembic import op
> 
> revision = '<new_id>'
> down_revision = 'ccd985e08120'
> branch_labels = None
> depends_on = None
> 
> def upgrade() -> None:
>     with op.batch_alter_table('documents', schema=None) as batch_op:
>         batch_op.create_index(batch_op.f('ix_documents_title'), ['title'], unique=False)
>     with op.batch_alter_table('folders', schema=None) as batch_op:
>         batch_op.create_index(batch_op.f('ix_folders_name'), ['name'], unique=False)
> 
> def downgrade() -> None:
>     with op.batch_alter_table('folders', schema=None) as batch_op:
>         batch_op.drop_index(batch_op.f('ix_folders_name'))
>     with op.batch_alter_table('documents', schema=None) as batch_op:
>         batch_op.drop_index(batch_op.f('ix_documents_title'))
> ```
> 
> ---
> 
> ## 注意事项
> 
> - `check_access_requirements` 本身不需要改动，预加载会使其自动命中 SQLAlchemy 的 identity map 缓存，不再触发额外查询。
> - 保持现有 API 接口（请求/响应格式）完全不变。
> - 保持现有测试文件不变。
> - 不要修改与搜索无关的其他代码。
> 


</details>

Closes #9

## Changes

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `src/components/WritingGrid.tsx` | `SentenceGrid` に `targetKanji`/`furiganaMap`/`gridStyle` props追加、手本行にふりがな表示、練習行で空欄化 |

- **ふりがなソース**: `allKanji` データから `char → readings.kun[0] ?? readings.on[0]` でマッピング。文脈依存の読み分けは行わない（形態素解析なし）

- **全出現空欄化**: 例文中に対象漢字が複数回出現する場合、すべて空欄にする（書き取り練習量を最大化）

body:
### 💡 What
- Added `Style="{ThemeResource AccentButtonStyle}"` to the primary "Toggle Monitor" and "Save Settings" buttons.
- Added `SelectionMode="None"` to the "Monitor Logs" and "Stats" `ListView`s.
- Added `ToolTipService.ToolTip` to all "Toggle Monitor" and "Clear Logs" buttons.
- Added missing `AutomationProperties.AutomationId` to the inline "Toggle Monitor" button and the "Clear Logs" button.

### 🎯 Why
- **Visual Hierarchy:** By applying the `AccentButtonStyle` to primary actions (toggling the monitor, saving settings), users' eyes are naturally drawn to the most important actions on the page.
- **Feedback:** Disabling selection on purely informational lists (logs and stats) prevents confusing visual hover and click states that imply interactivity where there is none.
- **Accessibility/Intuitiveness:** Tooltips help mouse users understand icon-only or brief buttons.

### ♿ Accessibility
- Added `AutomationProperties.AutomationId` to ensure all interactive elements can be consistently identified by screen readers and UI automation tools.

author: copilot
body:
Tenant gallery links crashed with React error #310 ("Rendered more hooks than during the previous render") because `handleSaveEmail = useCallback(...)` was declared after conditional early-return guards, violating the Rules of Hooks.

Tenant albums aren't in localStorage, so the initial render always hit the `if (!album || ...)` early return — recording hooks only up to that point. On re-render (after `fetchPublicAlbum` resolved), React found more hooks than the previous render recorded and threw. Regular galleries never hit this path since their album is available on first render.

## Changes

- **`AlbumDetail.tsx`**: Moved `handleSaveEmail` `useCallback` to before the first conditional return, alongside all other hooks. Updated `album.id` → `album?.id` in the callback body and dependency array to handle the pre-load state safely.

```tsx
// Before: declared at ~line 752, after three conditional returns
const handleSaveEmail = useCallback(async () => {
  // ...uses album.id (non-optional, would throw if album undefined)
}, [purchaserEmail, album.id, albumId, pendingStripeParams]);

// After: declared before any conditional returns
const handleSaveEmail = useCallback(async () => {
  // ...uses album?.id (safe optional access)
}, [purchaserEmail, album?.id, albumId, pendingStripeParams]);

if (!album || album.enabled === false) { /* loading/not-found returns */ }
```

author: ashleyzhang01
body:
We're adding one more step in the GitHub integration installation pipeline, namely GitHub OAuth2 authorize. This is transparent from the UX perspective as the data exchange happens without user interaction.

The pipeline will now fail in these cases:
- If there is a mismatch between currently authenticated GitHub user (derived from OAuth2 authorize step) and the user who installed the GitHub app (https://github.com/apps/sentry-io)
- If there is a mismatch between `state` parameter supplied by user and pipeline signature
- If GitHub could not generate correct `access_token` from the `code` (wrong or attempt of re-use of `code`).

In all those cases, this error is shown:
![image](https://github.com/getsentry/sentry/assets/1127549/18923861-2ead-4cf5-adda-7738aef801d7)

## Summary by Sourcery

Add an OAuth-based verification step to the GitHub integration installation pipeline and tighten validation of installation requests and users.

New Features:
- Introduce an OAuth login view in the GitHub installation pipeline to obtain and validate the installing GitHub user.

Bug Fixes:
- Ensure GitHub installation requests without a valid installation ID, state token, access token, or matching installing user are rejected with a consistent error response.
- Prevent reusing GitHub app installations across organizations when the authenticated GitHub user does not match the original installer.

Enhancements:
- Centralize GitHub integration installation error rendering into a shared helper that respects customer domains.
- Extend GitHub integration tests to cover the new OAuth authorization flow, invalid installation requests, user mismatch scenarios, and pending-deletion behavior.

Tests:
- Expand integration tests for the GitHub app installation pipeline to validate the new OAuth authorize step, state validation, and error handling paths.

author: ckoenig673
body:
### Motivation

- Improve security for notification webhook settings by avoiding plaintext storage in SQLite while preserving existing notification behavior. 
- Provide operators a safer UX for secrets in the Settings UI so secrets are never echoed back in plaintext.
- Give operators a lightweight way to verify notification configuration via a test-send action without crashing the service on failures.

### Description

- Add a minimal secret helper `src/chonk_reducer/secrets.py` that encrypts/decrypts secret values with an application-level key from `CHONK_SECRET_KEY` and stores encrypted payloads with the `enc::` prefix. 
- Persist notification webhook secrets encrypted-at-rest by encrypting them before writing in `ChonkService.update_editable_settings` and by auto-encrypting bootstrap/plaintext rows in `_bootstrap_editable_settings`. 
- Decrypt webhook values only at runtime in `notifications._load_settings` and safely handle decryption errors by logging a warning and treating the value as unset. 
- Add a `send_test_notification` helper in `src/chonk_reducer/notifications.py` and wire a small `POST /settings/test-notification` action (FastAPI and fallback HTTP server) that reports basic success/failure without failing the service. 
- Update the Settings UI so secret fields (`discord_webhook_url`, `generic_webhook_url`) render masked/empty with a `placeholder="Set (hidden)"`, display a status such as `Configured (hidden)` when present, include an explicit `clear_<key>` checkbox to remove a secret, and preserve existing stored secrets when the input is left blank. 
- Add/adjust tests to validate encrypted storage, decryption behavior, masked UI rendering, blank submission preserves secrets, secret replacement updates encrypted values, test-notification behavior, and non-fatal failure handling. 
- Update `README.md` to document encryption-at-rest for webhook URLs, `CHONK_SECRET_KEY` usage, masked UI semantics, and test notification support; bump package version to `1.30.0` and compose `APP_VERSION` to `v1.30.0`.

### Testing

- Ran unit tests for the updated areas with `pytest -q tests/test_notifications.py tests/test_service.py` which passed. 
- Ran the full test suite with `pytest -q` and observed all tests passing (`129 passed`). 
- Performed a manual service startup and captured a Settings page screenshot to verify masked secret rendering and the new test button; the service remained stable when notification failures were simulated.

body:
### Motivation

- Provide an endpoint to search products by an input image and return the top matching products with product details.  
- Reuse existing image embeddings to perform similarity matching instead of adding new infra.  
- Surface SKU, image URL, price, discount and product name for the best matches to support image-based product discovery.

### Description

- Added a new endpoint `POST /api/imagesearch/find-closest` in `ImageSearchController` which accepts an uploaded image (`IFormFile`) and a `limit` query parameter and returns `ImageSearchResultResponse` items.  
- Extended `IProductImageService` with `FindClosestProductImagesAsync(Stream imageStream, int limit = 5)` and added an `ImageSimilarityMatch` record to transport match results.  
- Implemented `FindClosestProductImagesAsync` in `ProductImageService` to generate an embedding for the query image via `GenerateEmbeddingFromAzureAsync`, load stored embeddings from `IProductImageRepository`, compute cosine similarity (`CalculateCosineSimilarity`) and return the top matches.  
- Added the response contract `ImageSearchResultResponse` (contains `SkuId`, `ImageUrl`, `Price`, `Discount`, `ProductName`) and controller unit tests in `src/BP.Api/tests/BP.Api.Tests/Controllers/ImageSearchControllerTests.cs` covering missing-image validation and a mocked successful match flow.

### Testing

- Added unit tests `ImageSearchControllerTests` which exercise the `FindClosestProducts` controller behavior (missing image returns `BadRequest`, mocked matches return expected payload).  
- Attempted to run the test suite with `dotnet test src/BP.Api/tests/BP.Api.Tests/BP.Api.Tests.csproj` but the command failed in this environment because the `dotnet` SDK is not available; tests could not be executed here.

body:
## 概要

RefreshTokenエンティティにハッシュ化されたトークンを持たせ、UseCaseのOutputからRefreshTokenエンティティを削除してplainRefreshTokenのみを返すように変更しました。

## やったこと

- RefreshTokenにハッシュ化されたトークンを保持する実装
  - `TokenValue`を`HashedTokenValue`にリネームして意図を明確化
  - `RefreshTokenIssueService.issue()`でトークンをハッシュ化してエンティティに格納
  - リポジトリからハッシュ化処理を削除（エンティティが既にハッシュ化済み）
  - 平文トークンとハッシュ化トークンを別々に返す: `['token' => RefreshToken, 'plainToken' => string]`

- UseCaseのOutputの最適化
  - `LoginOutputData`から`RefreshToken`プロパティを削除
  - クライアントに必要な`plainRefreshToken`のみを含める
  - `LoginInteractor`でRefreshTokenエンティティは内部処理のみで使用

- テストの修正
  - `WithAuth`トレイトを新しい戻り値構造に対応
  - `adminUserId`パラメータから不要な`#[SensitiveParameter]`属性を削除

```php
// Before
$refreshToken = $service->issue($adminUserId)->unwrap();

// After
['token' => $refreshToken, 'plainToken' => $plainToken] = $service->issue($adminUserId)->unwrap();
```

## やってないこと

- 既存のRefreshTokenの移行（新規作成のみ対応）

author: adamhkan
body:
### Motivation
- The paper-level institution extractor missed many obvious affiliations on first pages and produced false positives from title/abstract fragments, reducing recall and precision for downstream filtering.  
- The goal is to boost paper-level recall (detect institution lines) while guarding precision so downstream briefing/institution filters remain reliable.  

### Description
- Add a curated `COMMON_ROBOTICS_INSTITUTIONS` list for high-frequency robotics universities and labs and wire it into the pipeline so `build_institution_specs` uses config entries + this curated list.  
- Improve parsing heuristics in `institution_filter.py`: expand candidate-line selection around abstract boundaries, extract inline compact markers (e.g., `1KAIST 2POSTECH`), dedupe parsed fragments, and run a page-level alias scan fallback to map known aliases when normal parsing yields no affiliations.  
- Tighten matching rules to reduce false positives by adding an acronym allowlist, requiring at least two informative tokens for token-overlap, ignoring generic tokens (e.g., `university`, `institute`) in overlap scoring, and raising fuzzy-match thresholds.  
- Files changed: added `src/daily_robotics_briefing/common_robotics_institutions.py` and updated `src/daily_robotics_briefing/institution_filter.py` and `src/daily_robotics_briefing/main.py` to integrate the new list and new heuristics.  

### Testing
- Compiled the package with `python -m compileall src` which completed successfully.  
- Re-ran the updated extractor across `reports/2026-03-07/2026-03-07.json` (via `PYTHONPATH=src python ...`) and measured improvements: papers with no detected affiliations decreased from `40` to `31`, papers with no canonical institution decreased from `62` to `47`, and `15` papers recovered canonical institutions that were previously missing.  
- I also inspected several recovered and suspicious cases manually (samples shown in the validation script output) to ensure the fallback and stricter matching do not introduce obvious new false positives.

author: inigodelportillo
body:
## Summary

This PR reviews and corrects the ITU-R P.678-3 implementation introduced in #76, fixing five bugs discovered through a line-by-line comparison with the recommendation PDF and the library conventions documented in `implementing_a_new_recommendation.md`.

### Critical fixes

- **NPZ longitude grid** (`v3_lat/lon/climatic_ratio.npz`): Source data ran −179.75 → +179.75; reordered to the library convention 0.25 → 359.75. Added wrap-around guard columns (lon = −0.25 and 360.25) so queries anywhere in [0°, 360°) — including cities near the Prime Meridian such as London — never fall outside the interpolator's range and return NaN.

- **`risk_of_exceedance` denominator** (Eq. 8): Was dividing by `inter_annual_variability(p)` (the *variance* σ²). Fixed to divide by `np.sqrt(inter_annual_variability(p))` (the *standard deviation* σ). The PDF's own identity check — "p_ℜ = p leads to ℜ = 0.5" — passes exactly after this fix.

- **p-unit convention**: Both public functions now accept `p` as a fraction in [0, 1] (matching the recommendation wording "0.0001 ≤ p ≤ 0.02"). The previous implicit ×100 / ÷100 scaling caused the binomial variance term `p(1−p)` in Eq. 5 to evaluate at p = 1 or p = 100, returning 0 or a large negative number.

- **Missing `risk_of_exceedance` delegation** in `__ITU678__`: Every call to the public module-level function raised `AttributeError` because the wrapper class only delegated `inter_annual_variability`. The missing method has been added.

### Additional improvements

- `variance_of_estimation` result cached per `p` value; inner autocorrelation sum truncated once `exp(−a(iΔt)^b) < 1e-13` (≈200× speed-up vs. summing all N = 525 960 terms).
- `itur/models/__init__.py` and `itur/__init__.py`: registered `itu678` and exported both public functions so `itur.inter_annual_variability` / `itur.risk_of_exceedance` are accessible after install.

### Registration

- `itur/models/__init__.py`: added `itu678` to `__all__` and `import itur.models.itu678`
- `itur/__init__.py`: added `from .models.itu678 import inter_annual_variability, risk_of_exceedance`

## Validation tests (`ITURP678_3TestCase`, 10 cases)

Since no official ITU validation spreadsheet exists for P.678, all tests are derived analytically from the recommendation itself:

| Test | Basis |
|------|-------|
| Identity: `risk(p, p, …) == 50 %` | PDF Annex 3 explicit statement |
| `variance_of_estimation` positive and < 0.1 % | Eq. 5 bounds |
| `inter_annual_variability` positive and finite (5 locations × 4 p values) | Eq. 1 |
| Reference values for London and New York within 5 % of inline formula | Eqs. 5–6 |
| Risk monotonicity (risk ↑ as p_ℜ ↓ below p) | Eq. 8 erfc property |
| Risk bounded ∈ [0 %, 100 %] | Probability axiom |
| Western hemisphere lookup (New York, Rio, Mexico City, Calgary) finite | NPZ wrap fix |
| Geographic variation: Sahel σ² > London σ² | Climatic ratio data |
| Caching: repeated `variance_of_estimation` calls identical | Implementation |
| Scalar float inputs accepted without error | Public API contract |

All 40 tests pass (30 pre-existing + 10 new).

## Test plan

- [x] `PYTHONPATH=/path/to/ITU-Rpy python test/ITU_validation_test.py` — 40 tests, 0 failures
- [x] `risk_of_exceedance(p, p, 51.5, -0.14)` returns `50.0000000000 %` (identity check)
- [x] `inter_annual_variability(0.01, 51.5, -0.14)` returns a finite positive value
- [x] `inter_annual_variability(0.01, 40.7, -74.0)` (New York, western hemisphere) — finite and positive after NPZ fix
- [x] No regressions in the 30 pre-existing tests

author: rampageservices
body:
## Summary

Implements the `AB` (Aperture Block) command from the Gerber spec (section 4.11).

An aperture block defines a reusable group of graphics commands that can be
flashed like any other aperture. The syntax is `%ABD<code>*%` ... graphics ... `%AB*%`.

### Parser

- `%ABD<code>*%` — opens a block definition: creates a `GERBV_APTYPE_BLOCK` aperture entry, allocates a separate net list, and redirects net creation into it
- `%AB*%` — closes the block: stores the recorded net list on the aperture and restores normal net chain
- Block apertures are registered in the D-code stats list (fixes "undefined D code" warnings)
- Block recording is managed via state fields in `gerb_state_t`

### Renderer

The block renderer is extracted into `draw_render_block_nets()`, a static helper that supports all content types and recursive nesting:

| Content type | How rendered |
|---|---|
| Linear draws (D01) | Round-cap line stroke |
| Arc strokes (G02/G03 CW/CCW) | `cairo_arc`/`cairo_arc_negative` with scale transform |
| Rectangle draw strokes (D01 + rect aperture) | Filled quad path |
| Polygon regions (G36/G37) | `draw_render_polygon_object()` |
| Shape flashes (circle, rect, oval, polygon) | Standard shape draw + fill |
| Macro flashes (AM) | `gerbv_draw_amacro()` |
| Nested block flashes (AB inside AB) | Recursive call to `draw_render_block_nets()` |

### Cleanup

- Block net lists are freed when the image is destroyed

### Files changed

- `src/gerbv.h` — add `GERBV_APTYPE_BLOCK` enum, `block_netlist` field
- `src/gerber.h` — add block recording state to `gerb_state_t`
- `src/gerber.c` — parse AB open/close, redirect nets during recording, register in D-code stats
- `src/draw.c` — `draw_render_block_nets()` helper for full content type rendering
- `src/gerbv.c` — add "block" to aperture type name table
- `src/gerb_image.c` — free block net lists on image destroy
- `test/inputs/test-aperture-block.gbx` — exercises all content types
- `test/golden/test-aperture-block.png` — golden reference image

## Test plan

## Change Description

### Presidio Evaluation Flow

This PR introduces the **Presidio Evaluation Flow**, a new interactive tool under `evaluation/ai-assistant/` that guides users through a human-in-the-loop PII detection evaluation process.

**USE THE run.md file to run in your environment.**

This is the main evaluation branch. PRs will continue to be merged here until the full evaluation flow is complete.

The UI was designed as a Figma Make prototype and converted to working code using the **Figma MCP server**.

**Frontend:** React + TypeScript + Vite + Tailwind CSS v4 + shadcn/ui + Recharts
**Backend:** Python + FastAPI + Poetry + Pydantic v2

## Next Steps

- [x] **Dataset interface** — Users can load local CSV/JSON files by path, select datasets from a dropdown, and preview records. If the dataset includes a pre-tagged entities column, detection steps can be skipped. Entity schema uses `entity_type` to match Presidio Analyzer's `RecognizerResult` format.
- [x] **LLM integration (optional)** — Add real LLM-based entity detection as an optional comparison source; the flow should work without LLM if the user doesn't need it
- [x] **Improved sampling** — Added real backend sampling with two strategies: random (`pandas.sample()` with fixed seed) and length-based (stratified by text-length terciles into short/medium/long buckets). Frontend now lets users pick the method via radio buttons, with semantic diversity shown as coming soon.
- [x] **Run Presidio based on config** — Execute actual Presidio analysis using the configured recognizers and thresholds (skip if CSV with detected entities is provided)
- [x] **Improved tagging experience** — Better UX for the human review step (inline text highlighting, keyboard shortcuts, batch operations)
- [x] **Import presidio-research and presidio-evaluator** — Bring the evaluation and research tooling into the Presidio repo for tighter integration
- [x] **Use the actual evaluator** — Wire the evaluation step to `presidio-evaluator` for real precision/recall/F1 calculation against the golden set
- [x] **Improve the scoring dashboard** — Richer visualizations, drill-down by entity type, historical comparison across runs

### Motivation
- Deployed frontend reported runtime failures from OpenRouter (e.g. "Provider returned error" / "No endpoints found") that are provider-side routing or model issues rather than static deployment errors. 
- The goal is to reduce hard failures for recoverable OpenRouter routing problems and give clearer guidance to users when the provider truly fails.

### Description
- Added detection for OpenRouter runtime provider failures and an enriched, actionable error message advising to switch model and check OpenRouter credits/balance (`storymaster-pro-complete/storymaster-pro/src/services/apiService.js`).

- Changes are scoped to the OpenRouter generation path and do not modify other provider flows.

### Motivation

- Adjust VN input, policy and runner behavior to support the new call/return flow, switch/branch nodes and to simplify choice handling in favor of the new drink panel integration.

### Description

author: copilot
body:
Implements the core framework for Aurelius — a latent diffusion model for text-to-audio generation that conditions synthesis on explicit inter-event relations (temporal, spatial, semantic).

## Corpora

- **`AudioEventSet`** — PyTorch `Dataset` of individual audio events. Each entry carries a `label`, optional `audio_path`, `category`, `duration`, and `tags`. Supports JSON manifest I/O, category/label filtering, and waveform loading with resampling and duration clamping.

- **`AudioRelSet`** — PyTorch `Dataset` of pairwise audio relations. Typed across three axes with a fixed vocabulary:
  | Type | Values |
  |---|---|
  | `temporal` | `before`, `after`, `simultaneous` |
  | `spatial` | `left`, `right`, `center`, `above`, `below` |
  | `semantic` | `similar`, `contrasting`, `complementary` |
  Each entry validates relation type/value at construction and exposes a `text_prompt` string for direct model conditioning.

## Model (`Aurelius`)

Latent diffusion model with DDPM noise schedule conditioned on fused text + relation embeddings:

```
TextEncoder       → text_emb  (512-d)
RelationEncoder   → rel_emb   (256-d)
ConditioningProjector → cond_emb (512-d)
UNet1D (diffusion backbone) → latent
```

```python
from aurelius import Aurelius, AudioRelSet

dataset = AudioRelSet.from_manifest("relations.json")
item = dataset[0]
# item["text_prompt"] → "A dog barks before a cat meows."

model = Aurelius(text_dim=512, rel_embed_dim=256, cond_dim=512,
                 latent_channels=8, latent_length=256)

text_emb = model.encode_text([item["text_prompt"]])
latents = model.generate(text_emb,
                         relation_types=[item["relation_type"]],
                         relations=[item["relation"]],
                         num_steps=50)
```

Training uses the standard DDPM objective via `model(..., target_latents=z)["loss"]`. The `TextEncoder` defaults to a lightweight character-level stub, intended to be replaced with CLAP or T5.

## Utilities

- `aurelius/utils/audio_utils.py` — `load_audio`, `save_audio`, `compute_mel_spectrogram`, `pad_or_trim`. Audio loading uses `torchaudio.info` to resolve native sample rate before computing frame offsets.

Branch protection required `tests (3.10/3.11/3.12)` but CI ran a job named `ci` on only 3.11/3.12, creating a phantom gate. No protected-file enforcement or auditable release path existed.

## Changes

### `ci.yml`
- Renamed job `ci` → `tests`; added `"3.10"` to matrix — branch protection required checks now have real counterparts
- Added `protected-file-guard` job (PR-only): diffs `origin/<base>..HEAD` and fails if any of `authority_gate.py`, `stop_machine.py`, `commit_gate/`, `.github/workflows/` are touched
- Added `build-artefact` job (main push only, gated on `tests`): zips governance primitives, uploads with commit SHA as artifact name

### `release.yml` (new)
- Triggers on `v*.*.*` tags only
- `verify-protected-branch` job gates everything: fails if the tagged commit is not reachable from `origin/main` via `git merge-base --is-ancestor`
- Runs full `tests` matrix (3.10/3.11/3.12) before building
- Produces zip + SHA256 checksum; creates GitHub Release with commit SHA in release notes

matrix:
  python-version: [ "3.10", "3.11", "3.12" ]
