author: copilot
body:
Adds a third operating mode ("STA web server") alongside the existing AP and Poster modes, selectable from the poster configuration page. Also upgrades vite to patch a `server.fs.deny` bypass vulnerability.

## New mode: STA web server (`startPoster == "sta_web"`)

Same local web server as AP mode, but connects to the configured WiFi as a STA instead of running its own AP. Boot sequence:

1. Starts `UnitCamS3-WiFi` AP for **10 s** — if a client connects, holds AP for reconfiguration
2. If no client: closes AP, connects to configured WiFi as STA (breathing LED during connect; reboots after 30 s timeout)
3. Serves the full web UI on the STA IP

### Firmware

- `app/hal/hal.h` + `hal_unitcam_s3_5mp.h` — added `StartStaWebServer()` / `startStaWebServer()` virtual + override
- `app/app.cpp` — routes `startPoster == "sta_web"` to new method
- `server_sta_web.cpp` *(new)* — full mode implementation; AP-wait, STA connect, web server startup with named constants `AP_WAIT_TIMEOUT_MS` / `WIFI_CONNECT_TIMEOUT_MS`
- `api_poster.cpp` — added `/api/v1/start_sta_web` endpoint; sets `startPoster = "sta_web"` and reboots
- `server_ap.cpp` — fixed hardcoded HTML response length → `sizeof(AssetPool::GetImage().index_html_gz)`

### Web UI

- `card-poster-config.tsx` — `Switch` toggle selects **Image Poster** vs **Web Server (STA)**; interval/timezone fields hidden in web server mode; confirm dialog and post-save navigation update accordingly
- `card-sta-web-start.tsx` *(new)* + `page-sta-web-start.tsx` *(new)* — notice page explaining STA mode behavior (LED states, access via local IP, 10 s AP reconfiguration window)
- `main.tsx` — registers `/sta_web_start` route
- `json_server/unitcams3.json` — mock `start_sta_web` response for dev

## Security: vite `server.fs.deny` bypass

Upgrades vite from `5.0.5` → `5.4.21` (CVE affects 5.0.0–5.0.11, patched in 5.0.12). Rebuilt `app/assets/images/index.html.gz` (233 951 bytes) and updated the array size in `types.h` accordingly.

author: yuvrajangadsingh
body:
fixes #4898

adds inline commenting on commit diff views, same as PR review comments but standalone, no issue/PR needed.

## what this does

- new `commit_comment` table with migration (v326), stores repo_id, commit_sha, tree_path, line, poster, content, diff patch
- web handlers for GET (comment form), POST (create comment), POST (delete comment)
- generates diff context patch around the commented line using existing `GetFileDiffCutAroundLine`
- modified diff section templates (unified + split) to render existing commit comments inline between diff lines
- reuses existing JS for the add-code-comment button clicks and delete-comment flow
- separate templates from PR review comments (no review workflow, no resolve/unresolve, no pending state)

## how it works

1. user clicks the `+` button on a commit diff line (same button as PR diffs)
2. JS fetches the comment form via GET to `/{repo}/commit/{sha}/comment`
3. user writes comment and submits, JS POSTs to the same URL
4. handler creates the `CommitComment` record, renders the conversation HTML back
5. JS replaces the form with the rendered conversation (same as PR review flow)
6. on page reload, existing comments are loaded via `FindCommitCommentsForDiff` and rendered inline

## files changed

| file | what |
|------|------|
| `models/repo/commit_comment.go` | CommitComment model, CRUD, FileCommitComments grouping |
| `models/migrations/v1_26/v326.go` | migration to create commit_comment table |
| `models/migrations/migrations.go` | register migration |
| `routers/web/repo/commit_comment.go` | web handlers (form, create, delete) |
| `routers/web/repo/commit.go` | load commit comments in Diff handler |
| `routers/web/web.go` | register routes |
| `templates/repo/diff/box.tmpl` | conditional comment URL for commit vs PR |
| `templates/repo/diff/section_unified.tmpl` | render commit comments inline |
| `templates/repo/diff/section_split.tmpl` | render commit comments inline |
| `templates/repo/diff/commit_conversation.tmpl` | conversation wrapper (simplified) |
| `templates/repo/diff/commit_comments.tmpl` | individual comment rendering |
| `templates/repo/diff/commit_comment_form.tmpl` | comment form |
| `templates/repo/diff/new_commit_comment.tmpl` | form wrapper for GET endpoint |

this is an MVP. follow-up work could include: edit comments, reactions, email notifications, API endpoints, comment counts on commit list pages.

## Summary
Enhanced the `RecordReflectRefine` headline component with a multi-phase animation sequence and added a scroll-down indicator to the intro slide. The component now features a word-by-word reveal phase before cycling, with the subtitle and chevrons appearing after the first complete cycle.

## Key Changes

**RecordReflectRefine.jsx:**
- Implemented intro reveal phase where words appear one at a time with teal highlighting
  - Step 1: "Record," appears (teal)
  - Step 2: "Reflect," appears (teal), "Record," becomes dark
  - Step 3: "Refine:" appears (teal), previous words become dark
- Added `onFirstCycleComplete` callback that fires when the first full cycle completes after intro
- Introduced `showSubtitleText` state to fade in subtitle after first cycle completes
- Added opacity transitions (0.4s for words, 0.8s for subtitle) for smooth reveal animations
- Click behavior now advances intro steps before entering cycling mode
- Removed framer-motion dependency (now uses only React hooks)
- Updated JSDoc to reflect new intro behavior

**IntroSlide.jsx:**
- Added `ScrollChevrons` component displaying animated double-chevron scroll indicator
  - Positioned at bottom center with bounce animation
  - Uses teal color (rgb(82, 156, 156)) matching the design system
  - Appears after a configurable delay (default 3000ms) via `chevronDelay` calibration
- Integrated chevron visibility with headline's `onFirstCycleComplete` callback
- Added `showChevrons` state to control chevron visibility and animation

## Implementation Details
- Intro phase uses separate `introStep` state (0-3) to track reveal progress
- Transition from intro to cycling is gated by `introComplete` state
- Uses `useRef` to track whether first cycle callback has fired (prevents duplicate calls)
- Chevron animation uses CSS keyframes with staggered timing for visual appeal
- All timing is configurable through calibration props for flexibility across variants

author: lse0907
body:
### Motivation

- Standardize and expand order workflow by replacing legacy statuses with a clearer set (`new`, `checked`, `making`, `ready_for_packing`, `completed`, `cancelled`) and introduce per-item status, batching and persistent packing checks. 
- Add a configurable staff view mode (`simple` / `station`) so stores can use either a single-stream staff UI or a split station workflow. 
- Make frontend and server logic compatible by converting legacy values, normalizing older data, and adding automatic order-status recomputation from item statuses.

### Description

- Added migration `docs/sql/supabase-staff-view-v1.sql` that updates schema and data: adds `stores.staff_view_mode`, replaces and constrains `orders.status` values, adds `order_items.status` and `order_items.batch`, creates `order_item_packing_checks` table, implements `set_updated_at` trigger, and creates `recompute_order_status_from_items` function and trigger to recalculate order status from item states.

body: title! basically, previously we'd do this inline, and now we have each error type implement a trait to suggest if it's transient. also schema changes aren't errors, just require a reconnect (which will bust the relation cache / send them again) and this handles as a signal vs. just being a similar error. > [!NOTE] > ### Refactor replication error types to separate `SchemaChanged` from `ReplicationError` and add `is_transient` > - Removes `ReplicationError::SchemaChanged` variant and introduces a standalone `SchemaChanged` struct with `relation_id`, `namespace`, and `name` fields in [error.rs](https://github.com/a24films/puffgres/pull/99/files#diff-95a1ce0f9ba2d4b573600bcfcd36cc522e086609b61c6e82dfba8aa2829cbe4f). > - Adds `is_transient()` to `ReplicationError` (true for `Connection`/`Stream`) and a parallel `is_transient()` to `PgError` in [pg/src/error.rs](https://github.com/a24films/puffgres/pull/99/files#diff-dfc1c92ff34cef99589111a796ac3d2b0bf16a54681921b57221f3610ed390d1). > - `ReplicationStream::recv_batch` now returns `Result>` where `BatchResult` is either `Batch(StreamingBatch)` or `SchemaChanged(SchemaChanged)`, so schema changes are delivered as non-error signals instead of errors. > - Adds `ReplicationStream::recv_raw` for consuming raw WAL messages; commits are auto-acked and relation messages update the cache automatically. > - The CDC runner in [run.rs](https://github.com/a24films/puffgres/pull/99/files#diff-83f76f4167e32e162ccecf948bf5e0f2d45a07adcbccb7d748f88f9ef2978086) is updated to match on `BatchResult`, reconnecting on `SchemaChanged` and surfacing other errors. > - Risk: callers that previously matched on `ReplicationError::SchemaChanged` must now handle `BatchResult::SchemaChanged` in the `Ok` path. > > #### 🖇️ Linked Issues > Addresses [STU-2015](https://linear.app/a24/issue/STU-2015). > > > > Macroscope summarized 5edd631. > >

body:
Two unrelated test failures: team invitations failing with a MySQL NOT NULL constraint on `token`, and DNS update/delete endpoints returning 403 for record owners.

## Changes

- **`app/Actions/Jetstream/InviteTeamMember.php`** — populate the `token` field (required, non-nullable, no DB default) when creating a team invitation:
  ```php
  $team->teamInvitations()->create([
      'email' => $email,
      'role'  => $role,
      'token' => Str::random(64),  // added
  ]);
  ```

- **`routes/api.php`** — fix implicit route model binding for the DNS resource. `Route::apiResource('dns', ...)` generates `{dns}` as the route parameter, but controller methods declare `DnsSetting $dnsSetting`. Laravel resolves `$dnsSetting` by looking for route key `{dns_setting}`, finds nothing, and injects a fresh empty model — making `$dnsSetting->domain` always `null` and the auth check always 403:
  ```php
  // Before
  Route::apiResource('dns', DnsController::class);
  // After
  Route::apiResource('dns', DnsController::class)->parameters(['dns' => 'dnsSetting']);
  ```
  The `->parameters()` call renames the route segment to `{dnsSetting}`, matching the controller variable without changing any URLs.

The root cause was a combination of missing `resolveOrgContext` middleware on the GET endpoints (causing orgId mismatch between the X-Org-Id header and the raw `user.orgId`), no incident existence validation (silently returning empty results for invalid IDs), and lack of defensive data handling on the frontend.

## Type of Change

## Changes Made

**Backend (`server/routes/incidents.ts`)**:
- Added `resolveOrgContext` middleware to both `GET /api/incidents/:incidentId/evidence-chain` and `GET .../verify` endpoints (consistent with the POST endpoint)
- Changed orgId resolution from `req.user?.orgId` to `req.orgId || req.user?.orgId` to honor the X-Org-Id header
- Added incident existence check — returns 404 instead of silently returning empty array for non-existent incidents
- Added org boundary enforcement — returns 403 if incident belongs to a different org
- Added structured error logging for fetch failures

**Frontend (`client/src/pages/evidence-chain-viewer.tsx`)**:

author: sammyjoyce
body:
OpenAI Responses requests in the vendored Tachikoma dependency could describe JSON schema output at the public API layer, but the internal Responses payload types were still missing a first-class structured output representation. That meant callers could ask for structured output while the provider either dropped the format information or encoded it through loose JSON handling.

The root cause was that the Responses request model only carried GPT-5 verbosity settings and relied on untyped schema storage. The OpenAI provider also treated GPT-5 preamble support and structured output formatting as separate concerns, so non-GPT-5 requests with explicit output formats were not consistently encoded.

This change adds a typed structured output model, teaches the Responses payload to encode `text`, `json_object`, and `json_schema` formats directly, and threads provider output-format requests through the OpenAI Responses provider. It also expands model capability coverage and adds regression tests around structured output generation and Responses request encoding.

Validation used `swift test` in `vendor/Tachikoma` on March 8, 2026.

author: krishna-swaroop
body:
## Summary

This branch brings the RBAC session-auth work to `main`, followed by a focused performance pass and a documentation refresh.

From a user perspective, the changes do four things:
- switch the app to signed session-cookie auth with RBAC-managed access control
- reduce expensive backend work in workspace load, path resolution, commit history filtering, and file/folder lookups
- reduce frontend startup cost with safer route/dialog chunking outside the visualizer surface
- update the repo documentation so Docker hosting, local development, auth, and project conventions match the current codebase

## Root Cause and User Impact

Before this branch, there were three separate problems:

First, auth and permissions were not modeled around persistent RBAC-backed user sessions. That made it harder to host the platform safely with clear viewer/designer/admin boundaries.

Second, several backend and frontend paths were doing duplicate or overly expensive work. Workspace load duplicated project/folder hydration, `.prism.json` path resolution could fall back into repeated filesystem detection, filtered subproject history scaled poorly, and some UI paths made redundant requests or left polling active longer than necessary.

Third, the repo documentation had drifted behind the code. Docker instructions, auth expectations, session-secret handling, and several feature notes no longer described the runtime accurately.

The net effect for users was slower workspace/detail flows, extra backend load on larger repos, and confusing deployment setup when trying to host the app with Docker.

## What Changed

### Auth and access control

- added RBAC-backed session auth flow
- introduced signed `HttpOnly` session cookies
- enforced viewer/designer/admin role checks across API routes
- documented the requirement for `SESSION_SECRET` when auth is enabled

### Backend performance work

- added `/api/workspace/bootstrap` so workspace initial load can fetch projects and folders together
- reduced folder-tree work by avoiding unnecessary full project hydration
- improved `.prism.json` path resolution so explicit config is honored first and missing fields alone are auto-detected
- replaced expensive subproject commit-history filtering with path-scoped git queries
- added a lightweight commit-distance endpoint for project history UI
- cached folder metadata and repeated file listings where safe
- added a project overview endpoint to combine detail and README loading

### Frontend performance work

- moved workspace data loading to the bootstrap endpoint
- removed redundant fetches in project detail and settings flows
- cleaned up import-dialog polling on close and unmount
- memoized repeated tree and size calculations in assets/docs surfaces
- route-split non-visualizer app surfaces and deferred dialog/runtime code more aggressively, while avoiding the chunking pattern that broke the production Docker bundle

### Documentation

- updated the root README to match current auth, Docker, and local-dev behavior
- rewrote deployment guidance around Docker, `.env`, `SESSION_SECRET`, and Google OAuth
- refreshed docs for comments, metadata, path mapping, workspace behavior, frontend responsibilities, and project repo structure

## Validation

The branch was validated in pieces as the work landed:

- backend modules compiled successfully with `backend/venv/bin/python -m compileall backend/app`
- frontend lint and production builds passed with `npm run lint` and `npm run build`
- local benchmark runs showed meaningful improvements in filtered history, path-config resolution, folder-tree generation, workspace load, and repeated file-listing paths
- Docker hosting was manually checked after the chunking regression was narrowed down and corrected

## Notes

- visualizer-specific implementation was intentionally left out of the performance pass except for keeping viewer-related bundles isolated
- there is an unrelated unstaged local change in `frontend/vite.config.ts` in the working tree; it is not part of this PR

create table public.manual_payment_requests (
  id         uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  app        text not null,
  plan_id    text not null,
  plan_name  text,
  amount     numeric(10, 2),

  notes      text,
  created_at timestamptz not null default now(),
  updated_at timestamptz not null default now()
);
```

RLS mirrors the `subscribers` table: service role has full access; authenticated users can read their own rows. Indexes on `email`, `reference`, and `status`.

author: dangtrivan15
body:
## Summary

- **Process group kill**: `kill_process_tree()` now uses `os.killpg()` when the subprocess was started with `start_new_session=True`, killing the entire process group atomically. This eliminates the TOCTOU race where children get reparented to PID 1 before `psutil.children()` runs.
- **`start_new_session=True` on all 6 spawn sites**: Every `subprocess.Popen` call (orchestrator, agent manager, dev server manager) now creates a new process group on Unix.
- **`cli.js` process group kill**: `killProcess()` now sends SIGTERM to `-pid` (the process group) instead of a single PID. Uvicorn is spawned with `detached: true`.
- **Periodic orphan reaper**: Background task (Linux only) scans every 60s for chrome/node/esbuild processes orphaned under PID 1 and kills them after a 30s grace period.

## Problem

After each agent session, dev server processes (`node`, `npm`, `vite`, `esbuild`) and Playwright browser instances (`chrome`, `chrome_crashpad`) survive as orphans. Over hours, these accumulate to hundreds of processes consuming gigabytes of memory, eventually hitting the container memory limit and triggering OOM kills.

Root cause: `kill_process_tree()` uses `psutil.Process(pid).children(recursive=True)` to find children, but between the parent dying and the tree walk executing, children get **reparented to PID 1** and are no longer in the tree.

Observed in production: **183 out of 243 processes** were orphans (~67 Chrome processes, ~49 dev server processes, ~56 esbuild processes), consuming 4.4 GB growing toward a 10 GB limit.

## Test plan

- [ ] Run `python -m pytest tests/test_process_utils.py -v` — verifies process group kill works on children and grandchildren
- [ ] Deploy to a container, run agents for several hours, monitor orphan count stays near zero:
  ```bash
  kubectl exec <pod> -- bash -c 'for f in /proc/[0-9]*/status; do ppid=$(grep "^PPid:" $f 2>/dev/null | awk "{print \$2}"); pid=$(grep "^Pid:" $f 2>/dev/null | awk "{print \$2}"); [ "$ppid" = "1" ] && [ "$pid" != "1" ] && echo $pid; done | wc -l'
  ```
- [ ] Verify memory stays stable via `cat /sys/fs/cgroup/memory.current`
- [ ] Verify Windows is unaffected (process group changes are Unix-only)

Fixes #164, fixes #197.

TestCluster.Start warms up DefaultClass connections between all node pairs via GRPCDialNode so that GetCircuitBreaker(nodeID, DefaultClass) returns ok=true for every pair. In DRPC mode, GetBreakerForAddr dispatches to drpcGetBreakerForAddr, which looks only in rpcCtx.drpcPeers; those entries are never created by GRPCDialNode, so GetCircuitBreaker returned ok=false for nodes that had not yet sent a DefaultClass DRPC message.

TestReportUnreachableRemoveRace calls GetCircuitBreaker(DefaultClass) on server 1 and requires ok=true, but with DRPC enabled server 1 had no DefaultClass DRPC peer entry for the partitioned node, causing the test to fail.

Fix: when rpcCtx.UseDRPC is true, also call DRPCDialNode(DefaultClass) for every node pair in the warmup loop, creating the DRPC peer entries that mirror the existing gRPC ones.

body:
# PR summary: VP and reward phase fixes

**Branch:** `feature/vp-and-reward-phase-fixes`

## Victory Points (VP) and scoring

- **VP module** (`env_components/vp.py`): Primary mission scoring — 5 VP per controlled objective, cap 15 per turn; scored at end of Command from round 2 for both player and opponent.
- **EnvScoreState** (`types/env_score_state.py`): `player_vp` and `opponent_vp` exposed in observation and info for reward criteria and UI.
- **WargameEnv**: Holds `_vp_state`, scores player VP before opponent turn and opponent VP after their turn; passes score state into observation and step info.

## Reward phases and criteria

- **`player_leading_vp`** (`reward/criteria/player_leading_vp.py`): New success criterion so the phase can advance when the player has more VP than the opponent.
- **Episode termination**: Episode no longer ends when `player_leading_vp` is met; only max turns, game over, or other phase criteria end the episode.
- **`objective_control`** calculator: Reward = VP earned this step from controlling objectives (for the control_objectives phase).
- **`closest_objective` fix**: Uses the same offset-based “at objective” rule as the game (`norm_offset <= radius`). Phase-one (move_and_group) reward now matches the success definition so the agent gets reward for reaching objectives.

## Scripted opponent (`scripted_advance_to_objective`)

- **Overshoot**: `ActionHandler.best_action_toward(dx, dy, max_distance=...)` added; scripted policy caps movement by distance to capture boundary so units don’t overshoot.
- **Landing inside**: “At objective” is strict-internal (`norm_offset <= r`); movement aims at capture centre `(obj - r/2)` and allows a minimum step so units can step into the circle.
- **Alignment with game**: Policy uses the same offset-based “at objective” and capture circle as the env (distance_cache), so scripted units reliably land inside objectives.

## Observations and UI

- **Per-objective distances**: Each objective observation includes `closest_player_distance` and `closest_opponent_distance` for targeting.
- **Objective radius** in observation space for objectives.
- **South panel** (human renderer): Shows player/opponent VP and reward phase state.

## Config and docs

- **Env configs**: `4v4_scripted_opponent_fixed_objectives.yaml` and `9v9_scripted_opponent_fixed_objectives.yaml` (scripted opponent, fixed objectives, reward phases move_and_group → control_objectives).
- **Docs**: `opponent-policies.md`, `reward-phases.md`, `tabletop-rules-reference.md` updated for VP, scripted behaviour, and `closest_objective`.

## Tests

- VP and clock integration; fixed placement; opponents (scripted advance, no overshoot, lands inside radius); reward phases (`closest_objective` offset behaviour, `player_leading_vp`, phase manager); DQN/PPO and state tests updated for new obs/score state.

---

**Net:** VP scoring and env score state, reward-phase fixes (`player_leading_vp`, no early termination, `objective_control`, `closest_objective` aligned with at_objective), scripted opponent fixes (overshoot and landing inside objectives), richer objective observations and south-panel VP/phase display, new configs and docs.

author: gambletan
body:
## Summary

When a URL contains userinfo (e.g., `https://user@domain.com` or `https://user:pass@domain.com`), it was being processed as a valid URL and crawled, creating duplicate URLs. This is common with misconfigured mailto links that end up as malformed URLs.

This fix strips the userinfo portion from URLs while keeping the rest of the URL intact, so that `https://user@domain.com` becomes `https://domain.com` and is recognized as a duplicate.

## Changes

- Modified `resolveUrlWithBaseHref` in `apps/api/src/scraper/scrapeURL/lib/extractLinks.ts` to detect and strip userinfo from URLs
- When a URL has username or password in its userinfo section, we now return `url.origin + url.pathname + url.search + url.hash` which strips the userinfo but keeps the rest of the URL

## Testing

The fix handles these cases:
- `https://user@domain.com` → `https://domain.com`
- `https://user:pass@domain.com/path` → `https://domain.com/path`
- `https://email@domain.com` → `https://domain.com` (malformed mailto)

Fixes #2591

author: copilot
body:
Replaces the single Credentials provider with two fully isolated providers: `"player"` (userId only, no password) and `"admin"` (password only, no DB involvement). Updates middleware route protection and rebuilds the admin login page.

## `src/lib/auth.ts`
- **`"player"` provider** — renamed from anonymous default; verifies `is_active=1` and an active/scheduled game via `game_players` join; throws `"No active game found. Ask your host!"` if none exists
- **`"admin"` provider** — compares submitted password against `ADMIN_PASSWORD` env var using `crypto.timingSafeEqual` (both sides SHA-256 hashed to normalise buffer lengths before comparison); returns hardcoded `{ id: "admin", name: "Admin", role: "admin" }` — never touches the DB
- JWT/session callbacks unchanged in shape; `avatar_url` and `activeGameId` are `null`/`""` for admin tokens

```ts
Credentials({
  id: "admin",
  credentials: { password: { type: "password" } },
  async authorize(credentials) {
    const submittedHash = crypto.createHash("sha256").update(submitted).digest();
    const adminHash    = crypto.createHash("sha256").update(adminPassword).digest();
    if (!crypto.timingSafeEqual(submittedHash, adminHash))
      throw new Error("Invalid admin password");
    return { id: "admin", name: "Admin", role: "admin" };
  },
})
```

## `src/middleware.ts`
- `/admin/login` — pass-through unless already admin (→ `/admin/dashboard`)
- `/admin/*` (explicit `pathname !== "/admin/login"` guard) — requires `role === "admin"`, redirects to `/admin/login` instead of `/`
- `/game/*` — requires `role === "player"` (previously any session), redirects to `/login`
- `/login` — redirects to `/` only for active player sessions (not any session)

## `src/app/(admin)/admin/login/page.tsx`
- Rebuilt as a `"use client"` component — single password input, no email field, no player avatars
- Calls `signIn("admin", { password, redirect: false })`; shows inline `"Invalid password"` on failure; redirects to `/admin/dashboard` on success with `window.location.href` fallback

## `AGENT_MAP.md`
- Updated descriptions for `auth.ts`, `middleware.ts`, `admin/login/page.tsx`
- Added explicit rows for `/api/auth/callback/player` and `/api/auth/callback/admin` in the API routes table

## Summary
This PR adds a comprehensive test suite for the elliptec library using mocked serial ports and controllers, eliminating the need for physical hardware during testing. The test suite covers all device classes (Rotator, Linear, Iris, Slider, Shutter) and core components (Controller, scan module).

## Key Changes

### New Test Files
- **tests/test_devices_mock.py**: Comprehensive tests for all device classes using mocked controllers
  - Tests for Rotator (ELL14/ELL18): angle conversions, get/set/shift operations
  - Tests for Linear (ELL20): distance conversions and movement operations
  - Tests for Iris (ELL15): aperture range checking and movement with bounds validation
  - Tests for Slider (ELL6/ELL9): slot positioning and multi-slot configurations
  - Tests for Shutter: open/close operations with normal and inverted modes
  - Tests for Motor and ContinuousMotor base classes: home, jog, offset, and status extraction

- **tests/test_controller.py**: Controller class tests with mocked serial ports
  - Connection initialization and error handling
  - Context manager behavior
  - Response parsing (position, status, info dict)
  - Instruction sending with various message formats (string, int, negative int)
  - Connection closing

- **tests/test_scan.py**: Scan module tests
  - Port discovery with and without serial numbers
  - Device scanning across address ranges
  - Error handling for serial exceptions

- **tests/conftest.py**: Shared test fixtures and utilities
  - `make_info_response()`: Factory function for creating canned info responses
  - `mock_controller` fixture: Pre-configured mocked Controller instance

### Test Infrastructure
- Uses `unittest.mock` for mocking serial ports and controller responses
- Helper function `_make_device()` instantiates device classes with mocked controllers
- Canned protocol responses eliminate need for real hardware communication
- Tests cover both unit-level conversions and integration with mocked controller

### Existing Code Updates
- **tests/test_unit.py**: Added tests for motor info parsing (I1, I2 response codes) and move_check error handling

## Implementation Details
- Mock strategy: Controller.send_instruction is mocked to return canned protocol responses
- Device initialization properly loads motor info on first call, then returns position/status tuples
- Tests verify both low-level conversions (_pos_to_unit, _unit_to_pos) and high-level operations (get/set/shift)
- Comprehensive coverage of edge cases: out-of-range values, invalid commands, inverted modes
- All tests are isolated and can run without any physical hardware or serial ports

body:
The project failed to build due to three independent issues: a missing peer dependency, a network call to Google Fonts at build time, and a React Context violation in the Next.js App Router. ## Changes ### `react-is` missing peer dependency `recharts` requires `react-is` as a peer dep but it wasn't installed, causing a webpack `Module not found` error at compile time. Added `react-is` to `package.json`. ### Google Fonts removed from build path `layout.tsx` imported `Poppins` via `next/font/google`, which issues an outbound TLS request to `fonts.googleapis.com` during the build — fatal in offline/CI environments. Replaced with a CSS custom property fallback: ```css /* app/globals.css */ :root { --font-poppins: "Poppins", "Segoe UI", Roboto, Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif; } ``` All existing `.poppins` class usages continue to resolve through `var(--font-poppins)` unchanged. ### React Context in Server Component `layout.tsx` (a Server Component) was directly rendering `SessionProvider`, `AuthProvider`, `ThemeProvider`, `Toaster`, and `ToastContainer`, triggering *"React Context is unavailable in Server Components"* during static prerendering. Consolidated all client-side providers into the existing `providers.tsx` (`"use client"`) and reduced `layout.tsx` to a single `` wrapper. ```tsx // layout.tsx — before: SessionProvider/AuthProvider/ThemeProvider rendered directly in Server Component // layout.tsx — after: export default function RootLayout({ children }) { return ( {/* "use client" — all context lives here */} Loading...}> Loading...}>{children} ); } ``` ### ESLint config Added `.eslintrc.json` (`next/core-web-vitals` + `next/typescript`) with pre-existing `no-explicit-any` / `no-unused-vars` violations downgraded to warnings so they don't block the build. ## Result ![Stockly running — login page](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7bbf9b34-8dcd-4172-95a3-132f1ca27209) `npm run dev` starts cleanly; the app serves the login page at `/`. > [!WARNING] > >

Fixes #117199
Correctly emits `folding_changed` signal any time the `folded` property changes.

The current behaviour has many cases where the `folding_changed` signal is not emitted, despite the documentation describing it as "Emitted when the container is folded/expanded."

author: copilot
body:
SVG-only icon manifest breaks PWA installability on Android (Chrome requires raster icons) and iOS (Safari ignores SVG for `apple-touch-icon`).

### Changes

- **`manifest.json`** — Fix SVG icon `sizes` from fixed pixels to `"any"`. Add PNG fallback entries (192×192, 512×512, 512×512 maskable) for Android PWA install and TWA launcher
- **`index.html`** — Point `apple-touch-icon` to PNG (`icon-192.png?v=2`); keep SVG favicon for modern browsers
- **`icon-192.png` / `icon-512.png`** — Raster icons generated from existing SVG sources via `rsvg-convert`
- **`service-worker.js`** — Add PNG icons to precache list, bump cache version v32 → v33
- **`netlify.toml`** — Add `Cache-Control: no-cache` for `/*.png` to prevent CDN serving stale icons

### Manifest icon strategy

```json
{ "src": "icon-192.svg?v=2", "sizes": "any",     "type": "image/svg+xml", "purpose": "any" },
{ "src": "icon-512.svg?v=2", "sizes": "any",     "type": "image/svg+xml", "purpose": "any" },
{ "src": "icon-192.png?v=2", "sizes": "192x192", "type": "image/png",     "purpose": "any" },
{ "src": "icon-512.png?v=2", "sizes": "512x512", "type": "image/png",     "purpose": "any" },
{ "src": "icon-512.png?v=2", "sizes": "512x512", "type": "image/png",     "purpose": "maskable" }
```

SVG remains primary for browsers that support it; PNG fallbacks satisfy Android installability requirements and iOS `apple-touch-icon`. No old icon references remain anywhere in the codebase.

author: gannonh
body:
## Summary - add orchestrator and sub-agent session hierarchy with persisted child sessions, nested chat list rendering, and child transcript projection in Electron - wire delegated lifecycle events through storage, event processing, preload, and shared session types so sub-agent chats can be selected and hydrated independently - add a repo-managed pre-push validate hook and harden the hook environment so local validation matches CI without breaking git tests in worktrees ## Test Plan - [x] bun run validate:local ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **New Features** * Hierarchical sessions with nested UI, unread aggregation, and visual nesting * Subagent support: spawn/status lifecycle, child sessions with parent transcript projection and continuation context * Safe session upserts that preserve transcripts on metadata-only updates * Idle-turn finalization to avoid stale "Thinking..." indicators * **Tests** * Broad unit and e2e coverage for hierarchy, subagent flows, transcript merging, unread bubbling, and UI * **Chores** * CI/E2E workflow updates, local validate scripts, and git hook installer added

Greptile Summary

This PR implements a multi-agent orchestration session tree for the Electron app. When the Claude agent fires a `Task` tool call, the `SessionManager` intercepts it and materializes a child `ManagedSession` with full hierarchy metadata (`sessionKind`, `parentSessionId`, `orchestratorSessionId`, `delegatedToolUseId`, etc.), persists it to disk via `writeTaskChildSessionDurably`, and propagates lifecycle events (`subagent_spawned`, `subagent_status_changed`) to the renderer. The renderer projects these into a visual tree in `SessionList` (depth-1 indented rows with a `CornerDownRight` icon) and, when a child session is opened in `ChatPage`, builds a merged display transcript by projecting the parent's tool-use subtree via `projectSubagentTranscript` and combining it with the child's own messages. The PR also ships a hardened `pre-push` hook that clears injected GIT_* environment variables before running the local validate gate. Key changes to review: - **`mergeUpsertedSession` broad spread**: on every `subagent_status_changed` event, the incoming payload (built from the current parent session) will overwrite `isProcessing`, `model`, `thinkingLevel`, and `permissionMode` on the child session, potentially discarding child-specific configuration. Only `messages` is explicitly guarded against clobber. - **`delegatedToolUseId` missing from `SessionMeta`**: all seven sibling hierarchy fields are projected into `SessionMeta` and `extractSessionMeta`, but `delegatedToolUseId` is omitted, creating an inconsistency that could cause silent `undefined` returns in future consumers. - **`projectSessionTree` depth-1 only**: the tree projection only expands direct children of root sessions. Grandchildren (subagent spawning a subagent) are silently omitted from the list even though `SessionListItem.depth` is typed as `number`. - **`pre-push` hook drops `git lfs pre-push`**: the original LFS-generated hook is completely replaced; if any files in the repository are tracked via Git LFS, pushes will no longer perform LFS object validation.

Confidence Score: 4/5

- PR is safe to merge with a few logic gaps to address before they compound in future multi-level nesting scenarios. - The feature is well-architected and comprehensively tested across 15+ new test files. The data-flow design (main-process persistence → IPC events → renderer upsert) is clean and the transcript projection logic is correct. The score is held back by: (1) `mergeUpsertedSession` clobbering live session fields on every status-change event, which could produce subtle bugs when a child session is being actively used; (2) the removal of `git lfs pre-push` from the hook, which could allow broken LFS pushes; and (3) the depth-1 tree limitation which is undocumented and may surprise future contributors. None of these are blockers for the current feature scope, but #1 in particular could manifest as a user-visible regression. - `apps/electron/src/renderer/event-processor/helpers.ts` (mergeUpsertedSession clobber), `.githooks/pre-push` (LFS regression), `apps/electron/src/renderer/lib/session-tree.ts` (undocumented depth-1 limit)

Important Files Changed

 | Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | apps/electron/src/main/sessions.ts | Core orchestration logic: adds `ensureTaskChildSession`, `updateTaskChildSessionStatus`, and `buildSubagentContinuationPrompt` to the `SessionManager`. `processEvent` is now `async` to support awaiting child-session creation on `Task` tool events. The `toStoredSession` refactor cleanly extracts persistence. The `clearTaskChildSessionLinks` cleanup on session deletion is solid. | | apps/electron/src/renderer/event-processor/helpers.ts | Adds `mergeUpsertedSession` for child-session upserts. The `messages` field is correctly protected, but the broad spread of the incoming payload will clobber `isProcessing`, `model`, `thinkingLevel`, and `permissionMode` on every `subagent_status_changed` event with parent-derived values. | | apps/electron/src/renderer/lib/session-tree.ts | New utility for projecting the flat session list into a tree. author: felipeness
body:
## Summary

Related to #35481 — companion to #35978

Browsers normalize tab (`\t`), newline (`\n`), and carriage return (`\r`) characters to spaces when parsing HTML attribute values ([HTML spec](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/parsing.html#attribute-value-(double-quoted)-state)). React's hydration attribute comparison uses strict string equality, which can produce false mismatch warnings when server and client attribute values differ only by this whitespace normalization.

This change adds a fallback comparison in the hydration path that normalizes `\t`, `\n`, and `\r` to spaces before comparing, matching browser behavior.

### What changed

In `ReactDOMComponent.js`:

- Added `NORMALIZE_ATTRIBUTE_WHITESPACE_REGEX` and `normalizeAttributeValueForComparison()` helper
- Modified `hydrateAttribute()`: after strict equality fails, performs a normalized comparison before reporting a mismatch
- Modified `warnForPropDifference()`: adds whitespace normalization as an additional comparison step

### Context

- **This fix targets the DEV warning path** — in production, React does not compare individual attributes during hydration (only text content)
- **Defensive fix** — even if source transforms normalize whitespace (see #35978), this ensures React's hydration comparison is resilient to `\t\n\r` ↔ space differences from any source
- **Preserves existing behavior** — strict equality is checked first (fast path), normalization is only a fallback

### Relationship to #35978

| PR | Layer | What it fixes |
|----|-------|---------------|
| #35978 | React Compiler codegen | Normalizes whitespace in compiled JSX attribute output |
| This PR | React DOM hydration | Prevents false mismatch warnings for whitespace-only differences |

Either fix independently resolves the reported issue. Together they provide defense in depth.

## How did you test this change?

Added 3 test cases to `ReactDOMHydrationDiff-test.js`:

| Test | Scenario |
|------|----------|
| `does not warn when attribute values differ only by whitespace normalization` | `className` with `\n` vs space |
| `does not warn for tab and carriage return normalization` | `className` with `\t` and `\r\n` vs spaces |
| `does not warn for title attribute whitespace normalization` | `title` with `\n` vs space |

```bash
yarn test packages/react-dom/src/__tests__/ReactDOMHydrationDiff-test.js
# Test Suites: 1 passed, 1 total
# Tests:       40 passed, 40 total (37 existing + 3 new)
```

author: dritory
body:
## Summary
This PR resolves critical issues with type layout computation in the monomorphizer and adds support for closure parameters in function signatures. It also enables external package type declarations to be available during type checking.

## Key Changes

### 1. **Topological Sort for Type Declarations** (rask-mono)
- Added `topo_sort_type_decls()` using Kahn's algorithm to order struct/enum/union declarations by field dependencies
- Ensures that when a struct references an enum declared later in source order, the enum's layout is computed first and cached
- Fixes silent runtime crashes caused by structs getting incorrect field offsets when referencing unknown types
- Added `collect_type_deps()` to recursively extract type names from field type strings

### 2. **External Package Type Registration** (rask-resolve, rask-types)
- `ResolvedProgram` now includes `external_decls: HashMap<String, Vec<Decl>>` to track public types from imported packages
- `Resolver::resolve_package()` collects public struct/enum/trait/type-alias declarations from external packages
- Type checker registers these external types so qualified access (e.g., `pkg.Type`) resolves correctly through the type table
- Module namespace resolution (`__module_X.Field`) now looks up fields in the type table before falling back to hardcoded builtin mappings

### 3. **Closure Parameter Support** (rask-mir)
- Function parameters with function-type signatures (e.g., `f: |i32| -> i32`) are now registered as closure locals
- `closure_locals` set tracks which parameters are closures so call sites emit `ClosureCall` instead of `Call`
- `func_sigs` map stores return types for closure parameters to enable proper type inference at call sites

### 4. **Enum Payload Destructuring** (rask-mir)
- Added support for named-field destructuring in match arms (e.g., `Shape.Circle { radius }`)
- Extracts enum variant fields and binds them to local variables with correct types
- Handles field lookup by name within enum variants

### 5. **Test Coverage**
- Added `struct_forward_references_enum()` test verifying topological sort handles forward references
- Added `test_external_decls_populated()` confirming external package types are collected
- Added `test_external_decls_empty_for_single_file()` and `test_external_decls_excludes_private_types()` for edge cases

### 6. **Documentation Updates** (examples/README.md, TODO.md)
- Marked examples 10, 11, 14, 15 as runnable (previously spec-only)
- Updated TODO.md to reflect completed work on enum destructuring, type layout resolution, and closure parameters

## Notable Implementation Details
- Topological sort gracefully handles cycles by appending remaining declarations in source order
- Type dependency collection handles `UnresolvedNamed`, `UnresolvedGeneric`, `Option`, `Result`, and `Slice` types
- External declarations are only collected for public types (filtered by `is_pub` flag)
- Module namespace resolution is now generic and extensible via the type table rather than hardcoded cases

author: tternquist
body: Adds `auth_ttl` to cache entries and introduces a configuration to refresh hot/warm entries when they exceed their authoritative TTL. This feature allows the cache to prioritize freshness for frequently accessed (hot/warm) records by refreshing them when they become "stale" according to the original upstream TTL, even if they are still valid by the extended cache TTL. This balances high cache hit rates with respecting source intent for dynamic data, without increasing upstream load for cold entries. A design note on refresh configuration simplification has been added in `docs/refresh-config-simplification-notes.md` to address concerns about increasing complexity. ---

## Summary
This PR adds consistent whitespace trimming across multiple endpoints to improve data quality and prevent issues with leading/trailing spaces in user inputs.

## Key Changes
- **Items endpoint** (`backend/routes/items.py`):
  - Strip whitespace from `upc`, `source`, and `notes` fields in `create_item()`
  - Strip whitespace from `upc` field in `update_item()`
  - Add conditional stripping for `source` and `notes` in `update_item()` to handle null values safely

- **Categories endpoint** (`backend/routes/categories.py`):
  - Strip and validate category names in `create_category()` to reject empty strings after trimming
  - Strip category names in `update_category()` before checking for duplicates and updating

- **Authentication endpoint** (`backend/routes/auth.py`):
  - Strip whitespace from usernames in `register()`, `login()`, and `update_user()` endpoints
  - Updated comments to reflect that usernames are now normalized with both stripping and lowercasing

## Implementation Details
- Whitespace stripping is applied before validation checks to ensure consistent behavior
- Null/empty value checks are performed after stripping to catch whitespace-only inputs
- Conditional stripping (`.strip() if value else value`) is used in update operations to safely handle null values
- This prevents duplicate entries caused by whitespace variations and improves data consistency across the application

This pull request introduces a new configuration system for managing recommended AI models based on GPU VRAM, and refactors how VRAM is accessed throughout the codebase. The main changes include the introduction of a new `ModelInfoConfig` class to encapsulate model metadata, a static list of recommended models, and utility methods for querying VRAM. These changes improve maintainability and make it easier to recommend appropriate models for different hardware setups.

**Model recommendation and configuration improvements:**

* Added a new `ModelInfoConfig` class and `ModelLevel` enum in `ModelInfoConfig.cs` to represent model metadata and performance levels (Light, Balanced, Powerful) for recommended models.

body:
`PlaceRepository.DeleteAsync(id)` accepted only an ID with no ownership check, allowing any authenticated user to delete any place by guessing its ID.

## Changes

- **`IPlaceRepository` / `PlaceRepository`** — Changed `DeleteAsync(string id)` to `DeleteAsync(string id, string userId)`. Implementation uses `GetByIdAsync(id, userId)` — a single user-scoped query that both verifies access and retrieves the entity — before deletion. Returns silently if the user lacks access or the place doesn't exist.

- **`WishlistDetailPage.razor` / `PlacesPage.razor`** — Updated `DeletePlace` to pass the current user's ID to `DeleteAsync`, with explicit null guards.

- **`OllamaChatService` / `PlaceMcpTools`** — Updated to pass `userId` to `DeleteAsync` for defense-in-depth (both already performed a pre-check via `GetByIdAsync`).

```csharp
public async Task DeleteAsync(string id, string userId)
{
    var place = await GetByIdAsync(id, userId);
    if (place != null)
    {
        _context.Places.Remove(place);
        await _context.SaveChangesAsync();
    }
}
```

author: ll1r1k-1337
body:
💡 What: Refactored `NatsServerBuilder` setter methods to mutate `this.options` directly instead of using object spread syntax (`...this.options`) on every call. Added `readonly` modifier and cloned `DEFAULT_NATS_SERVER_OPTIONS` in the constructor to prevent shared state mutation.

🎯 Why: Every call to a builder method (like `setPort`, `setVerbose`, etc.) was previously creating a completely new object via spread syntax. For a chained builder pattern, this creates unnecessary short-lived objects that increase garbage collection overhead. Mutating a single cloned object is significantly more efficient.

📊 Impact: Reduces object allocations during builder chaining. If a user calls `NatsServerBuilder.create().setPort(4222).setVerbose(false).setIp('127.0.0.1').build()`, it now creates 1 options object instead of 4.

🔬 Measurement: Run `npm run lint` and `npm test` to verify no functionality or type safety was broken. The tests already assert that custom options are properly applied and default options are not mutated.

# Ticket
https://community.openproject.org/wp/70213

# What are you trying to accomplish?
Stabilize unit specs that are susceptible to out-of-hours or wall-clock-sensitive failures.

This branch currently contains only unit-spec fixes on top of the feature-spec branch it is based on.

Example failed run:

- https://github.com/opf/openproject/actions/runs/22880794198/job/66382848520?pr=22086

# What approach did you choose and why?
I kept this follow-up branch focused on unit-side stabilization only.

The current concrete changes are:
- a speculative hardening of a component spec with a relative-time assertion by freezing the clock and using a deterministic `updated_at` value, so the rendered "Updated about 1 month ago" text no longer depends on the actual date the suite is run
- deterministic reminder service specs that no longer depend on the real current date/time for future/past validation and timezone conversion paths

The branch is intentionally based on #22251 because the broader out-of-hours investigation and reporting work lives there, but the changes in this PR should read as unit-spec-only follow-up fixes.

author: garretfick
body:
## Summary
Implements the FIND and REPLACE standard functions for string manipulation in IEC 61131-3, enabling substring searching and string replacement operations.

## Key Changes

- **VM Execution (vm.rs)**
  - Added `FIND_STR` opcode: searches for the first occurrence of one string within another, returning a 1-based position (0 if not found)
  - Added `REPLACE_STR` opcode: replaces L characters at position P in a string with another string, allocating result to a temporary buffer

- **Code Generation (compile.rs)**
  - Modified assignment compilation to handle STRING variables stored in the data region separately from stack-based variables
  - Added `compile_find()`: generates code for FIND(IN1, IN2) function calls
  - Added `compile_replace()`: generates code for REPLACE(IN1, IN2, L, P) function calls with proper temporary buffer allocation
  - Added helper functions `resolve_string_arg()` and `collect_positional_args()` for function argument processing

- **Emitter (emit.rs)**
  - Added `emit_find_str()`: emits FIND_STR opcode with string data offsets
  - Added `emit_replace_str()`: emits REPLACE_STR opcode with string data offsets

- **Opcodes (opcode.rs)**
  - Defined `FIND_STR` (0xE3) and `REPLACE_STR` (0xE5) opcodes with their operand specifications

- **Standard Library (stdlib_function.rs)**
  - Registered FIND and REPLACE function signatures in the standard library
  - Updated function count assertions to reflect the two new string functions

- **Tests**
  - Added comprehensive end-to-end tests for FIND covering: substring matching, not found cases, start/end positions, empty strings, and exact matches
  - Added comprehensive end-to-end tests for REPLACE covering: middle replacement, insertion-only, deletion-only, start/end replacements, and variable arguments

## Implementation Details

- FIND returns a 1-based position following IEC 61131-3 conventions
- REPLACE handles edge cases: clamping position to valid range, handling negative lengths, and respecting temporary buffer capacity
- Both functions work with STRING variables stored in the data region with proper header management (max_length and current_length fields)
- String arguments must be variable references; expressions are not supported (enforced via `resolve_string_arg()`)

## summary

author: mustafa11300
body:
## Summary

Fix the `RunTaskStreaming` handler in the ReAct Actor to stream steps in real-time as they are produced, instead of batching them all after execution completes.

## Motivation

The `RunTaskStreaming` message variant exists specifically to let consumers receive [ReActStep](cci:2://file:///Users/mustafahussain/mofa/crates/mofa-foundation/src/react/core.rs:32:0-53:1)s incrementally as the agent reasons. However, the current implementation calls `agent.run()` (which collects all steps internally into a `Vec`), waits for it to finish, and *then* sends every step through the `mpsc` channel in a loop:

```rust
// ❌ Before — all steps arrive in a burst AFTER completion
let result = agent.run(&task).await;
if let Ok(ref res) = result {
    for step in &res.steps {
        let _ = step_tx.send(step.clone()).await;
    }
}
```

This defeats the purpose of streaming — the consumer sees nothing until the entire task is done, then receives every step at once.

## Changes

- **[core.rs](cci:7://file:///Users/mustafahussain/mofa/crates/mofa-foundation/src/react/core.rs:0:0-0:0)** — Add `ReActAgent::run_streaming(&self, task, step_tx)` method that mirrors the existing [run()](cci:1://file:///Users/mustafahussain/mofa/crates/mofa-foundation/src/react/actor.rs:485:4-533:5) loop but sends each step through the provided `mpsc::Sender<ReActStep>` immediately as it is produced (Thought, Action, Observation, FinalAnswer).
- **[actor.rs](cci:7://file:///Users/mustafahussain/mofa/crates/mofa-foundation/src/react/actor.rs:0:0-0:0)** — Replace the run-then-forward pattern in the `RunTaskStreaming` handler with a single call to `agent.run_streaming(&task, step_tx).await`.

```rust
// ✅ After — steps stream in real-time
agent.run_streaming(&task, step_tx).await
```

## Related Issues

Closes the streaming steps bug in the ReAct Actor.

## Testing

1. `cargo check -p mofa-foundation` — compiles with zero warnings ✅
2. `cargo test -p mofa-foundation react` — all 14 tests pass ✅

## Checklist

- [x] `cargo fmt --check` passes
- [x] `cargo check -p mofa-foundation` passes
- [x] `cargo test -p mofa-foundation react` passes (14/14)
- [x] Architecture layer rules respected (change is entirely within `mofa-foundation`)
- [x] No new dependencies added
- [x] PR is small and focused (one logical change, 2 files)
- [x] Commit message follows Conventional Commits

body:
## Summary
This PR adds a fallback mechanism to look up users in Firebase Auth when they're not found in Firestore, and implements a one-time migration to apply pending MedicPoints to existing Firebase Auth users who were missing email fields in their Firestore documents.

## Key Changes
- **Firebase Auth fallback lookup**: Added fallback logic in `preload_points_for_email()` and `get_user_medicpoints()` to search Firebase Auth by email when Firestore queries return no results. When a user is found in Firebase Auth, their Firestore document is backfilled with the email field to prevent future lookup failures.

- **Pending points migration function**: Implemented `flush_pending_medicpoints()` to process all pending MedicPoints documents and apply them to users who exist in Firebase Auth. This fixes the issue where users who claimed points in the Mini App never received them due to missing email fields in their Firestore documents.

- **Startup migration**: Integrated `flush_pending_medicpoints()` into the FastAPI application lifespan to automatically run the migration on server startup, with error handling and logging.

## Implementation Details
- The Firebase Auth lookup is wrapped in try-except blocks to gracefully handle cases where users don't exist in Firebase Auth yet
- Email backfilling uses `merge=True` to preserve existing user data
- The migration function updates both the user document and leaderboard, then deletes the pending document after successful application
- Comprehensive logging tracks applied, skipped, and failed migrations for monitoring

author: perongh
body:
## Summary
Extend `boot-assets` so ArcBox can ship and build the guest assets required for
native k3s support.

This adds direct binary source support, publishes the guest `k3s` runtime
binary, expands the rootfs with the extra host utilities k3s expects, and fixes
local EROFS image generation so the produced rootfs boots correctly with the
`v0.0.5` kernel.

## What Changed
- add direct binary source support to upstream runtime sync
  - new `format = "binary"` support alongside archive extraction
  - validation so `tgz` sources require `extract` and direct binaries do not
- add guest `k3s v1.34.3+k3s1` to `upstream.toml`
- update `sync-binaries` to download direct executables and preserve executable permissions
- expand the rootfs contents for k3s support
  - `ebtables`
  - `ethtool`
  - `socat`
  - required shared libraries for those packaged tools
- move EROFS image creation into Docker instead of relying on host `mkfs.erofs`
- disable xattrs in the Dockerized EROFS build so local macOS builds work correctly on host-mounted source trees
- update README documentation for:
  - direct-binary runtime sync
  - manifest-listed runtime binaries
  - expanded rootfs contents
  - Docker-only local build prerequisites

## Why
ArcBox native Kubernetes needs:
- the guest `k3s` binary shipped with the runtime asset set
- extra guest utilities that k3s expects to find
- a reproducible local build path for `rootfs.erofs`

During manual testing, the local macOS build path produced an EROFS image that
did not boot with the required `v0.0.5` kernel. The proper fix was to stop
building the EROFS image on the host and instead generate it inside Docker,
which makes the local build behave like CI/release artifacts.

## Manual Verification
- built local runtime binaries, including `k3s`
- built a local `boot-assets v0.4.0` release using the `v0.0.5` kernel
- inspected the resulting `rootfs.erofs`
- confirmed the rebuilt rootfs uses a `4096` byte EROFS block size and boots successfully in ArcBox manual testing


Resolves ABX-186 ABX-187

author: asmithbot
body:
## Summary
Reworked `CMapMesh::Draw` to use a more plausible original ordering:
- resolve null `materialSet` fallback before draw-loop state setup
- initialize `remaining` as an unsigned count from `unkCount` (`0xA`) after fallback
- keep draw entry iteration logic intact while using an explicit decrement pattern

This preserves behavior while improving code generation around loop/control flow and register setup.

## Units/functions improved
- Unit: `main/mapmesh`
- Function: `Draw__8CMapMeshFP12CMaterialSet`
  - Before: **89.347824%**
  - After: **94.347824%**
- Neighboring effect in same object:
  - `DrawMeshCharaShadow__8CMapMeshFUsUs`: **90.2381% -> 98.57143%**

## Progress evidence
From objdiff:
- Unit `main/mapmesh` code (`.text`) match:
  - Before (selector snapshot): **68.9%**
  - After: **69.34384%**
- No data regressions introduced in this change.
- Build verifies successfully with `ninja`.

## Plausibility rationale
The updated structure is closer to natural game-source style:
- perform default parameter resolution first
- then derive loop state (`remaining`, entry pointer)
- iterate display-list entries with straightforward loop control

This avoids contrived compiler coaxing and keeps the function readable and source-plausible.

## Technical details
Key objdiff change for `Draw` was in loop/control-flow codegen. Reordering initialization around the null fallback and using an unsigned loop count improved emitted compare/decrement sequence and reduced function-level instruction diffs.

author: caifer88
body:
The endpoints `/api/assets`, `/api/history`, and `/api/transactions` previously constructed custom dictionaries with manual mapping to match the frontend `camelCase` expectations. This approach lost Pydantic's powerful validation features.

This update introduces specific Pydantic response models (`AssetResponse`, `HistoryResponse`, `TransactionResponse`) that utilize `ConfigDict(alias_generator=to_camel)`. This ensures that properties like `is_archived` correctly surface as `archived` (via `validation_alias`) and `risk_level` correctly surfaces as `riskLevel`. 

For complex formatting, such as converting `snapshot_date` to `month` (`YYYY-MM`) and handling `Decimal` to `float` castings for Javascript consumption, a `@model_validator(mode="before")` is used. This method safely intercepts the ORM object and builds a mapping dictionary.

Lastly, the `main.py` route definitions are simplified down to returning the raw database results directly, letting Pydantic cleanly handle all the formatting logic.

author: copilot
body:
The project was deployable only via Docker. This adds first-class support for deploying on **Render** (PaaS) and **Hostinger** (shared hosting) with no container runtime required.

## New files

- **`render.yaml`** — Render Blueprint spec. Build step runs `composer install`; start command uses PHP's built-in server via `router.php`. Declares the three Mailgun env vars so the dashboard prompts for them.
- **`router.php`** — Built-in server router for Render. Routes `/` and bare `.php` requests to `frontend/`, passes static assets through, blocks `.env` access.
- **`.htaccess`** — Apache/LiteSpeed rules for Hostinger. Mirrors `docker/apache.conf`: sets `DirectoryIndex frontend/index.php`, rewrites `/` to the SPA entry point, routes bare PHP filenames (AngularJS XHR template fetches like `/home.php`) to `frontend/`, and denies HTTP access to `.env`.

## Modified files

- **`backend/contact-form.php`** — Adds a zero-dependency `.env` file parser that runs before any business logic. Only activates when `.env` exists **and** the variable is not already in the environment, so Docker and Render behaviour is unaffected. Handles both `"quoted"` and `'quoted'` values correctly.

```php
// Only loads when platform hasn't injected the var
if ($key !== '' && getenv($key) === false) {
    putenv("{$key}={$val}");
    $_ENV[$key] = $val;
}
```

- **`README.md`** — Restructured into three deployment options: Render (Option 1), Hostinger (Option 2), Docker (Option 3, retained for local dev/VPS).

This PR comprehensively modernizes the project's dependency management, CI/CD security, and local development workflow.

### Dependency Management (uv)
- **Switched to uv**: Migrated the project to [uv](https://astral-sh.uv/) for high-performance dependency management.
- **NEP-29 Alignment**: Adjusted core dependencies to match **xarray 2024.9.0** requirements (NumPy >= 1.23, SciPy >= 1.9), following the ~18-month rolling support window.
- **Optimized Xarray**: Transitioned to `xarray[io,accel,parallel]` to automatically manage high-performance I/O and parallel processing libraries.
- **Deterministic Builds**: Added `uv.lock` to ensure reproducible environments across all platforms.

### Pre-commit & Security
- **Modern Hooks**: Updated all pre-commit hooks to their latest versions and expanded Mypy type-checking coverage.
- **Developer UX**: Configured local hooks to run as **pre-push** for faster, uninterrupted local commit cycles.
- **Security**: Implemented a CodeQL security fix in the Docker Publish workflow to prevent untrusted code execution.

### Documentation & Branding
- **README Refresh**: Updated all installation and quality control instructions to use `uv run`.
- **Badge Polish**: Rearranged badges for better readability, grouping CI and Docs Status at the top.
- **Feature Refinement**: Updated feature descriptions to accurately reflect the new optimized Xarray integration.

author: eddie0199
body:
### Motivation
- Users visiting `/reset-password` directly were immediately shown an "invalid or expired" message because the invalid branch was triggered when no recovery tokens existed.
- The goal is to only show the invalid/expired state for real recovery attempts that include tokens and to present a neutral guidance state (or allow a redirect) for direct visits without tokens.

### Description
- Modified `src/components/ResetPasswordPage.js` to add a `hadRecoveryTokens` state and to detect whether recovery tokens were present in the request (tracked during bootstrap as `hadRecoveryTokensInAttempt`).
- Changed bootstrap logic so the invalid message is only set when token-based recovery was attempted and failed to establish a session, and errors from non-token direct visits do not set the invalid error.
- Adjusted the `invalid` condition to `hadRecoveryTokens && Boolean(error) && !hasSession` and added a `showNeutral` render branch for direct visits without tokens that displays a neutral guidance message and a back-to-login button.
- Kept the existing successful recovery flow intact so the real reset form (`showForm`) is shown when a session is established after token exchange/verification.

### Testing
- Ran `npm run build` successfully to validate the bundle and catch syntax/runtime issues; the build completed without errors.
- Started the dev server with `npm start` and verified the `/reset-password` page manually to confirm the neutral state vs. token flows behaved as expected.
- Executed a Playwright script that opened `http://127.0.0.1:3000/reset-password` and captured a screenshot of the neutral state, which completed successfully.

body:
`OllamaChatService.ExecuteToolAsync` used null-forgiving operators (`!`) on model-supplied parameters, causing `NullReferenceException` inside repository calls when a required arg was missing — surfacing only as a generic `"Tool execution failed"` response.

## Changes

**`OllamaChatService.cs`** — Replaced all 8 `Str(args, "x")!` usages with explicit guard validation, consistent with the already-correct `delete_place` pattern:

```csharp
// Before
"delete_trip" => await DeleteTripAsync(Str(args, "trip_id")!, userId),

// After
"delete_trip" => Str(args, "trip_id") is { } deleteTripId && !string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(deleteTripId)
    ? await DeleteTripAsync(deleteTripId, userId)
    : "Missing required parameter: trip_id",
```

Affected tools: `create_trip`, `update_trip`, `delete_trip`, `get_wishlist`, `create_wishlist`, `update_wishlist`, `delete_wishlist`, `get_place`.

**`ChatPage.razor`** — Removed `@onkeydown:preventDefault="@(e => e.Key == "Enter" && !e.ShiftKey)"`. Blazor does not support a delegate here (requires `bool`), and the attribute also conflicts with the existing `@onkeydown` binding, causing a build failure. The Enter-vs-Shift+Enter logic is already handled in `HandleKeyDown`.

body:
💡 What: Combined multiple separate counting queries in `/audio-digests/statistics` and `/podcasts/statistics` into a single, efficient multi-dimensional `GROUP BY` query. The respective grouped tuples are then reduced in Python to calculate marginal totals for statuses, voice providers, etc.
🎯 Why: Previously, the statistics endpoints executed several independent full-table count queries grouped by individual properties (status, voice, provider). This created an N+1 style bottleneck and redundant DB scans.
📊 Impact: Reduces the number of database queries executed in `get_audio_digest_statistics` from 4 to 2 (1 for all categorical counts, 1 for scalar total duration), and in `get_podcast_statistics` from 3 to 2, effectively eliminating repetitive full table scans and significantly reducing DB latency.
🔬 Measurement: Run the test suite using `DATABASE_URL=sqlite:///./test.db TEST_DATABASE_URL=sqlite:///./test.db uv run pytest -m "not e2e" tests/api/test_podcast_api.py tests/api/test_audio_digest_api.py`. Performance can be measured by tracing DB query execution count during route calls.

author: adrienbrault
body:
useSudoku uses useReducer with an init function, so the puzzle
parameter is only read on initial mount. When rematch fires and
Yjs propagates a new puzzle, the prop updated but the reducer
state stayed stale — the board never actually reset.

Adding key={mp.puzzle} forces React to unmount and remount
MultiplayerBoard with the new puzzle, fully reinitializing
the useSudoku reducer, timer, and all local state.

The LA County scraper stored the entire per-department HTML response as a single `CapturedDocument` even when it contained multiple cases. This caused:

- **`fetch_documents()`** — now calls `_split_cases_html()` on each POST response and creates one `CapturedDocument` per case section

author: je223xa
body:
Hey there,
I hope these are not too many changes, I tried to keep it as clean as possible. I dont know where the PR should point, merging it directly to main problably doesnt make much sense.
First of all: Awesome application! Thanks for spending the time, this really is the easiest finance application out there. One functionality that was missing for me, was being able to better view expenses by tags and other categories. However, with the current architecture with html and css, scaling the app is not very feasible and itś getting quite complex

I wanted to propose a change where the backend and frontend of your application are split, therefore making it easier in the future to switch to a more flexible frontend solution like react. This PR could be the first step to enable that switch easily in the future.

I have moved all endpoints under a new subpath called `/api`, as this is standard for the openapi spec. I also generated a openapi spec file, which could be used to generate automatic frontends for react or other applications. I included a collection for the api client application [Bruno](https://www.usebruno.com/), that way when it goes to test the app manually its easier for frontend developers to check.

I have also some explanations in [changelog.md](changelog.md). I have removed the react app for now, but I left the comment to show the approach.


So, summary:
1. implemented a devcontainer for containerized development
2. moved all endpoints under `/api`
3. added openapi spec
4. moved the frontend code to the internal folder to be able to start them on different ports


Let me know what you think!

author: ashimnandi-trika
body:
## Summary

- Adds `examples/stocks/risk-managed-momentum-agent.py` -- a self-contained momentum trading agent that validates every order through [System R](https://systemr.ai)'s pre-trade risk gate before execution
- Demonstrates the pattern: **detect signal -> validate with risk API -> execute if approved**
- Uses `alpaca-py` for market data and order execution, `httpx` for the System R API call

## What is System R?

[System R](https://systemr.ai) is an AI risk intelligence platform that provides pre-trade risk checks for autonomous trading agents. The `pre_trade_gate` endpoint evaluates proposed trades against configurable risk limits (concentration, drawdown, sector exposure) and returns an approve/reject decision in real time.

- Demo repo: https://github.com/System-R-AI/systemr-agent-demo
- API docs: https://agents.systemr.ai/docs

## How the example works

1. Scans a universe of 7 large-cap symbols for 20-day high breakouts
2. For each breakout signal, calls `POST https://agents.systemr.ai/v1/compound/pre-trade-gate` with the proposed trade details
3. If the risk gate returns `"decision": "approve"`, submits a market order via `TradingClient`
4. If rejected, logs the reason and skips the trade (fail-closed design)

## Test plan

- [ ] Verify the example runs with valid Alpaca paper trading keys and a System R API key
- [ ] Verify the example gracefully handles System R API downtime (fail-closed)
- [ ] Confirm the example follows existing patterns in `examples/stocks/`

body:
This PR fixes a bug that occurs when the consumer opts to set the `showNoOptionsFound` prop to `true` (i.e. they want the "No results found" component to display when that is the case). Generally, the "No results found" component displays when it is intended to, although not in this scenario: - input is empty - user enters character(s) - while results are being fetch (and the loading component is displayed), the "No results found" component also displays (underneath the loading component) This is a result of that scenario legitimately meeting all the current conditions that determine the boolean assigned to `showNoOptionsFound`: https://github.com/andygout/accessible-autocomplete/blob/1b475bdc0eeeb56a79dfe4134d3eb2741e87ccbd/src/autocomplete.js#L441-L442 - `this.props.showNoOptionsFound` is `true` - `inputFocused` is `true` - `options` is still `[]` until the async callback returns, i.e. `noOptionsAvailable` is `true` - `queryNotEmpty` is `true` - `queryLongEnough` is `true` However, once any search for results has been completed, `noOptionsAvailable` becomes `false`, meaning the issue does not happen for subsequent changes to the input. It is only when the input changes from no characters to one or more characters. #### Before https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ed9c7911-941e-4323-9358-c663e1194947 #### After https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d98405a1-4296-4820-bcf1-697bdb2dc25a --- #### Update I got to the bottom of what was causing this issue though I don't see a way of fixing that particular issue. 1. Upon page load, the autocomplete component contains this element: ```html
``` 2. author: simple-agent-manager[bot]
body:
## Summary

- Removed token revocation from `handleCompleteTask()` in `mcp.ts` — the MCP connection outlives individual tasks (scoped to ACP session), so revoking the token on task completion broke all subsequent MCP tool calls permanently
- Token cleanup is now handled by KV TTL auto-expiration (default 2h) and task-runner DO cleanup on failure
- Added 3 regression tests covering token lifecycle across task completion

## Post-Mortem

**Root cause**: `handleCompleteTask()` revoked the MCP token from KV immediately, but the MCP connection (and bearer token) is scoped to the entire ACP session with no refresh mechanism. After revocation, the MCP client received 401, fell into OAuth discovery recovery, and entered permanent failure.

**Class of bug**: Credential lifecycle mismatch — a credential scoped to a shorter lifecycle (task) was invalidated while the connection depending on it (ACP session) persisted.

**Process fix**: Added "Credential Lifecycle Alignment" rule to `.claude/rules/06-technical-patterns.md` requiring verification that credential lifecycles match their consuming connections.

Full post-mortem: `docs/notes/2026-03-08-mcp-token-revocation-postmortem.md`

author: jameshartig
body:
We need to improve the accuracy of the "savings" calculation. Currently if we fill up the battery during a day it shows as significant negative energy savings (i.e. cost). But this isn't accurate because we will end up using the battery in the future. Come up with an improvement to the savings calculation that accurately reflects how we are saving them money by charging one day and using it later for cheaper. We also need to ignore battery savings (and costs) when the action for that time is paused or when storm hedge was enabled and a storm forced charging.
Actions are taken every 13 minutes. It should be more accurate than just if ANY pause happens during an hour. Instead look at what the state was for each part of the hour and assume proportional energy use. So if it was paused for half the hour then don't count half the charge use.

Rather than trying to track energy inventory which will be hard to explain to an average user instead just not track energy cost that was not associated with unused battery. Then when calculating discharge savings calculate to the best of your ability when it was charged from looking at the prices history and the energy history for the last 24 hours. Assume that battery use in one hour comes from the most recent hour that was charged from and work backwards to account for when the energy used was charged and what the rate was.

Add extensive and comprehensive tests  to the savings tests as new subtests with assertions to ensure the calculations are correct and the returned fields are as expected.

author: maxwellcalkin
body:
## Summary

Fixes #6119

When `disableToolCallResolution: true` is used with `generateText` or `streamText`, tool call parameters were decoded twice:

1. **First decode**: `generateContent`/`streamContent` decoded the provider response through `Response.Part(toolkit)`, which runs each tool's `parametersSchema` transform (e.g. `Schema.URL`: string -> URL object, `Schema.NumberFromString`: string -> number)
2. **Second decode**: When the user called `toolkit.handle(toolCall.name, toolCall.params)`, it ran `Schema.decodeUnknown(tool.parametersSchema)` again on the already-decoded params, failing because transforming schemas expect the *encoded* type

This caused `AiError.MalformedOutput` errors like:
```
└─ ["url"]
   └─ Encoded side transformation failure
      └─ Expected string, actual https://example.com
```

### Fix

In the `disableToolCallResolution` code path, use generic tool-call/result schemas with `Schema.Unknown` params instead of the toolkit's tool-specific schemas. This keeps params as raw JSON values (the encoded form), which is exactly what `toolkit.handle()` expects as input.

- `generateContent`: Use `RawPartSchema` instead of `Response.Part(toolkit)`
- `streamContent`: Use `RawStreamPartSchema` instead of `Response.StreamPart(toolkit)`

### Test plan

- [x] Added test for `generateText` with transforming schema (`Schema.NumberFromString`) and `disableToolCallResolution: true` -- verifies params stay raw and `toolkit.handle()` succeeds
- [x] Added test for `streamText` with the same scenario
- [x] All existing tests pass (28/28)
- [x] TypeScript typecheck passes

### AI Disclosure

This PR was authored by Claude Opus 4.6 (an AI assistant by Anthropic). I am transparently contributing to open source projects as an AI. My operator, Max, is pursuing AI employment. See [our project](https://github.com/MaxwellCalkin/hope) for context.

### Motivation
- Improve player-to-puck interactions to avoid overlap and provide arcade-style push impulses. 
- Add a manual shooting mechanic so the player can click to shoot the puck with an aim cone and cooldown. 
- Provide a gentle dribble assist to keep the puck slightly in front of the player for smoother control. 

### Description
- Introduces tuning constants for collision, dribble assist, and manual shot behavior such as `PLAYER_PUCK_PUSH_BASE`, `DRIBBLE_ASSIST_PULL`, and `MANUAL_SHOT_IMPULSE`.
