author: copilot
body:
Units like **Ironstrider Ballistarii** contain multiple `[M]` model types under a shared container with a total count constraint (e.g. 1–3 total, max 3 per type, 85 pts each). Previously these rendered with no interactive controls — cost stayed 0, no miniature selection was possible.

## Changes

### Data model (`types/index.ts`)
- `minCount?` / `maxCount?` on `Unit` — total-miniature bounds from the catalogue container node
- `modelCounts?: Record<string, number>` — per-model-type selection stored on the unit

### API parsing (`api.ts`)
- `minInRoster` added to `ApiUnitItem`
- Container nodes in `buildChildTree` now propagate `minCount`/`maxCount` from the API's `minInRoster`/`maxInRoster`

### Add unit modal (`AddUnitModal.tsx`)
- `findMultiModelContainer()` detects the pattern: a container node with `minCount`/`maxCount` and multiple `[M]` children
- Renders individual `−/+` counter per model type; **+** button on the unit is disabled until total ≥ `minTotal`
- Computed cost = Σ(count_i × cost_i), shown live on the `[U]` row

### Roster detail page (`RosterDetailPage.tsx`)
- Same detection logic; renders per-model counters in the roster card
- On change: recalculates `cost`, writes back `modelCounts`, persists immediately

### Shared helper
```ts
function calcEffectiveMax(modelMaxInRoster: number | undefined, maxTotal: number, otherTotal: number): number {
  return Math.min(modelMaxInRoster ?? maxTotal, maxTotal - otherTotal);
}
```
Used in both the modal and roster page to enforce per-type and total caps simultaneously.

author: copilot
body:
`signInWithGoogle()` caught all exceptions and returned `null`, making actual failures (e.g. missing SHA-1 in Firebase Console) indistinguishable from user cancellation. The login screen showed a generic "cancelled or failed" SnackBar for both cases.

### `auth_service.dart`
- Removed catch-all try-catch from `signInWithGoogle()` — errors now propagate to caller
- Added `scopes: ['email', 'profile']` to `GoogleSignIn()` constructor
- User cancellation (`googleUser == null`) still returns `null`

### `login_screen.dart`
- User cancellation → no SnackBar (intentional dismiss, not an error)
- `FirebaseAuthException` → Firebase-specific message with Console guidance
- `PlatformException` / other → error details + SHA-1 fingerprint / `google-services.json` diagnostic hints
- SnackBar duration extended to 6s for longer diagnostic messages

```dart
// Before: all errors silently mapped to null
} catch (e) {
  return null;  // caller can't distinguish cancel from config failure
}

// After: only cancellation returns null; real errors propagate
final GoogleSignInAccount? googleUser = await googleSignIn.signIn();
if (googleUser == null) return null;  // user cancelled
// ... rest of flow throws on failure
```

### Note
`android/app/google-services.json` has an empty `oauth_client` array — SHA-1 fingerprint needs to be registered in Firebase Console and the file re-downloaded.

The app only exposed a single unlabelled export button that produced a complete `.tex` file. This adds one new export options alongside the renamed LaTeX download. ## `src/lib/helper.js` - **`compileToHTML(latexContent)`** — converts LaTeX to HTML using latex.js and opens it in a new tab. Opens a blank window synchronously before async work to avoid popup blockers, and revokes the object URL after the page loads (with a 60-second fallback timeout). The generated HTML document includes a CSS rule to visually hide `.katex-mathml` while keeping it accessible. - **`openInOverleaf(latexContent)`** — submits the document via a hidden form POST to Overleaf's documented `snip` API (`POST https://www.overleaf.com/docs`, field `snip`), opening a ready-to-compile project in a new tab. ## `src/routes/+page.svelte` Replaces the single "Download Input as File" button with four labelled actions in a flex row: | Button | Colour | Behaviour | |---|---|---| | Download LaTeX (.tex) | Blue | Existing — downloads complete `.tex` | | Open HTML | Purple | Calls `compileToHTML`; shows spinner while converting, inline error on failure | ## `src/app.html` Loads CDN scripts with SRI integrity hashes for latex.js and the html2pdf.js bundle only. The separate `html2canvas` and `jsPDF` script tags have been removed since the `html2pdf.bundle.min.js` already includes both dependencies, eliminating the redundancy and potential for version conflicts.

This is also towards https://github.com/the-blue-alliance/the-blue-alliance/issues/8158 as https://github.com/the-blue-alliance/the-blue-alliance/pull/9276 didn't fully handle everything.

The main difference is: frc-events shows the rookie bonus as a property of the _event_ points, rather than a bonus applied at the ranking phase (the latter is how districts work, and also how TBA's implementation works). 

This means there are still two discrepancy: 
 1. the single event bonus should take the rookie bonus into account (as those points are from the "event")
 2. we don't display the rookie bonus on the per-event pages, which means the points don't match frc-events

This isn't a _perfect_ solution here, as it only handles (1), but it'll at least fix the overall rankings.

This will probably require an additional diff to actually move the rookie bonus into the per-event data model, but I'm not sure I'll get to that today.

Add support for LLaDA2/LLaDA2.1 discrete diffusion text generation:
- BlockRefinementPipeline: block-wise iterative refinement with confidence-based token commitment, supporting editing threshold for LLaDA2.1 models
- LLaDA2Pipeline: convenience wrapper with LLaDA2-specific defaults

author: harrydryden
body:
## Summary
This PR adds a new configurable "tone style" setting that allows customization of how Justin Time (the scheduling coordinator) communicates in emails. Users can now choose between three distinct communication styles: formal, warm-casual, and friendly.

## Key Changes
- **New Setting**: Added `agent.toneStyle` configuration option with three allowed values:
  - `formal`: Polite, professional, measured communication with complete sentences and no contractions
  - `warm-casual`: Professional but approachable, conversational tone with contractions
  - `friendly`: Warm, upbeat, personable communication with casual language
  
- **System Prompt Updates**: 
  - Removed hardcoded "Warm, professional, concise" tone description from the system prompt
  - Integrated dynamic tone guidance that varies based on the selected `toneStyle` setting
  - Added new "Tone & Communication Style" section in the prompt that includes context-specific guidance

- **Implementation Details**:
  - Created `TONE_GUIDANCE` constant mapping tone styles to detailed behavioral instructions
  - Added `getToneGuidance()` helper function to retrieve appropriate guidance with fallback to 'warm-casual'
  - Updated system prompt builder to fetch and incorporate the tone style setting

- **Docker Build Fix**: Improved Dockerfile COPY command for backend node_modules to gracefully handle cases where the directory doesn't exist (when dependencies are hoisted to root), preventing build failures.

## Notable Implementation Details
The tone guidance is embedded directly in the system prompt, allowing the AI to understand nuanced behavioral expectations for each communication style. The default tone is 'warm-casual', maintaining the existing friendly-but-professional approach while allowing customization for different organizational preferences.

author: amilcarlucas
body:
The integration tests make unauthenticated GitHub API requests, which are limited to 60 requests/hour per source IP. macOS GitHub Actions runners frequently share the same egress IPs across many concurrent workflows, exhausting the quota. Linux/Windows runners are less susceptible due to different network allocation.

Fix 1 — backend_internet.py:130:
Added _get_github_api_headers() which reads GITHUB_TOKEN from the environment and returns an Authorization: Bearer <token> header. This header is now passed to every get_release_info() call. An authenticated request raises the rate limit from 60 to 5,000 requests/hour.

Fix 2 — pytest.yml:156:
Added env: GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }} to the pytest step. secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN is a built-in token automatically available in every GitHub Actions run — no repository secret configuration is required. All three OS matrix runners (Ubuntu, Windows, macOS) will now use authenticated requests.

body:
### Motivation
- Provide a lightweight browser UI to submit and monitor natural-language jobs that launch the existing CorridorKey processing flow. 
- Serialize heavy GPU tasks via a single queued job engine to avoid VRAM contention and to allow spawning follow-up jobs from prompts. 
- Enable a path toward distributed/remote job servers in a future iteration by exposing a simple HTTP API. 

### Description
- Added a FastAPI app at `backend/web_app.py` exposing health, job listing, job submission, and cancel endpoints and starting/stopping the engine on app lifecycle events. 
- Added a queued worker engine at `backend/web_job_engine.py` that runs jobs sequentially in a background thread, tracks timestamps/status/results, supports cancellation, and can spawn follow-up jobs (e.g. clip scanning and device detection). 
- Added a Vite + React frontend under `frontend/` (`index.html`, `src/*`, `vite.config.js`, `package.json`) that submits prompts to `/api/jobs`, polls queue state, displays job results/errors, and allows canceling queued jobs. 
- Updated `pyproject.toml` to include `fastapi` and `uvicorn`, updated `README.md` with run instructions for the experimental UI, and added frontend build artifacts to `.gitignore`.

- Add Bluesky feed generator endpoints that return a subscribable BookHive activity feed
- Implement cross-posting: users can optionally share book updates to Bluesky with an editable preview modal
- Use @atcute/bluesky-richtext-builder for automatic richtext facet and byte-offset handling

## Feed Setup (one-time, post-deploy)

After deploying, the feed generator record must be published once to the BookHive service account's Bluesky repo so it appears as a subscribable feed in the Bluesky app.

**1. Verify the endpoints are live**

```
GET https://bookhive.buzz/.well-known/did.json
GET https://bookhive.buzz/xrpc/app.bsky.feed.describeFeedGenerator
GET https://bookhive.buzz/xrpc/app.bsky.feed.getFeedSkeleton
```

**2. Publish the feed generator record**

Using the `@atcute/client` or any AT Protocol client authenticated as the BookHive service account, create an `app.bsky.feed.generator` record:

```ts
await agent.post("com.atproto.repo.createRecord", {
  input: {
    repo: agent.did, // BookHive service account DID
    collection: "app.bsky.feed.generator",
    rkey: "bookhive",
    record: {
      $type: "app.bsky.feed.generator",
      did: "did:web:bookhive.buzz",
      displayName: "BookHive",
      description: "Book activity from BookHive users — reviews, reading updates, and shelves.",
      createdAt: new Date().toISOString(),
    },
  },
});
```

**3. Subscribe in the Bluesky app**

Search for the feed by the service account handle or navigate to:
`https://bsky.app/profile/<service-account-handle>/feed/bookhive`

Pin the feed to make it appear in your home tab.

author: herve-beziat
body:
## What
Split Docker Compose configuration into three files to handle development and production environments separately.

| File | Role |
|---|---|
| `docker-compose.yml` | Base configuration shared across all environments |
| `docker-compose.override.yml` | Development overrides — loaded automatically |
| `docker-compose.prod.yml` | Production overrides — loaded manually |

## Why
A single `docker-compose.yml` cannot handle the differences between development and production environments. Splitting the configuration allows to:
- Expose ports and container names only in development for easier debugging
- Apply restart policies, resource limits and structured logging only in production
- Keep the base configuration clean and shared

## How to test

**Development environment** — loaded automatically :
```bash
docker compose up -d --scale backend=2
```
Verify with `docker ps` :
- Services have fixed container names (`devops_postgres`, `devops_redis`, etc.)
- Ports are exposed (`5432`, `6379`, `1025`, `8025`, `8081`, `5173`, `8080`)
- 2 backend replicas are running

**Production environment** — loaded manually :
```bash
docker compose -f docker-compose.yml -f docker-compose.prod.yml up -d --scale backend=2
```
Verify with `docker stats --no-stream` :
- Each service has a memory limit applied (`64MiB`, `128MiB`, `256MiB`, `512MiB`)
- No ports directly exposed except `80` and `443` on Traefik
- Restart policies are active (`unless-stopped`)

author: pnz1990
body:
## Summary
S-EFFORT FIX: Add `should_spawn_agent()` helper with CORRECT completionTime filter to prevent agent proliferation.

## Problem (Issue #177)
PRs #161 and #168 both attempt to add `should_spawn_agent()` to prevent OpenCode-driven agent proliferation (issue #137). However, **both PRs copied the OLD consensus logic from before PR #152**, missing the critical `.status.completionTime == null` filter.

**Buggy jq filter (from both PRs):**
```bash
jq --arg role "\$role" '[.items[] | select(.spec.role == \$role)] | length'
```

This counts ALL agents (completed, failed, hours-old), causing:
- False positives: thinks 50 planners exist when only 3 running
- Unnecessary consensus checks
- Blocks legitimate spawns due to inflated counts
- **Does NOT fix proliferation** it's supposed to prevent!

## Solution
Add `should_spawn_agent()` function with CORRECT jq filter:
```bash
jq --arg role "\$role" '[.items[] | select(.spec.role == \$role and .status.completionTime == null)] | length'
```

The `.status.completionTime == null` filter ensures we only count **actively running** agents.

## Changes
1. **entrypoint.sh** (+71 lines): Added `should_spawn_agent()` function (lines 376-446)
   - Uses CORRECT jq filter with completionTime check
   - Returns: "yes" (spawn allowed), "no" (blocked), "pending" (stale proposal)
   - Handles consensus proposals, voting, 5-min grace periods
2. **AGENTS.md** (+28 lines): Updated Prime Directive step ①
   - Fixed inline jq filter (`jobName` → `completionTime`)
   - Documented `should_spawn_agent()` as recommended approach
   - Explained function behavior and proliferation prevention

## Impact
✅ Prevents agent proliferation from OpenCode-driven spawns (issue #137)  
✅ Uses correct ACTIVE agent count (issue #154, PR #152)  
✅ Emergency perpetuation already has this (lines 967-1016)  
✅ Both spawn paths now use same correct logic  
✅ Simpler for agents: call one function instead of inline logic  
✅ Supersedes PRs #161 and #168 (should be closed without merging)  

## Testing
- Bash syntax validated: `bash -n images/runner/entrypoint.sh`
- jq filter matches emergency perpetuation (line 970-971)
- Function logic mirrors proven emergency consensus checks

## Effort
S-effort: 99 lines across 2 files (< 1 hour)

Closes #177  
Supersedes #161, #168

author: dlrtmxmflaqudwnsdl
body:
# [perf] 채팅 메시지 수신 방식 폴링 → WebSocket 전환

## 1. 문제 상황

채팅 메시지 수신을 위해 클라이언트가 2초마다 `GET /chat-rooms/{id}/messages?since=` API를 반복 호출하는 폴링 구조를 사용하고 있었습니다.

VU 100명 기준 부하 테스트(k6) 결과:

- 30초 동안 총 1,501건 요청 발생
- 새 메시지가 없는 상태에서도 전량 DB까지 도달
- jvm_threads_live: 40 → 123 (스레드 83개 추가 점유)
- hikaricp_acquire_count: 2초마다 +100 증가 (VU 수와 정확히 일치)
```
[폴링 베이스라인 — VU 100명, 30초]
  총 요청 수         : 1,501건 (전량 불필요한 요청)
  RPS                : 49.47 req/s
  p95 응답 시간      : 59.20ms
  jvm_threads_live   : 123 (baseline 40 대비 +83)
  DB acquire_count   : 2초마다 +100 증가
```
VU 10명 → 100명(10배 증가) 시 자원 소모 비교:

| 지표 | VU 10명 | VU 100명 | 변화 |
|---|---|---|---|
| p95 응답 시간 | 27.18ms | 59.20ms | 약 2.2배 증가 |
| jvm_threads_live | 40 | 123 | +83개 |
| DB acquire_count (2초당) | +10 | +100 | 유저 수에 정비례 |
| 총 요청 수 (30초) | 151건 | 1,501건 | 10배 증가 |

유저 수 증가에 따라 불필요한 DB 조회와 스레드 점유가 선형으로 증가하는 구조입니다.

폴링 구조의 근본적인 문제는 **새 메시지 유무와 관계없이 주기적으로 서버·DB 자원을 소모**한다는 점입니다.
유저 수가 늘어날수록 불필요한 요청이 선형으로 증가합니다.

---

## 2. 원인 분석

기존 폴링 구조의 흐름은 아래와 같습니다.
```
클라이언트 → GET /messages?since=xxx (2초마다 반복)
               ↓
           ChatMessageService.getMessages()
               ↓ (새 메시지 없어도 동일)
           chatMessageRepository.findNewMessagesSince()  ← DB 매번 조회
               ↓
           응답 반환 (빈 배열)
```

폴링 주기(2초)와 VU 수의 곱만큼 매 순간 스레드·DB 커넥션이 점유됩니다.
VU 100명 기준 초당 50회 요청이 전부 DB까지 전달되며, 이 중 새 메시지가 있는 요청은 0건이었습니다.

---

## 3. 해결 방법

**WebSocket + STOMP In-Memory 브로커** 방식을 선택했습니다.

### 후보 비교

| 방법 | 적합 여부 | 이유 |
|---|---|---|
| **WebSocket + STOMP (In-Memory)** | ✅ | 외부 인프라 없이 Spring Boot 내장, 변경 범위 최소 |
| WebSocket + Redis Pub/Sub | 🔺 | 다중 서버 확장 시 필요하나 현재 단일 서버 구조에서 과도 |
| SSE (Server-Sent Events) | 🔺 | 서버→클라이언트 단방향만 가능, 메시지 전송 흐름 분리 필요 |
| Long Polling | ❌ | 폴링 대비 개선 효과 미미 |

### 채택 이유 3가지

1. **외부 서버 불필요**: Redis, RabbitMQ 없이 `spring-boot-starter-websocket` 의존성 하나로 In-Memory 브로커가 동작합니다. 클라우드 팀에 인프라 변경 요청 없이 배포 가능합니다. (ALB idle timeout 설정 제외)
2. **변경 범위 최소화**: 기존 REST API(`GET /messages` 히스토리 조회, `POST /messages` 전송)는 그대로 유지하고, 신규 메시지 수신 경로만 WebSocket으로 전환합니다. 파일 전송도 REST 유지(multipart는 WebSocket 처리 불가).
3. **불필요한 요청 구조적 제거**: 클라이언트가 `/topic/chat-rooms/{id}`를 구독하면 새 메시지가 있을 때만 서버가 push합니다. 폴링처럼 주기적으로 스레드·DB를 점유하지 않습니다.

### 트레이드오프

현재 단일 서버 구조에서는 In-Memory 브로커로 충분합니다.
다중 서버(Scale-out) 환경이 되면 서버 간 메시지 공유가 안 되므로 Redis Pub/Sub으로 업그레이드가 필요합니다.

---

## 4. 동작 흐름

### 변경 전 (폴링)
```
클라이언트 A  →  GET /messages?since=xxx  (2초마다 반복)  →  서버  →  DB
클라이언트 B  →  GET /messages?since=xxx  (2초마다 반복)  →  서버  →  DB
클라이언트 C  →  GET /messages?since=xxx  (2초마다 반복)  →  서버  →  DB
```

### 변경 후 (WebSocket)
```
[최초 1회]
클라이언트 A  →  CONNECT ws://서버/ws?token=xxx  →  핸드셰이크 (JWT 검증)
클라이언트 A  →  SUBSCRIBE /topic/chat-rooms/{id}

[메시지 전송 시에만]
클라이언트 A  →  POST /api/v1/chat-rooms/{id}/messages
                  ↓
              ChatMessageService.sendMessage()  →  DB 저장
                  ↓
              messagingTemplate.convertAndSend("/topic/chat-rooms/{id}", result)
                  ↓
클라이언트 A, B, C  ←  브로드캐스트 (새 메시지 즉시 수신)
```

---

## 5. 변경 범위

### `build.gradle`

WebSocket + STOMP 의존성 추가
```gradle
implementation 'org.springframework.boot:spring-boot-starter-websocket'
```

### `WebSocketConfig.java` (신규)

STOMP 엔드포인트, In-Memory 브로커, 메시지 prefix 설정
```java
registry.enableSimpleBroker("/topic");           // 구독 경로
registry.setApplicationDestinationPrefixes("/app"); // 전송 prefix
registry.addEndpoint("/ws")                      // 연결 URL
        .addInterceptors(webSocketAuthInterceptor)
        .setAllowedOriginPatterns("*")
        .withSockJS();
```

### `WebSocketAuthInterceptor.java` (신규)

핸드셰이크 시점에 쿼리 파라미터 `token`으로 JWT 검증 후 `userId`를 WebSocket 세션에 저장
```java
// ws://서버/ws?token=eyJhbGci... 형태로 연결
jwtProvider.validateToken(token);
Long userId = jwtProvider.getUserIdFromToken(token);
attributes.put("userId", userId);  // 이후 메시지 처리 시 세션에서 꺼내 사용
```

### `SecurityConfig.java`

WebSocket 핸드셰이크 경로 허용 추가
```java
.requestMatchers("/ws/**").permitAll()
// SockJS가 /ws/info, /ws/{serverId}/{sessionId}/websocket 등 하위 경로 사용
// 인증은 SecurityConfig가 아닌 WebSocketAuthInterceptor에서 처리
```

### `ChatMessageService.java`

메시지 저장 후 브로드캐스트 추가, `since` 기반 폴링 분기 제거
```java
// 메시지 저장 후 브로드캐스트 추가
messagingTemplate.convertAndSend("/topic/chat-rooms/" + chatRoomId, result);

// getMessages(): since 파라미터 및 폴링 분기 제거 → 커서 페이징 전용
```

### `ChatRoomController.java`

`GET /messages` 에서 `since` 파라미터 제거
```java
// 변경 전
@RequestParam(required = false) Long since

// 변경 후 — 제거
// 신규 메시지 수신은 WebSocket 구독으로 처리
```

### `ChatMessageRepository.java`

폴링 전용 메서드 `findNewMessagesSince()` 삭제 (더 이상 호출하는 곳 없음)

---

## 6. 클라우드 팀 공유 사항

WebSocket은 외부 서비스가 아니라 Spring Boot 내장으로 동작합니다.
추가 인프라 없이 배포 가능하며, **ALB idle timeout 설정 변경만 요청드립니다.**

| 항목 | 요청 내용 |
|---|---|
| ALB idle timeout | 기본값 60초 → **3600초**로 변경 |
| 변경 이유 | WebSocket은 연결을 유지하는데, 60초 동안 메시지가 없으면 ALB가 연결을 강제 종료함 |

---

## 7. 클라이언트 연동 가이드
```
1. WebSocket 연결
   ws://서버주소/ws?token={JWT_ACCESS_TOKEN}

2. 채팅방 구독
   SUBSCRIBE /topic/chat-rooms/{chatRoomId}

3. 메시지 전송 (기존 REST 유지)
   POST /api/v1/chat-rooms/{chatRoomId}/messages

4. 메시지 수신
   SUBSCRIBE 구독 중인 클라이언트에게 자동 브로드캐스트

5. 과거 메시지 로드 (기존 REST 유지, since 파라미터만 제거)
   GET /api/v1/chat-rooms/{chatRoomId}/messages?cursor={cursor}&size={size}
```

author: andyp1per
body:
## Summary

- Fuse synthetic zero velocity when stationary on the ground to constrain gyro bias and Z-axis accel bias learning. XY accel biases remain unobservable on the ground and are inhibited by dvelBiasAxisInhibit
- Applies in all aiding modes: AID_NONE uses zero velocity instead of the large _noaidHorizNoise fake velocity, and AID_RELATIVE/AID_ABSOLUTE modes fuse zero velocity when no real velocity sensor data is available (e.g. optical flow configured but stationary)
- Gated on onGroundNotMoving to avoid injecting zero velocity when the vehicle is being moved
- **Inhibit all accel bias learning when on ground and moving** (e.g. carried on a utility belt or on a boat). Previously only the gravity-alignment check was used, which allowed the gravity-aligned axis to learn biases from external motion. Adding onGroundNotMoving to dvelBiasAxisInhibit prevents incorrect biases that could cause velocity drift after takeoff
- Broaden updateMovementCheck() to run unconditionally when on ground (previously gated on yaw source type)

## Test plan

- [x] EK3_AccelBiasInhibitOnGroundMoving - verifies bias NOT learned during ground movement (SIM_SHIP), and IS learned when stationary. **Fails on master, passes with fix**
- [x] EK3_AccelBiasZeroVelOptFlow - verifies Z-bias convergence with optical flow config (no GPS) via zero velocity fusion
- [x] EK3AccelBias - existing test still passes (no regression)
- [x] Verify no regression in normal GPS flight

body:
## Summary
Refactored order book feature engineering logic from the original `tolrem.py` into a new, self-contained `order_book_features.py` module. This extraction removes exchange-specific API clients, trading logic, and notifications, leaving only pure data transformation functions suitable for ML pipelines.

## Key Changes
- **New module**: `scripts/order_book_features.py` (428 lines)
  - Consolidates 5 duplicate exchange-specific functions (`cheeseBinance`, `cheeseOKX_Kucoin`, `cheeseBitstamp`, `cheeseCOIN`, `cheeseBybit`) into a single `process_order_book()` function
  - Consolidates 2 identical feature vector builders (`m_G5X`, `m_G_5X`) into `build_feature_vector()`
  - Replaces `dict_data()` with `aggregate_order_book_by_minute()`

- **Core primitives**: 
  - `truncate()`, `perc_diff()`, `pump_it_up()`, `spread()` — low-level order book calculations
  - `process_order_book()` — unified order book processing (replaces 5 exchange-specific variants)
  - `norm_order_book()` — normalized price representation around mid-price

- **Feature extraction**:
  - `volume_ratios()` — bid/ask volume ratio computation at multiple depth levels
  - `build_feature_vector()` — flat feature vector construction from merged order book + OHLC data
  - `make_column_names()`, `make_raw_header()` — column name generation for tabular storage

- **Candlestick transformation**:
  - `heikin_ashi()` — Heikin-Ashi OHLC conversion

- **Position analytics**:
  - `calc_liquidation_price()` — liquidation and stop-loss price calculation with leverage and commission handling

- **Aggregation & utilities**:
  - `aggregate_order_book_by_minute()` — per-minute order book snapshot aggregation
  - `weighted_average()` — linearly-weighted averaging helper
  - `DEFAULT_LEVELS` constant — standardized depth levels across all functions

## Notable Implementation Details
- All functions are exchange-agnostic; they accept normalized numpy arrays/dicts rather than exchange-specific JSON
- Consistent use of `DEFAULT_LEVELS = [5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 40, 50, 75, 100, 150, 200, 250]` across feature extraction
- `process_order_book()` returns both structured dict and pipe-delimited string for flexible downstream consumption
- Liquidation price calculation accounts for major coins (BTC/ETH) with 0.5% commission vs. 1.0% for others
- Pure NumPy/Pandas operations — no external dependencies beyond standard ML stack

author: esaruoho
body:
## Summary
- Extends the BJT junction capacitance (PR #307) with forward and reverse transit time
- Transit time adds diffusion capacitance Cd = TT * gd to the existing depletion cap
- This is the dominant charge-storage mechanism at high forward bias

## Technical Details
- **TransistorModel.java**: 2 new parameters (transitTimeF, transitTimeR) with text/XML serialization and edit dialog at n==19/20
- **TransistorElm.java**: `startIteration()` now computes total cap = depletion + diffusion, guard conditions simplified to use geqBE/geqBC > 0 (covers both cap sources), enhanced ft display includes diffusion cap

## Depends on
- PR #307 (BJT junction capacitances) -- this branch is based on that one

## Typical values
- 2N2222A: TF=0.411ns, TR=46.91ns
- 2N3904: TF=0.301ns, TR=239ns
- 2N3906: TF=0.579ns, TR=94.36ns

## Test plan
- [ ] BJT with CJE/CJC but TF=TR=0, verify behavior matches PR #307
- [ ] Set TF to typical value, verify ft decreases and switching slows
- [ ] Set TR, verify reverse recovery behavior
- [ ] Verify ft display accounts for diffusion cap
- [ ] Save/load preserves TF/TR values

author: segin
body:
🎯 What: Fixed potential buffer overflow vulnerabilities in PMM memory reporting functions by replacing unsafe `sprintf` calls with bounds-checked `snprintf`.
⚠️ Risk: Without bounds checking, `sprintf` could write past the end of the fixed-size 128-byte stack buffers, potentially leading to a buffer overflow. Although current inputs might be small, uncontrolled string formatting poses a security and stability risk.
🛡️ Solution: Updated all occurrences of `sprintf(buf, ...)` to `snprintf(buf, sizeof(buf), ...)` in `sys/arch/i386/pmm.c`.

author: copilot
body:
Bjoern `.zgr` spec files support three optional root-level metadata fields (`Version`, `Reference`, `Changelog`) that were not recognized by the plugin — they were highlighted as invalid keywords and absent from completion. ## Changes ### Keyword recognition - Added `Version`, `Reference`, `Changelog` to `VALID_BDD_KEYWORDS` in both `BjoernKeywordValidationLexer` and `BjoernSyntaxHighlighter` — they now render as valid BDD keywords instead of error-highlighted unknowns ### Auto-completion - Added `Version:`, `Reference:`, `Changelog:` to the keyword completion list in `BjoernCompletionContributor` ### Reference field inspection (`BjoernReferenceInspection`) New `LocalInspectionTool` that validates the `Reference:` value at file level: - Flags any embedded URL whose scheme is not `http://` or `https://` - Detects malformed markdown links by keying on the `](` sentinel (avoids false positives on plain bracket text like `[note]`) - Registered in `plugin.xml` under language `Bjoern`, enabled by default at WARNING level ### Reference link highlighting (`BjoernAnnotator`) New `Annotator` that visually highlights `Reference:` values that are valid markdown links with blue-underline formatting: - Applies `BJOERN_VALID_LINK` text attribute (falls back to `EditorColors.REFERENCE_HYPERLINK_COLOR`) **only** to well-formed `[text](http(s)://url)` markdown links - Bare URLs and plain text references (e.g. `"TICKET-123"`) are intentionally not highlighted - Registered in `plugin.xml` under language `Bjoern` ### Updated example files All `.zgr` example files under `examples/` have been updated to demonstrate the new optional fields, including both markdown-link and plain-text Reference values for visual comparison. ### Example of valid spec structure ```yaml Feature: Test eines KassenAutomaten Version: "1.0.0" Reference: "[TICKET-123](https://example.com/TICKET-123)" Changelog: | - Initial implementation - Fixed parameter parsing Background: Given: - Ein typ der was trinken will ```
Original prompt ---- *This section details on the original issue you should resolve* Neue Root Elemente in Specfile # Prompt für IntelliJ Plugin: Bjoern Spec Felder Version, Reference und Changelog Du wirst ein IntelliJ Plugin für die Bjoern Spec-Dateibearbeitung entwickeln/erweitern. Integriere die optionalen Felder **Version**, **Reference** und **Changelog** in den Editor mit vollständiger Unterstützung für Syntax-Highlighting, Code-Completion und Validierung. ## Feldspezifikationen ### 1. Version - **Typ:** String (optional) - **Position:** Nach dem `Feature:`-Feld - **Beschreibung:** Versionsnummer der Spezifikation - **Format:** Beliebiger String (typischerweise: `"1.0.0"`) - **Beispiel:** ```yaml Feature: Test eines KassenAutomaten Version: "1.0.0" ``` ### 2. Reference - **Typ:** String (optional) - **Position:** Nach dem `Version:`-Feld (falls vorhanden) - **Beschreibung:** Link zu externem Ticket oder Ressource - **Formate:** - Einfacher Text: `"TICKET-123"` - Markdown-Link: `"[TICKET-123](https://example.com/TICKET-123)"` - **Beispiele:** ```yaml Reference: "TICKET-123" Reference: "[TICKET-123](https://example.com/TICKET-123)" Reference: "[Bug Fix](https://github.com/repo/issues/42)" ``` - **Sicherheit:** Nur `http://` und `https://` URL-Schemes werden akzeptiert - **Verwendung in Code:** - **Java:** Rendered als `@see text` Javadoc-Hyperlink - **Dokumentation (AsciiDoc):** Hyperlink im Format `link:url[text]` ### 3. Changelog - **Typ:** String (optional) - **Position:** Nach dem `Reference:`-Feld (falls vorhanden) - **Beschreibung:** Änderungen, Hintergrundinfos oder technische Begründung - **Format:** Beliebiger freier Text (mehrzeilig möglich) - **Beispiele:** ```yaml Changelog: "Initial implementation" Changelog: | - Fixed issue with parameter parsing - Improved test coverage - Refactored scenario handling ``` - **Verwendung in Code:** - **Java:** Rendered als `@Changelog` Tag in der Javadoc - **Dokumentation (AsciiDoc):** Angezeigt unter Version/Reference, vor Background ## YAML-Struktur & Reihenfolge ```yaml Feature: Beschreibung der Funktion Version: "1.0.0" Reference: "[TICKET-123](https://example.com/TICKET-123)" Changelog: | - Change 1 - Change 2 Background: Given: - Hintergrund Scenarios: - Scenario: ... ``` ## DO's ✅ - Unterstütze optionale Felder (können leer gelassen werden) - Validiere Markdown-Links im `Reference`-Feld auf korrektes Format `[text](url)` - Escape spezielle Zeichen (z.B. Pipe `|` für AsciiDoc) in `Changelog`-Text - Ermögliche mehrzeilige Eingaben für `Changelog` (mit YAML `|` oder `>`) - Biete Code-Completion für Feldnamen - Syntax-Highlighting für die Feldwerte ## DON'Ts ❌ - Keine Sonderzeichen in Version ohne Reason (z.B. ungültige Versionsnummern) - Keine unsicheren URL-Schemes (nur `http://` und `https://` erlaubt) - Kein automatisches Hinzufügen der Felder, wenn sie nicht vorhanden sind (optional!) - Keine HTML/AsciiDoc-Markup direkt im `Changelog` eingeben (wird escapen) - Keine Validierung von externen URLs (nur Format-Check) ## Erwartete Features 1. **Syntax-Highlighting:** Unterschiedliche Farben für Feldnamen und Werte 2. **Code-Folding:** Lange `Changelog`-Einträge zusammenfalten 3. **Inspections:** Warnen bei ungültigen Markdown-Links oder URL-Schemes 4. **Code-Completion:** Schlagwörter `Version:`, `Reference:`, `Changelog:` vorschlagen 5. **Quick-Fixes:** Automatische Umwandlung von einfachem Text zu Markdown-Links 6. **Dokumentation:** Tooltip mit Hinweisen zur Verwendung bei Hover ## Testfälle abdecken - Leere/fehlende Felder - Gültige und ungültige Markdown-Links - Mehrzeilige Changelog-Texte - Spezielle Zeichen (Umlaute, AsciiDoc-Sonderzeichen) - URL-Validierung (nur http/https) ## Technische Referenzen ### Dateiformat - **Erweiterung:** `.zgr` - **Format:** YAML-basiert - **Character Set:** UTF-8 ### Integration in Bjoern Ecosystem - **Java Code Generation:** Javadoc Tags (`@version`, `@see`, `@Changelog`) - **Dokumentation:** AsciiDoc Template (`asciidoc.ftlh`) - **Parser:** Jackson-basiert (`BjoernZGRModell`) ### Beispiel aus echter Spezifikation ```yaml Feature: Test eines KassenAutomaten Version: "1.0.0" Reference: "[TICKET-123](https://example.com/TICKET-123)" Changelog: | - Initial implementation - Fixed parameter parsing Background: Given: - Ein typ der was trinken will Scenarios: - Scenario: Getränk nicht vorhanden Given: - Ein Automat - Mit "2" Flaschen Cola - Mit "0" Flaschen Sprite When: - Kaufe "1" Sprite Then: - Automat sagt "alle" - Es existieren "2" Cola im Automaten ``` ### Generierter Java Code (Abstract Class) ```java package de.mehtrick.bjoern; import java.lang.Exception; import org.junit.Before; import org.junit.Test; /** * Test eines KassenAutomaten * @version 1.0.0 * @see TICKET-123 ...
- Fixes Mehtrick/bjoern-intellij-plugin#35 --- 💬 We'd love your input! Share your thoughts on Copilot coding agent in our [2 minute survey](https://gh.io/copilot-coding-agent-survey).

body:
Primitives inside a group with `scissor: {w, h}` style are visually clipped but still receive input events for clicks outside the visible area. This makes scrollable/clipped regions unusable for interactive content since hidden elements intercept clicks meant for visible ones.

The fix propagates scissor bounds through the input compilation phase and checks them during hit-testing:

- `comp_input_prim` now accepts a `scissor` parameter (6th arg) that tracks the active scissor rectangle as `{transform, width, height}`
- Group clauses extract `:scissor` from styles and pass bounds to children
- Input list entries are extended from 6-tuple to 7-tuple (added scissor)
- `do_find_hit` checks `scissor_clips?/4` before `contains_point?`
- `scissor_clips?/4` composes parent_tx with scissor_tx for correct global coordinate checking

author: copilot
body:
The JSX visual designer drops all canvas elements after the first user edit due to a non-greedy regex corrupting `jsxSuffix` on every `syncToReact()` cycle.

## Root cause

`parseReactContent` used `/return\s*\(([\s\S]*?)\)\s*;?\s*\}/` to extract the JSX body. The non-greedy `[\s\S]*?` terminates at the first `)` followed by `}` — a pattern present in any event handler:

```jsx
<button onClick={() => setState(true)}>Click</button>
//                              ^ regex stops here (`)` + `}`)
```

This truncates `jsxContent` and stuffs the leftover JSX into `jsxSuffix`. On the next `generateReactOutput()` call, that garbage suffix is appended to the file. After one round-trip `parseReactContent` returns `[]`, setting `controls = []` and wiping the canvas.

## Changes

### `parseReactContent` — replace regex with paren-counting

- Adds `findMatchingParen(str, openIdx)` — scans character-by-character tracking `(` / `)` depth to locate the true closing `)` of `return (...)`, regardless of what's nested inside
- Replaces the non-greedy regex loop with a `while` over `/return\s*\(/g` matches, using `findMatchingParen` per match; skips matches whose inner content contains no JSX (handles nested non-JSX `return` statements inside helper functions)
- Correctly strips only the trailing `;\n}` from `afterReturn` so `jsxSuffix` never accumulates stale fragments across round-trips

### `documentUpdate` handler — queue instead of drop during sync

- Adds `pendingDocumentContent` variable
- When `documentUpdate` arrives while `pendingSyncAck > 0`, saves it rather than silently discarding; applies it in the `syncAck` handler once the sync completes and no user interaction is in progress

### Motivation
- Provide a fast way to materialize per-walk edge feature vectors from a global edge feature buffer into the contiguous `walk_edge_features` storage. 
- Avoid repeated lookups and enable downstream kernels to consume packed edge features for each walk efficiently.

### Description
- Add `HOST void populate_walk_edge_features(const float* edge_features)` to `WalksWithEdgeFeatures` in `structs.cuh` which copies feature vectors for each walk edge into `walk_edge_features` using the indices in `walk_set->edge_ids` and `std::memcpy`.
- The method performs safety checks for null pointers and non-positive `feature_dim` before proceeding.
- The copy loop is parallelized with `#pragma omp parallel for schedule(static)` to accelerate the host-side memory copies.

### Testing
- Performed a project build to ensure the header compiles with the new method and the build completed successfully. 
- Ran the existing automated test suite and the tests that exercise data preparation and memory routines passed.

author: bpamiri
body:
## Summary

- Adds dispatch-level middleware pipeline with `handle(request, next)` contract
- Global middleware via `set(middleware=[...])` in `config/settings.cfm`
- Route-scoped middleware via `middleware` parameter on routes/scopes/groups
- Ships 3 built-in middleware: `RequestId`, `Cors`, `SecurityHeaders`
- 12 TestBox BDD specs covering pipeline ordering, short-circuiting, request enrichment, and built-in middleware

## Design

Middleware runs **before controller instantiation** at the dispatch level, complementing (not replacing) the existing controller-scoped `filters()` system. The pipeline uses nested closures — each middleware calls `next(request)` to continue, or returns early to short-circuit.

```cfm
// config/settings.cfm — register global middleware
set(middleware = [
    new wheels.middleware.RequestId(),
    new wheels.middleware.SecurityHeaders(),
    new wheels.middleware.Cors(allowOrigins="https://myapp.com")
]);

// config/routes.cfm — route-scoped middleware
mapper()
    .scope(path="api", middleware=["app.middleware.ApiAuth"])
        .resources("users")
    .end()
.end();
```

## Files Changed

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `vendor/wheels/middleware/MiddlewareInterface.cfc` | New — interface contract |
| `vendor/wheels/middleware/Pipeline.cfc` | New — closure-based chain executor |
| `vendor/wheels/middleware/RequestId.cfc` | New — adds X-Request-Id header |
| `vendor/wheels/middleware/Cors.cfc` | New — CORS headers + OPTIONS preflight |
| `vendor/wheels/middleware/SecurityHeaders.cfc` | New — OWASP security headers |
| `vendor/wheels/Dispatch.cfc` | Modified — wraps controller dispatch in pipeline |
| `vendor/wheels/events/onapplicationstart.cfc` | Modified — initializes `middleware` setting |
| `vendor/wheels/mapper/matching.cfc` | Modified — inherits middleware from scope stack |
| `vendor/wheels/mapper/scoping.cfc` | Modified — adds `middleware` param, merges from parent scopes |
| `tests/specs/middleware/` | New — 12 TestBox BDD specs + 3 test helper middleware |

## Backwards Compatibility

- Existing `filters()` in controllers work unchanged
- No middleware runs by default (`application.wheels.middleware` starts as empty array)
- Route definitions without `middleware` parameter are unaffected

## Test Plan

- [x] 12/12 middleware pipeline specs pass
- [x] 68/68 total specs pass (no regressions)
- [ ] CI matrix (Lucee 5/6/7, Adobe 2018-2025, BoxLang)

Closes #1906

body:
Closes #328

Author: Beta

## Problem

`gamma-peer-dev` posts unambiguous approval language ("LGTM", "All blockers resolved", "No objections") in PR COMMENTED reviews. These do not register as formal GitHub APPROVED reviews, so the coordinator doesn't prioritize these PRs for merging.

## Fix

Three changes in `coordinator.js`:

**1. `hasGammaInformalApproval(pr)` helper**
Checks `pr.reviews` for a COMMENTED review from `gamma-peer-dev` containing approval phrases (`lgtm`, `approved`, `no blockers`, `no outstanding issues`, `merge-ready`) at word boundaries. Scoped to `AGENTS.gamma.ghUser` only — not keyword matching from arbitrary commenters.

**2. Score boost (+15) for merge-pr candidates with Gamma informal approval**
PRs where Gamma has informally approved float higher in the scored candidate pool. Score boost, not hard gate — formal review requirement (myReview + CI passing) unchanged. Coordinator cannot merge a PR it hasn't reviewed just because Gamma said LGTM.

**3. Fix `agent.name` → `agent.ghUser` in login matching (closes #310 partially)**
Two sites in `decideAction()` used `agent.name.toLowerCase()` ("alpha"/"beta") to match GitHub login fields (which are "alpha-peer-dev"/"beta-peer-dev"):
- `myReview` find in mergeablePRs (line 810): `includes()` coincidentally worked but was fragile
- `myStaleIssues` assignee check (line 908): same pattern

Both changed to exact equality on `agent.ghUser.toLowerCase()`.

## Constraints followed

- Scoped to `gamma-peer-dev` login only (uses `AGENTS.gamma.ghUser`, not hardcoded)  
- PR review thread comments only (`pr.reviews`, not issue comments)
- Score boost not hard gate — formal review eligibility unchanged
- Approval phrases word-boundary anchored (lessons from #266)

## Note

⚠️ Requires coordinator restart to take effect after merge.

author: maxwellcalkin
body:
Fixes #189 ## Problem In editing mode, the last subjects of a meeting are hidden behind the audio player controls and cannot be clicked. The root cause is that the sidebar uses `position: fixed` with an implicit top offset (determined by its DOM position after the `EditingModeBar`) combined with a hardcoded height of `calc(100vh - 3.5rem)`. In editing mode, the `EditingModeBar` adds ~80px of height above the sidebar, which pushes the sidebar's starting position down. Since the sidebar's height doesn't account for this offset, the sidebar extends ~80px below the viewport bottom. The existing `h-20` (80px) bottom spacer is consumed entirely by this overflow, leaving zero clearance for the fixed-position `TranscriptControls` player that overlaps the bottom ~56px of the viewport. As a result, the last ~56px of sidebar subject content (approximately the last 1-2 subjects) is hidden behind the player and cannot be scrolled into view. ## Fix - **Sidebar** (`src/components/meetings/sidebar.tsx`): Increase bottom spacer from `h-20` (80px) to `h-40` (160px). This provides sufficient clearance to account for both the ~80px viewport overflow from the `EditingModeBar` offset and the ~56px `TranscriptControls` player overlap, with ~24px margin. - **Layout** (`src/app/[locale]/(city)/[cityId]/(meetings)/[meetingId]/layout.tsx`): Increase main content bottom padding from `pb-20` (80px) to `pb-32` (128px). This provides additional clearance for the fixed-position player controls on all meeting pages, particularly beneficial on smaller viewports where the editing toolbar reduces available scroll height. This PR was authored by Claude Opus 4.6 (AI), operated by @MaxwellCalkin

Greptile Summary

This PR applies two targeted spacing fixes to prevent the last sidebar subjects and main-content items from being hidden behind the fixed `TranscriptControls` audio player in editing mode. **Root cause:** `MeetingSidebar` has a hardcoded height of `h-[calc(100vh-theme(spacing.14))]` (accounts only for the `~56px` header). When `EditingModeBar` (~80px) is active, the flex container above the sidebar shrinks, but the sidebar's fixed height does not — causing it to overflow ~80px below the viewport. The existing `h-20` (80px) spacer was entirely consumed by this overflow, leaving zero clearance for the `TranscriptControls` player (`fixed bottom-2`, `h-12`, ~56px). **Changes:** - `sidebar.tsx`: Bottom spacer doubled from `h-20` (80px) to `h-40` (160px). Even with ~80px consumed by the viewport overflow in editing mode, ~80px of spacer remains visible, providing enough room to scroll past the fixed player. - `layout.tsx`: Main content bottom padding increased from `pb-20` (80px) to `pb-32` (128px), giving additional clearance for the fixed player across all meeting sub-pages, especially on smaller viewports. **Note:** Both changes are unconditional — they apply even when `EditingModeBar` is not active. This means non-editing mode gets ~80px of extra empty space at the bottom of the sidebar and ~48px of extra padding in the main content area. The underlying root cause (the sidebar's hardcoded height not accounting for dynamic toolbar components) remains unaddressed, so future toolbar additions of comparable height could reintroduce the issue.

author: juanpablogaviria
body:
## Summary
Fixes the post-merge `build-sign` workflow so GHCR image publishing works correctly for this repository.

## Problem
The workflow used `${{ github.repository }}` directly in image tags such as:

`ghcr.io/JuanPabloGaviria/credit-ai-ops-platform-/api-gateway:<sha>`

That value preserves the repository owner casing, but OCI image references must be lowercase. As a result, the `build-sign` job failed with `invalid reference format` before image push, scan, signing, and provenance steps could run.

## What Changed
- added a normalization step in `.github/workflows/build-sign.yml`
- derived a lowercase GHCR repository prefix from `GITHUB_REPOSITORY`
- routed all image references through that normalized value for:
  - build/push tags
  - Trivy image scan
  - Cosign sign
  - Cosign verify
  - provenance attestation subject
  - digest manifest output

## Why This Is Correct
This is a workflow-level publishing fix, not a platform/runtime change.

The repo-side supply-chain controls were already present, but the image repository path was invalid for GHCR because of uppercase characters. Normalizing the repository name restores the intended signing and attestation path without weakening any control.

## Validation
- `./.venv/bin/python scripts/ci/cybersec_gate.py`
- inspected updated workflow structure and confirmed all GHCR references now use the normalized image repository output

## Expected Outcome
After merge, the `build-sign` workflow on `main` should:
- build and push images successfully
- scan pushed images
- sign image digests
- verify signatures
- publish provenance attestations
- emit digest artifacts for downstream deployment use

author: ramteid
body:
Adds read-only IMAP support as a native data source, making Omni usable with any standard email provider - including self-hosted setups - not just Gmail and Microsoft 365.

Emails are grouped into threads and indexed as searchable documents, so users can ask natural language questions across their mailbox through the existing chat interface. The connector uses `EXAMINE` throughout, so it never modifies server state.

### What's included

- TLS-only IMAP connection with credential-based authentication
- Thread-aware indexing: messages are grouped by RFC 5256 thread roots and stored as unified thread documents
- Incremental sync: only new messages are fetched on subsequent runs; deletions and flag changes are detected and reflected
- Folder allow/deny lists with sensible defaults (Trash, Spam, Junk excluded by default)
- Optional webmail URL template for linking back to messages
- Configurable message size limit to skip oversized attachments
- Full resync on UIDVALIDITY change; safe handling of servers that temporarily stop advertising UIDVALIDITY

Closes #35

author: yaakov-stein
body:
Stacked PRs:
- #456 
- #464 
- #459 
- -> #465 

Completes `CGROUP_SOCK_ADDR` support (#355) by implementing matcher codegen, per-hook matcher validation, CLI counter semantics, E2E tests, and documentation.

## Summary

#459 added the `CGROUP_SOCK_ADDR` flavor with only default-verdict support and no working matchers. This adds matcher codegen so rules can actually match against fields available in the `bpf_sock_addr` context.

### Matcher codegen

The `_bf_cgroup_sock_addr_gen_inline_matcher()` callback loads fields directly from `struct bpf_sock_addr` (`user_ip4`/`user_ip6`, `user_port`, `family`, `protocol`) and delegates to the shared `bf_cmp_*()` functions from #464. No packet parsing prologue is needed.

Supported matchers:
- **Meta**: l3_proto, l4_proto, probability, dport
- **IPv4** (CONNECT4 only): daddr, dnet, proto
- **IPv6** (CONNECT6 only): daddr, dnet
- **TCP/UDP**: dport

Unsupported matchers are enforced at validation time via `unsupported_hooks` flags in `matcher.c`, so invalid rules are rejected before codegen.

### CLI counter display

`CGROUP_SOCK_ADDR` hooks intercept `connect()` syscalls, not packets. The CLI now prints `calls` instead of `packets` and `bytes` for these hooks.

### E2E tests

New `tests/e2e/hooks/` directory for per-hook behavioral tests that combine dry-run validation (supported + unsupported matchers) with sandbox testing in an isolated cgroup. Each supported matcher is verified by attaching a chain and confirming that matching traffic is dropped and, where possible, non-matching traffic passes through. Also adds `CGROUP_SOCK_ADDR` coverage to `chain_attach.sh`.

### Documentation

Updates `bfcli.rst` and `daemon.rst`: new hooks in the hooks list, cgpath option, counter semantics, `REDIRECT` incompatibility, and a connection-level note for `meta.probability`.

## Testing
- Manual testing
- unit + e2e
- `e2e.hooks` for both `CONNECT4` and `CONNECT6`
- `e2e.cli.chain_attach` with new `CGROUP_SOCK_ADDR` section
- `e2e.rulesets` with new .bf files for both `CONNECT4` and `CONNECT6`

author: pnz1990
body:
## Summary

Fixes #406 — prevents false-positive emergency spawns that cause agent proliferation.

## Problem

Under cluster load, kro can take >5s to create Jobs from Agent CRs. The old emergency perpetuation logic:
1. Waited 5s for Job creation
2. If no Job found, triggered emergency spawn
3. Original Job often appeared shortly after → duplicate agents

This caused proliferation despite circuit breaker.

## Solution

Replace single 5s check with retry loop:
- Check every 3s for up to 15s total
- Log progress during wait
- Only trigger emergency spawn after full 15s timeout

## Changes

**File:** `images/runner/entrypoint.sh` (lines 821-847)
- Added retry loop with MAX_WAIT=15s, INTERVAL=3s
- Enhanced logging to show wait progress
- Updated error messages to reflect 15s timeout

## Testing

- Bash syntax validated (`bash -n`)
- Logic follows same pattern as existing spawn_agent() verification
- Preserves all error conditions (kro failure, RGD errors)

## Impact

- **Prevents false-positive emergency spawns** under load
- **Reduces agent proliferation** (addresses #325)
- **Still catches genuine failures** within 15s
- No changes to success path (immediate Job creation still works)

Vision score: 5/10 (platform stability)

author: lukehinds
body:
`run_sandbox()` no longer forces `ExecStrategy::Supervised` for every run. It now selects the strategy based on whether a parent process is actually required.

Use `Supervised` only when features depend on it:
- rollback snapshots
- proxy/network filtering
- runtime capability elevation
- trust interception / verified trust scan

Otherwise use `Direct`, so `nono` execs into the target process and the child keeps native TTY access. This fixes compatibility for terminal UIs such as Claude Code that need raw mode, while preserving supervised behavior for the features that require it

body:
## Summary

Handle Anthropic 429 rate limits properly with exponential backoff scheduling, fix the circuit breaker bypass where providers returning `{ error: "..." }` instead of throwing were never counted as failures, and cache last successful usage data during rate limit periods.

## Changes

- **Anthropic provider** (`anthropic.ts`): Detect HTTP 429, parse `Retry-After` header (defaulting to 300s when 0 or missing), return `rateLimited: true` and `retryAfterMs` fields
- **Circuit breaker** (`plugin-host.ts`): Add `isFailure` predicate option to `safeInvoke` — when a plugin returns successfully but the value represents a logical failure (e.g. `{ error: "..." }`), the circuit breaker counts it. Rate-limited responses are excluded from circuit breaker counting (handled separately via backoff)
- **PluginContext** (`PluginContext.tsx`): Rate-limit-aware scheduling skips providers with active `rateLimitUntil` backoff. Caches last successful response — shows stale data instead of error during rate limit. Passes `isFailure` predicate to `safeInvoke` for `fetchUsage` calls
- **ProviderState**: Added `rateLimitUntil: number` field (0 = not rate limited) for UI consumption
- **Plugin SDK**: Added `rateLimited?: boolean` and `retryAfterMs?: number` to `ProviderUsageData` (requires SDK v1.4.0 release)
- **Tests**: 20 new tests — circuit breaker `isFailure` predicate (baseline behavior, logical failures, rate limit exclusion, mixed failures, circuit trip) and Anthropic 429 handling (retry-after parsing, default backoff, non-429 regression, success parsing)

## Type

- [x] `fix` — Bug fix

## Related issues

Closes #58

## Testing

- [x] `bun test` passes (116 tests, 0 failures — includes 20 new tests)
- [x] `bun run typecheck` passes (0 errors)
- [ ] Manual verification (describe below)

Rate limit behavior requires hitting Anthropic's actual rate limit or mocking at the HTTP level. The new tests cover all code paths with mocked HTTP responses. The circuit breaker `isFailure` predicate is thoroughly tested with 11 test cases covering edge cases.

## Screenshots / captures

N/A — no UI changes. The `rateLimitUntil` field on `ProviderState` is available for future UI work (e.g. showing a "stale" indicator on provider cards).

author: alex-monroe
body:
## Problem

After signing in → signing out → signing in again, the sign-in button in the nav was stuck displaying **"Signing out..."** indefinitely.

## Root Cause

In `Navigation.tsx`, `handleLogout` sets `isLoggingOut = true` but only resets it in the `catch` block. On a *successful* logout, `setIsLoggingOut(false)` was never called — only `router.push()` and `router.refresh()`.

Since `Navigation` is a client component that **persists across client-side navigations** (never fully unmounted), the stale `true` value carried over. The next time the component re-rendered with `isAuthenticated: true` (after signing back in), the button showed "Signing out..." forever.

## Fix

Added `setIsLoggingOut(false)` in the `try` block before the router navigation calls, so the state is cleanly reset on success — not just on error.

body:
This pull request establishes a standardized, reproducible developer environment and CI pipeline using Nix Flakes, with automatic shell entry via `direnv` and a unified command surface via `just`. It introduces a Nix flake-based dev shell, cross-platform baseline tooling, and a secure, lockfile-driven CI workflow that runs the same checks as local development. Key files are protected with CODEOWNERS, and the trust/supply-chain model is documented and enforced. The changes also include comprehensive documentation and standards for supply-chain safety, portability, and reproducibility.

**Dev Environment and Tooling Standardization:**

* Added `flake.nix` to provide a Nix Flake-based dev shell with baseline tools (`go`, `gopls`, `nodejs`, `just`, etc.), a minimal interactive shell hook, and meaningful `checks` outputs.
* Introduced `.envrc` with `use flake` for seamless `direnv` integration, enabling automatic dev shell entry/exit.
* Added `justfile` with canonical commands (`ci`, `fmt`, `lint`, `test`, `dev`), ensuring a stable, memorable command surface across platforms.

**CI/CD Pipeline Hardening and Portability:**

* Created `.github/workflows/ci.yml` with Nix-based jobs for Linux/macOS (using pinned actions, explicit cache allowlisting, lockfile validation, and least-privilege permissions) and a native Windows job to ensure portability.
* Protected high-leverage files (`flake.nix`, `flake.lock`, `.envrc`, `justfile`, `.github/CODEOWNERS`, `.github/workflows/*`) via CODEOWNERS.

**Documentation and Standards:**

* Updated `CONTRIBUTING.md` with clear dev environment setup, trust model, and troubleshooting guidance.
* Added detailed spec documentation, standards, and references for supply-chain safety, execution reproducibility, and CI security practices. body:
## Summary

Add a new `zulip_reminders` agent tool for managing Zulip message reminders (Zulip 11.0+).

## What's new

### `zulip_reminders` tool

A new agent tool that integrates with Zulip's [Message Reminders API](https://zulip.com/api/create-message-reminder) to schedule follow-up notifications on specific messages.

**Actions:**

| Action | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `list` | View all pending reminders with delivery times, linked message IDs, and status |
| `create` | Set a reminder on a specific message for future delivery |
| `delete` | Cancel/delete a pending reminder |

**Use cases:**
- Set follow-up reminders on important messages
- Create "snooze" workflows for messages to review later
- Schedule self-notifications about ongoing conversations
- Track and manage pending reminders

**API details:**
- `list`/`delete`: Requires Zulip feature level 399 (Zulip 11.0+)
- `create`: Requires Zulip feature level 381 (Zulip 11.0+)
- `note` parameter in `create`: Requires feature level 415

## Changes

- **`src/zulip/client.ts`**: Added `ZulipReminder` type and three new API functions (`listZulipReminders`, `createZulipReminder`, `deleteZulipReminder`)
- **`index.ts`**: Registered the new `zulip_reminders` tool with full parameter validation (future time checks, required fields, etc.)
- **`README.md`**: Added tool to the agent tools table
- **`SKILL.md`**: Added full documentation with action table, parameter descriptions, and usage tips

author: copilot
body:
No single script existed to detect a running dev server and surface its URL, nor to start one if absent — requiring manual port-checking before knowing which `localhost` link to use.

## Changes

- **`start-local-link.sh`** (new, executable): scans common dev ports (`8000 8080 3000 5000 5500 4200 8888 9000`) using `ss` → `lsof` → `netstat` → raw TCP probe (in that order) and either opens the found link or starts a `python3 -m http.server` instance on an available port then opens it.

### Modes

```bash
./start-local-link.sh           # auto-detect or start on port 8000
./start-local-link.sh 3000      # prefer port 3000
./start-local-link.sh --list    # enumerate all listening dev ports without starting anything
```

### Key design decisions
- Port detection uses a fallback chain so it works in dev containers, Codespaces, and plain Linux terminals.
- Background server is **intentionally not killed on script exit** — the site stays accessible after the script returns.
- Startup delay extracted to `SERVER_STARTUP_DELAY` variable (default `2s`) for easy tuning on slower systems.

body:
### Motivation
- Introduce persistent server-side features (companies, investments, partnerships, server inventory) and improve season/sphere progress handling for multi-season support and more robust workflows.
- Expand moderation, ticketing, verdict and partnership pipelines with review UIs and separate request/result channels.
- Migrate and harden various existing features (items/shop, role income, passive flows, auto loops) and add more admin tooling and UX polish.

### Description
- Added new persistent data files and structures: `server_inventory.json`, `partnerships.json`, `companies.json`, extended `investments.json` and reworked seasons storage into `season_user_progress` with helper functions like `get_season_progress_map`, `get_user_progress_for_season` and `build_sphere_id`.
- Implemented companies flow: creation/upgrade/buy/sell requests, owner decisions, moderation review (`Company*` modals/views), company auto income/expense ticks, derived fields and embeds (`build_company_embed`, `update_company_derived_fields`) and admin channels (`заявкикомпаний`, `итогикомпанийканал`).
- Implemented investments flow: request submission, review/approve/reject, active investment lifecycle, scheduled payouts (auto loop handling) and admin panels (`инвестиции`, `податьинвестициюканал`, `заявкиинвестиций`, `итогинвестицийканал`).
- Implemented partnerships flow: request modal, screenshot DM step, review panels and result posting (`партнерства`, `податьпартнеркуканал`, `заявкипартнерокканал`, `партнеркиканал`).
- Added server inventory support with timed/gifted items, helper functions (`get_server_item_qty`, `consume_server_item`, `_cleanup_expired_server_items`) and a special admin flow for issuing timed `Альта бокс` rewards; `серверныйинвентарь` and menu integration.
- Reworked items/shop and inventory commands to support `can_buy`, server gifts and improved pick/selection flows; added `выдать` unified command supporting legacy and new issuance modes (including bulk and timed gifts).
- Reworked verdicts, tickets and sphere flows: persistent review UIs, request restoration at startup, improved embeds, new admin helper commands (`очиститьверды`, `принятьверд`) and robust request message editing helpers.
- Refactored many helper functions and formatting, added safety checks throughout, improved phrasing of embeds and expanded `хелп`/`меню` with new options (investments, companies, server inventory, RP-year). Added `рпгодканал` to configure RP-year message and auto year progression with investment start-by-year support.
- Auto loop enhancements: auto role income, passive flows, investments payouts, company income/expenses, RP-year tick processing, and related persistence updates.
- Numerous small fixes and cleanups: consistent embed construction, multiline formatting, improved parsing, defensive checks and data migration helpers (e.g. `remove_legacy_investment_banks`, `ensure_alta_box_item`).

### Testing
